# Редизайн на листа за час

## A case study of calendar event creation, and the complete specification for this app's staff appointment sheet

**Status:** design brief · **canonical for this surface.** Supersedes the visit-sheet sections of [staff-schedule-uiux-design.md](./staff-schedule-uiux-design.md), records a dated override of that document's drag-to-reschedule rejection (§4.3), and — **2026-08-26, first pass — records the owner's reversal of its OWN body-drag exclusion (§3.4.9, §4.4) together with four further rulings: the segmented list is the design system's, ~~services and people are one token field~~ _(withdrawn the same day — see the note below)_, the frame and the typed clock are both always visible, and the sheet is always editable (§3.2).**
**Scope:** the appointment sheet only — its tiers, its anatomy, its edit model, and the domain work each region implies
**Surface:** `staff-visit-sheet` ([staff-dashboard.html:1212](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1212) — today a `sheetId` on the dashboard, not a component) → `staff-visit-editor` (**new**)
**Companions:** [staff-schedule-uiux-design.md](./staff-schedule-uiux-design.md) · [staff-schedule-remediation-plan.md](./staff-schedule-remediation-plan.md) · [booking-flow-architecture.md](./booking-flow-architecture.md)
**Method:** fourteen research and audit agents across Apple, Microsoft, Google and eight salon products, three competing proposals judged by a barber, a design-system owner and an engineer, then two adversarial verification passes against the repo — and, for the twelve-comment pass, a further round on Apple's four date-picker styles, the start-plus-duration convention across six salon products (**6/6**, no end field), and the HIG's rules for navigating inside a modal sheet, verified 3× against the repo
**Date:** 2026-08-26 · **two passes, both dated — see the resolution note below**

> ### ⚠ 2026-08-26, second pass — the twelve-comment resolution
>
> **This is the document's second dated pass of the same day, and it reverses more than it adds.** The owner left twelve comments on the prototype. All twelve are answered; three of the answers are rulings that overturn text written that morning, and each of those reversals is carried as a dated callout in the section it lands in — never as a silent deletion.
>
> |       | Ruling                                                                                                                                                               | What it overturns                                                                                                                                                                                    |
> | ----- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
> | **A** | **The date is a tinted pill in the `Ден` row whose calendar expands INLINE**, as a sibling segment of the same `ui-list-group` — `ui-calendar-grid uiSize="regular"` | the nested date-picker sheet is deleted; `ui-calendar-scroller` leaves this surface (§3.5, R0's tier table)                                                                                          |
> | **B** | **`Начало` + `Времетраене`. The end time is DERIVED and never stored** — duration is a `ui-menu` of ~8 values, each naming the end it yields                         | `От`/`До` is deleted from the appointment sheet. It stays in the block sheet, which has no catalogue to derive from (§3.5)                                                                           |
> | **C** | **A service opens a PUSHED PAGE inside the sheet's own navigation stack**, one level deep, one path, no second `Готово`                                              | §3.6.4's _"inline expansion, never a popover"_ and R2's token-editor extension. `span[uiToken]`, `[uiCombobox]`, the APG grid popup and `.staff-sheet__tokens` all leave this surface (§3.3.0, §3.6) |
>
> **The reconciling law, stated here once so A and C are never read as a contradiction:**
>
> > **A _value_ with a spatial editor of its own expands in place. A _row that owns several values_ pushes a page.**
>
> The date is one value with a calendar, so it expands. A service is three values plus a destructive verb, so it travels. Apple's own event editor obeys exactly this split inside a single sheet — `Starts` expands, `Travel Time` pushes — and the split is the doctrine, not the exception to it.
>
> **The other nine, and where each lands.** The large title is deleted for a static `Час` in the header bar plus a pinned `[sheet-accessory]` summary strip (**4** — R0, R1); the people field becomes **clients only**, with the barber named per service and the `Стол` row deleted (**2 + 7** — §3.5, §3.6); a `Промоция` row pushes a page and `⋯` gains a read-only catalogue (**3** — R0, R5); the frame's footnote is silenced unless it carries a verdict (**6** — §3.4); the ladder reorders to **date → frame → time** (**9** — §3.5); every visible section title is deleted and survives only as `aria-label` (**11** — R0, R1, every region); the team note becomes an on-demand reveal (**12** — R6).
>
> **Read this as a net simplification, because that is what it is.** Two novel, unstandardised primitives — a token field and a grid-combobox popup whose APG pattern has been [open since 2020](https://github.com/w3c/aria-practices/issues/1512) — are replaced by **navigation**, which every platform has already solved.

# Part 1 — Case study

Four families of software solve the same problem: _a person needs to put a thing on a timeline and change it later._ They disagree about almost everything else. What follows is what each of them actually does, checked against vendor documentation and — where the vendors are silent — against corroborated community reporting, with the confidence marked.

---

## 1.1 How Apple does it

### The sheet

iOS Calendar's New Event is a **full-height page sheet** — not a detent sheet, no grabber, no medium detent, no drag-to-resize. `Cancel` sits leading and plain; the title reads **New Event**; `Add` sits trailing and bold. Editing an existing event goes read-only detail → `Edit` → the same ladder with `Done` instead of `Add`. The title field is first responder on open, so the fastest possible path is _type a title, tap Add_ — and Apple's own instructions concede the form overflows: _"Swipe up, if necessary, to enter all the meeting information."_

This is straight out of the HIG: _"the Cancel button belongs on the leading edge of the top toolbar. When present, the Done button belongs on the trailing edge"_ — and, separately, _"Avoid showing all three buttons — Cancel, Done, and Back — together."_

### The field ladder

Grouped-inset list, five or six groups, ~44pt rows, label leading and value trailing, chevron only where the row pushes a sub-screen:

```
┌ 1 ───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Title                        [text field]        │
│ Location or Video Call           ›               │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌ 2 — SCHEDULING ──────────────────────────────────┐
│ All-day                            ( switch )    │
│ Starts            [ Sat, 23 Aug ] [ 10:00 ]      │
│ Ends              [ Sat, 23 Aug ] [ 11:00 ]      │
│ Time Zone                Sofia  ›   ← conditional│
│ Repeat                    Never ›                │
│ End Repeat                Never ›   ← conditional│
│ Travel Time                None ›                │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌ 3 — PEOPLE ──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ● Calendar                 Work ›                │
│ Invitees                   None ›                │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌ 4 — NOTIFICATION ────────────────────────────────┐
│ Alert                      None ›                │
│ Second Alert               None ›   ← conditional│
│ Show As                    Busy ›   ← conditional│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌ 5 — PAYLOAD ─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ URL / Notes / Add attachment                     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌ 6 — EDIT MODE ONLY ──────────────────────────────┐
│              Delete Event  (red, centred)        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### The single most transferable idea Apple has

**Conditional rows, never disabled rows.** Five rows exist only under a condition, and each appears _in place_, animated, pushing the rows below it down:

| Row            | Appears when                                                                                                            |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `End Repeat`   | Repeat ≠ Never                                                                                                          |
| `Second Alert` | first Alert ≠ None                                                                                                      |
| `Time Zone`    | the account supports time-zone events                                                                                   |
| `Show As`      | the account tracks free/busy (removed for iCloud in iOS 18 — an Apple adviser called it _"likely an oversight/glitch"_) |
| `Travel Time`  | disabled when All-day is on                                                                                             |

A default event shows ~9 rows. A fully-specified recurring meeting shows ~14. **The form grows to meet the task instead of pre-showing empty complexity.**

### The disclosure picker

`Starts` and `Ends` render their value as **two independent tinted pills** — a date pill and a time pill — right-aligned, each its own hit target. Tapping the date pill reveals a month grid; tapping the time pill reveals a wheel that also accepts typed digits. **The editor expands beneath its own row inside the same scroll view**, pushing subsequent rows down, and **only one is open at a time**.

The HIG mandates this explicitly: _"Avoid switching views to show a picker. A picker works well when displayed in context, below or in proximity to the field people are editing."_ And, decisively for us: _"Consider providing less granularity when specifying minutes in a date picker… You can optionally increase the minute interval as long as it divides evenly into 60."_ **5 divides evenly into 60. A 5-minute step is HIG-sanctioned.**

Minute granularity in the wheel is 1 minute by default; **a double-tap on the picker toggles it to 5-minute steps** — an undocumented, undiscoverable Easter egg.

### The chevron contract

Chevron ⇒ **pushes a sub-screen** (Repeat, Alert, Travel Time, Invitees, Calendar, Location). No chevron ⇒ **edits in place** (Title, All-day, Starts/Ends pills, URL, Notes). Apple never violates this. The chevron is a load-bearing signal of _where the interaction happens_.

Note also what Apple does **not** do: the whole Calendar ladder has exactly **one** leading glyph — the coloured dot on the `Calendar` row. Settings gutter-aligns an SF Symbol per row; Calendar chose density over iconography.

### All-day

`All-day` is a `UISwitch` in a list row (HIG: _"Use the switch toggle style only in a list row. You don't need to supply a label in this situation because the content in the row provides the context."_). Flipping it on:

1. **The time pills vanish from both `Starts` and `Ends`.** The rows do not disappear; they lose half their content. Apple does not disable or grey the time pills — it **removes** them.
2. `Ends` defaults to the same date; a later end date produces a multi-day banner.
3. `Travel Time` becomes unavailable.
4. The `Alert` option list **swaps to a different vocabulary** — day-anchored alerts, driven by a separate global default.
5. On the grid, the event leaves the time axis and moves to the **All-Day band** pinned above the hour grid.

### Direct manipulation in the grid

**Create by gesture.** iOS: touch and hold an empty spot. Apple's copy/paste flow confirms the block is placed at the touch point and _then_ the sheet opens: _"touch and hold the time where you want to paste the event. When you release, the New Event screen appears."_ macOS has three distinct creation gestures — drag from start to end (the growing block is the duration control, with its times rendered inside as it grows), double-click beside a time, double-click in the all-day band.

**Two grab handles.** Apple's own term is _"grab points"_: _"In Day or Week view, touch and hold the event, then drag it to a new time, or adjust the grab points."_ The model is: **long-press selects → handles appear → drag body = move, drag handle = resize → tap-away commits and deselects.** Selection is a persistent mode, not a transient drag. On macOS there are no round handles at all — you drag the top or bottom edge directly.

Handle sizing, per HIG: iOS default control size **44×44 pt**, absolute minimum 28×28; _"it works well to add about 12 points of padding around elements that include a bezel."_

**Snap granularity: 15 minutes. Everywhere. No modifier, no setting.** Corroborated structurally by Apple's own shortcut table — `⌃⌥↑`/`⌃⌥↓` move the selected event 15 minutes. Fantastical and BusyCal both fixed this with Shift-drag for 1-minute precision; Apple never did.

**There is no time bubble.** No floating magnifier, no gutter callout, no numeric readout during a drag, on any Apple platform. The only feedback is the block's own label updating inside the block. **That is a gap, not a pattern.** It is also exactly why 15-minute snapping is tolerable for Apple and would not be for us at 5: fine snapping without a numeric readout is unusable.

The HIG names the obligation anyway: _"Handle gestures as responsively as possible… provide feedback that helps them predict its results."_ And: _"Display a drag image as soon as people drag a selection about three points."_

**Edge auto-scroll**, from the HIG's drag-and-drop page: _"When people drag an item within a scrolling container that has a lot of content, the content can automatically scroll… but if they continue the drag operation outside of the container, automatic scrolling is no longer necessary."_ Two rules fall straight out: auto-scroll only inside the container's bounds, stop the moment the finger leaves.

**Spring loading**, also named in the HIG: _"Calendar lets people drag a selected event over the day, week, month, or year segments in the toolbar, giving them a convenient way to move the event to a different date."_ Hover-to-activate a scope control mid-drag.

**Overlap rendering** is the known defect: same start/end → equal side-by-side columns; partial overlap → cascaded with a horizontal offset. Users report the choice is _"completely arbitrary."_ And Apple offers **no conflict warning anywhere** — overlaps are rendered, never flagged.

### Speed

- **Duration for New Events** is a real iOS setting (default 1 hour). macOS has no equivalent.
- **Duration carry-over**: changing Starts shifts Ends by the same delta. There is no setting to turn it off, and users complain.
- **Title autocomplete that back-fills the whole event** — the single best speed feature Apple has: _"suggestions appear based on existing events. Select a suggestion to fill in event details. To reuse event details for an event at a new time, enter a different time before entering the event name."_ Its documented defect: it silently overwrites location and invitees, and Apple's own workaround advice is _"don't title the event the same as a previous one."_
- **Natural language — macOS only.** _"Soccer Game on Saturday from 11am-1pm"_, with hard-coded `breakfast/morning = 9am`, `lunch/noon = 12pm`, `dinner/night = 7pm`. Never shipped on iPhone.
- **Auto-invitee prediction**: after two invitees, Calendar suggests the third based on who you usually invite together.
- **macOS Availability panel** (`⇧⌘A`): free/busy bars for all invitees, drag the block inside the panel to reschedule, **"Next Available Time"** button. **iOS has nothing.** The phone — the device a working professional holds — is the weaker tool.

### What Apple gets wrong for a professional context

15-minute snap with no escape. No numeric readout during drag. The 5-minute wheel is a hidden double-tap. Six rows each push a full-screen sub-page (setting a 15-minute alert costs three interactions and two screen transitions for a choice among nine). Delete is at the bottom of a scroll in edit mode only — and cancelling an appointment is the most frequent destructive act in a salon. No conflict warning. No resource/chair model. No money. No status lifecycle. Invitee entry **fails silently** if you press Return before a match resolves. Location autocomplete is all-or-nothing. No visible undo after a drag on iOS.

## 1.2 How Microsoft does it

### A correction to a common assumption

There is **no vertical mini-day-view inside Outlook's compose form.** Microsoft ships three separate things, none of which is that composite:

|       | Surface                                | Orientation                                           | Draggable            | Where                                 |
| ----- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| **A** | Scheduling Assistant                   | **horizontal** — time on X, one row per attendee on Y | **yes**              | a second _tab_ that replaces the form |
| **B** | Calendar peek in a received invitation | **vertical** mini day strip, collapsible by chevron   | **no**               | the reading side                      |
| **C** | Inline creation on the live grid       | vertical                                              | yes (it is the grid) | the calendar itself                   |

The mental model of _a close-up vertical day frame, inside the sheet, with handles on the block_ is closest to **B**, but B is read-only and lives on the wrong side of the flow. **Microsoft has never shipped B's visual language with A's interactivity.** That gap is a design opening, not a thing to copy.

### Peek vs full compose

**Tier 1 — inline creation.** Microsoft replaced the old floating quick-compose pop-up with inline creation: single-click an empty slot and type the title _directly into the grid cell_ (MC846387). Double-click still opens the full form.

```
09:30 ┌───────────────────┐
      │ Haircut▌          │   30-min block appears, caret live in the title
10:00 └───────────────────┘   Enter = save. Esc = discard. No other field reachable.
```

**Tier 2 — the compose dialog**, overlaying the grid, carrying the `Event` / `Scheduling Assistant` tab pair. **Tier 3 — popped out to its own window.**

### The field ladder, and its ordering lesson

Microsoft's current step list runs: title → **`Invite attendees`** → time/`All day` → location + `Teams meeting` toggle → `Add a room` → `Repeat` → `Send`.

`Invite attendees` used to sit near the bottom. **Microsoft moved participants to slot #2 — because who is coming determines everything downstream:** the Teams toggle, the Room Finder, whether Save becomes Send, whether the Scheduling Assistant has anything to show. **Participants before time is the correct information architecture, and Microsoft learned it the hard way.**

### The scheduling preview strip

```
              08:00   09:00   10:00   11:00   12:00   13:00
 All Attendees ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░░░░░░░░▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░░░▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓
 ● You        ▒▒▒▒▒▒▒░░░░░░░░░░░░▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░
 ● Ivan  (req)░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░░░▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓
 ● Maria (req)░░░░░░░▚▚▚▚▚▚▚░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓
 ▣ Chair 2    ░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░
                          ┃▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓┃
                          ▲          ▲
                    GREEN start   RED end   ← both draggable

 ░ Free  ▓ Busy  ▒ Outside working hours  ▚ Tentative (hashed)
```

Classic Outlook draws two vertical bars — green at the start, red at the end — and _"Drag the green (start) and red (end) handles on the meeting bar to any open vertical strip."_ New Outlook and web draw one horizontal selection bar which is **blue**, and — the important part — **the bar itself is the conflict verdict**: _"A red bar indicates at least one scheduling conflict. A green bar indicates a conflict-free meeting time… If the vertical bar is red, drag it across the grid until it turns green."_ Colour is not decoration; it updates continuously as you drag.

**The colour legend is the genuinely good accessibility idea.** Solid blue = busy. Light blue **hashed** = tentative. **Diagonal stripes** = working elsewhere. **Striped grey** = no information. Grey = outside working hours. **Hue carries the category; pattern carries the certainty.** Outlook never relies on hue alone.

**Snap granularity — the definitive answer.** Microsoft, verbatim: _"Although the most common calendar intervals are 15 minutes and 30 minutes, you can also change the time scale interval of your calendar to 5, 6, 10, or 60 minutes."_ The full ladder is **5 / 6 / 10 / 15 / 30 / 60**, and the famous odd one is 6 (60 ÷ 6 = 10 rows/hour).

But there is a hard split between _display scale_ and _drag snap_: on classic Windows desktop a registry value genuinely changes snapping; the View-menu time scale alone changes grid density only; on web, snapping is fixed. **Outlook offers a 5- and 6-minute display scale on every client and a 5-minute drag snap on none.**

**No drag tooltip is documented anywhere.** The Start/End fields _above_ the grid update live. **The numbers are never where the finger is.**

Drag-to-reschedule on the main grid in new Outlook and mobile is a **2026** feature (Roadmap 568367, GA targeted August–September 2026). This is not a mature interaction to copy reverently; it is a laggard catching up.

### The people picker

Typing a name triggers suggestions _"based on the people you've met with or emailed recently"_ — recency- and frequency-ranked, not alphabetical. Picking one resolves the person into a **chip carrying avatar + name**, removable via ✕, with a **presence dot on the avatar**.

Mobile makes that dot the primary availability signal: **"small indicators on attendee's images turning green if they are free."** That is the cheapest possible free/busy affordance — availability collapsed onto the avatar the user is already looking at, with no grid at all.

**Required / Optional / Resource is one axis on one control.** And Outlook's cleanest structural idea: **a room is an attendee.** Room mailboxes have calendars, appear as rows in the assistant alongside humans, are booked by being invited, and auto-accept per policy. Free-typed locations are never a forced choice between structured and free-form: typing triggers matching, and you may take a suggestion or keep your own text.

**Free/busy is silently unreliable.** Empty space means _"Exchange has no event recorded there"_ — not that the person is free. External guests, personal accounts, Google/iCloud users all render as blank white space identical to genuinely free. The most dangerous state in the entire visual system is indistinguishable from the best one.

### Suggested times

New Outlook and web put a **`Suggested times`** panel in the right rail, ranked by how many required attendees are free. Classic calls the same thing `AutoPick`; web sometimes calls it `Find a time`. It returns three slots with **no regenerate and no "show more."** A dead end.

### Outlook mobile — the most transferable idea in the entire corpus

Mobile ships **no Scheduling Assistant.** Instead:

```
┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ ✕   New Event             ✓  │
├──────────────────────────────┤
│ Team sync                    │
│ 📅  Fri 25 Aug               │
│ 🕐  10:00 – 10:30      ⬤RED │ ← the verdict, one dot
│     ⚠ Doesn't work for all   │
│                    [ Time ]  │ ← escape hatch → full picker
│ 👥  (I)(M)(P)                │
│      ●  ●  ●                 │ ← green dot = that person is free
└──────────────────────────────┘
```

Microsoft's phone answer to _"does this time work"_ is **one binary colour verdict, plus per-person dots, plus a `Time` escape hatch.** The grid is demoted to a second screen you only reach when the answer is no. For a barber holding clippers, that is exactly the right shape: **answer the question, don't render the data.**

### Speed features worth stealing

- **The morphing commit button.** _"If you have invited attendees or added a room, the top left button will say Send instead of Save."_ One control, one position, label derived from state — **the commit verb tells you what kind of object you made** without a mode switch or a dropdown.
- **"End early" as policy, not control.** `Shorten duration for all events` trims 5 minutes off events ≤ 1 h and 10 off longer ones. **Two numbers and a radio, not a rules engine** — a policy that silently biases every new event rather than a control you re-operate.
- **Natural-language date parsing in every date field.** `next Tuesday`, `today + 12 days`, `3w 1d`, and — the detail to internalise — **`125p` → 1:25 pm**. A time field that accepts `1030`, `10.30` and `1030a` costs nothing and removes an entire picker interaction.

### What Microsoft gets wrong

**The Scheduling Assistant is a mode, not a view** — it replaces the form, so you cannot see the title field and availability simultaneously. **Axis inversion** — time runs horizontally there and vertically everywhere else in the product. Discoverability is broken by Microsoft's own admission (renamed to "Scheduler" and moved, then restored, with the official support answer being _"update your client"_). Density is unmanaged. **The quick tier is too thin and then abandons you** — inline creation gives title + time and nothing else, with **no in-place promotion** to the full form; you commit, then reopen. Regressions shipped without replacements (Ctrl-drag duplicate gone, Ctrl+C/V gone, default-duration setting gone, invitation peek shrunk from a full day to one hour for months with no explanation).

---

## 1.3 How Google does it

### Two tiers, and the split is the point

**Tier 1 — the quick-create bubble.** Click or click-drag an empty slot and a small card pops anchored to the click point, reading **"Add title and time"** and accepting natural language: _"Tennis practice at 5pm"_. The bubble carries an autofocused title field, a segmented Event/Task/Appointment-schedule row, the date and time as **inline clickable text rather than form controls**, and compact rows for guests / Meet / location. Footer: **"More options"** and **Save**.

**The bubble is not a reduced form. It is a different object** — title plus time — and the full page opens only when the user declares they need it. 80% of events never leave the bubble.

**Tier 2 — the full edit page**, a full-screen route (not a modal), two columns: scheduling and payload on the left, the **Guests panel** on the right with per-guest optional toggles and `Modify event / Invite others / See guest list` permissions. Two tabs across the body: **Event Details** and **Find a Time**.

### The duration dropdown — the single most stealable control here

Once a start is chosen, opening the **end**-time dropdown shows times at 15-minute steps where **each row is annotated with the resulting duration**:

```
1:30pm (30 minutes)
2:00pm (1 hour)
2:30pm (1 hour 30 minutes)
3:00pm (2 hours)
```

The user picks the **outcome** ("an hour"), not the arithmetic ("2:00pm"). Three consequences worth copying exactly:

1. The start dropdown lists raw times; the **end** dropdown lists times _plus_ duration. Asymmetric on purpose.
2. The list is **anchored at the current start** and only runs forward — **so an end before the start is unreachable, and no validation error is ever needed.**
3. Typing is allowed in the same field, so `2p`, `14:00`, `90m` short-circuits the list.

### All-day

A checkbox immediately beside the date/time fields. Checking it **collapses two time controls into nothing** — the row physically shrinks — and the event **relocates** out of the timed axis into the all-day gutter pinned above the hour grid. **The change of representation is the feedback, more than the checkbox state.** Unchecking restores the previously chosen times, not defaults. It also silently removes the time-zone control and re-keys the reminder defaults.

### Find a Time, and its cheaper sibling

**Find a Time** switches the body to a horizontal availability grid — one row per attendee, blue blocks = busy — and you drag the proposed-event overlay across it. **Suggested times** is a plain link _beneath the guest list_ that opens a list of concrete slots where everyone is free. **Most users use the link, not the grid.**

### Grid mechanics

Snap is **15 minutes**; the grid draws 15-minute subdivisions; dragging updates the time label inside the block live. Resize is via a ~4–6px hot zone on the top/bottom edge with **no visible handle until hover** — a mechanic with no touch equivalent whatsoever. **Undo is a toast plus the `z` shortcut**, and that is what makes destructive-feeling direct manipulation safe.

### Speed

`c` create · `e` open · `z` undo · `t` today · `/` search · `?` cheat sheet. **Default duration** is a setting (15/20/25/30/45/50/60/90/120 or custom). **Speedy meetings** turns 30 → 25 and 60 → 50 — but only for newly created default-duration events; it does not retro-trim and does not apply when you drag a custom duration. Optimistic save: the block appears in the grid before the write confirms, and failure rolls back with a toast.

### Material 3 Expressive — what actually changed

Rolling out from Android app version 2025.30.x: time slots now sit in containers with a solid Dynamic Color background layer instead of faint hairlines; month view wraps each date in its own rounded rectangle; the FAB expands to Event/Task/Birthday chips with the label _inside_ the chip and an explicit ✕ to dismiss; Google Sans Flex throughout.

**Critically: the M3E pass did not touch the event editor.** 9to5Google states plainly that _"events, creation interface, settings, etc. — today have not been updated."_ **There is no M3-Expressive event editor to copy.** The expressive language currently lives only in the grid chrome, and reviewer reaction was mixed — _"more modern, but it feels heavier to browse."_

---

## 1.4 How the salon incumbents do it

### Cross-vendor comparison

|               | Add a service                     | Multi-service stacking                                 | Per-line staff                              | Duration override                           | Price override                 | Add-ons                                       | Discount / promo                                 | Client quick-create                     |
| ------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| **Mangomint** | `⊕ ADD SERVICE` centred ghost row | repeating sentence-blocks in one panel                 | `with <name>` inline                        | `for 30 min` inline                         | in the service block           | "Service customizations" option groups        | at checkout                                      | `Search or create client` + `⊕`         |
| **Fresha**    | `⊕ Add service` outlined pill     | `Services` section, one card each                      | inside Edit service                         | `Duration` field                            | `Service price` field          | add-on **groups** with a client-facing prompt | per-line `Discount` **and** cart discount        | `Add client` → Existing / New / Walk-in |
| **Square**    | `Add a service` / `Add an item`   | polymorphic line items                                 | tap line → staff dropdown                   | `Block extra time` step                     | editable, incl. on repeats     | items attached as lines                       | **discount is a line-item type**                 | `Add customer` → `+`                    |
| **Booksy**    | `New Appointment`                 | **Combo Services**: Sequence (with breaks) or Parallel | per-service staffer                         | Service **Variants**                        | Variants; combo custom pricing | first-class, **price-only or time-only**      | rule-based: Flash Sale, Happy Hours, Last Minute | inline                                  |
| **Vagaro**    | `Service with…` menu; up to 10    | up to 10 services or a bundle                          | per-service provider                        | **`Duration`** field (total, incl. padding) | **`Price`** field              | `Add-On` field                                | Service Bundles; `Deposit Due`                   | `Select Customer` → `+`                 |
| **Phorest**   | multi-select **checkboxes**       | Packages; `Options > Add group`                        | per-service, subject to Multi-service rules | per-staff durations                         | per-staff pricing              | Add-On services                               | Packages / offers                                | dedicated flow                          |
| **Acuity**    | pick appointment **type**         | one type per appointment                               | one calendar                                | ✕ type-level only                           | ✕ type-level only              | checkbox list, incl. **Admin-only**           | coupon/package code                              | typed inline                            |
| **Treatwell** | client, then service              | thin docs                                              | per-column staff                            | in service menu                             | in service menu                | —                                             | —                                                | typed inline                            |

### Mangomint — the cleanest editor of the eight

Read state, in a ~380px right rail flush against the calendar:

```
Appointment                              ⋯   ✏️
─────────────────────────────────────────────
● Confirmed                        ( CHECK-IN )
─────────────────────────────────────────────
On  Fri, Jul 17        │        At  3:00 PM
─────────────────────────────────────────────
(avatar)  Rob Smith                       💬
          Client since September 2024
─────────────────────────────────────────────
Signature Haircut                          $85
with Victoria     request: none
at 3:00 PM        for 30 minutes
```

Four observations, all load-bearing:

1. **Status is a row, not a badge** — a teal dot plus `Confirmed` on the left, and the _one_ contextually-correct next action, `CHECK-IN`, as a **hugged outlined pill on the trailing edge of the same row**.
2. **`On <date> │ At <time>` is a single two-cell row split by a vertical hairline.** Both halves tappable. Far better on a phone than a stacked From/To.
3. **The service block is written as an editable sentence.** Function words are muted lowercase (`with`, `at`, `for`); the _values_ are the emphasised, tappable parts. Three short lines carry service, staff, request flag, start and duration with **zero field labels and zero boxes**.
4. **Read mode and edit mode are the same layout.** `Appointment` → `Update Appointment` swaps the title, swaps the pencil for `CANCEL`, and **grows one 🗑 per removable object**. Nothing reflows, so the operator never re-reads the panel.

Creation is four fields — `Search or create client` (search and create are **one control**, no mode switch), `Select a service`, date/time, note — with `or create time block` as a **plain underlined link under the title**. While the panel is open, a **live peach ghost block is already drawn in the calendar column** and grows as services are added. **The grid _is_ the preview.** That is the strongest argument for an embedded mini-frame: Mangomint gets the benefit by keeping the real grid adjacent, which a phone cannot do.

On the calendar, a service split by processing time is labelled **`SIGNATURE HAIRCUT (1/2)`** and `(2/2)`; a break renders as a grey diagonally-hatched block.

### Fresha — the best override UI

The `Edit service` sheet is the piece to steal:

```
✕                       Edit service
  [ Blow Dry, 40min                              › ]

  Service price            Discount
  [ USD | 25          ]    [ No discount      ⌄ ]

  Start time               Duration
  [ 1:50pm            ⌄]   [ 40min            ⌄ ]

  Team member
  [ ♡  Ben Adams                                ⌄ ]

  Advanced options ⌄

  🗑                            [    Apply     ]
```

- **Price and duration are peers in a 2×2 grid**, both plain pre-filled fields. **There is no "override" mode — editing _is_ overriding.**
- **`Discount` is a field on the service line**, defaulting to the literal string `No discount`, so the *un*discounted state is legible without opening anything.
- The service selector reads **`"Blow Dry, 40min"`** — name and duration in one string, so changing service and changing duration are the same control.
- **`♡` sits inside the team-member field** and means _the client requested this professional_ — a per-line preference flag, not a separate field.
- **`Advanced options ⌄`** hides extra time and resources: the rarely-used 10% is one tap away and costs zero vertical space.
- Footer: destructive 🗑 leading, primary `Apply` hugging trailing. **Two-level commit** — `Apply` closes the sheet, `Save` commits the appointment.

Two rulings baked into Fresha's model:

- _"Will the appointment price change if I reduce the time? **No** — changing an appointment's duration will keep its original price."_ **Duration and price are decoupled.** It is an FAQ, which means enough people asked.
- _"To schedule an appointment, at least one service will need to be added."_ The empty appointment does not exist.
- **Double-booking is permitted, not blocked.**

Empty client state: a lavender person-plus circle, **`Add client`**, sub-caption **`Or leave empty for walk-ins`**. **Walk-in is the _absence_ of a client, not a mode.**

Add-ons are **groups** attached to services, with an internal `Group name` and a client-facing `Prompt to clients`, each option carrying `Additional pricing` and `Additional duration`, plus group-level `Limits`, `Linked services`, and three advanced flags including **`Apply discounts to add-ons within this group`** (an explicit discount-cascade rule) and **`Hide from online booking`** (a staff-only upsell).

Discounts stack by a stated rule: **fixed-amount discounts apply first to individual items, then percentage discounts apply to the remaining total.** Note the first half of that sentence — _to individual items_ — is the part our own evaluator cannot express today; see R15.

### Square — line-item thinking

Square treats the appointment as a **cart**, which is coherent because the same object becomes the sale. The flow chooses the **`Event type`** first (Appointment / Class / Blocked time / All-day) — **type-before-content**, which is how Square handles the all-day and block cases _without_ a toggle inside the editor. Services and retail items are the **same kind of row**, and **discount is literally a line-item type** you add and assign to a staff member. Double-booking triggers a warning notification but is not blocked. Multi-staff is gated behind a setting that governs **online booking only** — _"Disabling this feature does not prevent you or your staff from manually creating appointments with multiple assigned staff on behalf of the client."_

### Booksy — the clearest vocabulary for stacking

**Combo Services** require ≥2 services and choose a **Booking type**:

- **`Sequence`** — one after another, **with the option to add breaks between them**;
- **`Parallel`** — all start at the same time and **involve more than one staff member**.

Then **Pricing**: summed from members, or **`Custom pricing`** (an implicit bundle discount). This is prior art for the flexible parallel+sequential arrangement model this project already ruled on.

**Add-ons are deliberately orthogonal**: _"They can have no price and only add time to a service, or they can have no duration and only impact price. When a service is booked with Add-ons, the price and duration of the appointment update automatically."_

**Promos are rule-based, not hand-applied** — Flash Sale, Happy Hours, Last Minute (e.g. booking ≤4h before start). The booking picks up the promo because it _matches_. **Booksy = declarative promos; Fresha = imperative discounts.**

### Vagaro — the most legible overrides

Every knob is a labelled field on the appointment, not buried in a catalogue: `Add-On`, `Date`, `Time`, `Price`, `Duration`, `Deposit Due`, `Resource`, `Appointment Type`, `Appointment Notes`. Two definitions matter:

- **`Price`** — _"The price the customer will need to pay. This is set to the default price set in your service menu."_
- **`Duration`** — _"The amount of time needed to perform this service appointment, **including gap processing time, cleanup time, and any add-ons.**"_

**Pre-fill from catalogue, expose as an ordinary editable field, and make `Duration` the total.** The block you see always equals the number.

### Phorest — the best multi-select and the best splitting rules

Service selection was rebuilt so you can **use checkboxes to pick several services or packages in one go** within a category — changelog headline _"Select Multiple Services in One Go"_, framed as making creation _"faster, smoother, and way less click-heavy."_ **Direct evidence that multi-select beats sequential single-select for exactly this workflow.**

**Multi-service rules** — the sharpest articulation of the splitting problem anywhere: `Can Be Split` / `Can't Be Split` / **`Will Only Split For Max Utilisation`** (prefer one staff member, but split when you run out of slots). The third is the correct default for a barbershop.

### Treatwell — colour by lifecycle

Hard 15-minute snap: _"an appointment can only be entered at lines (:00, :15, :30 and :45)."_ Grey regions = staff not active, and **"It is not possible to create or move appointments within these inactive sections"** — the calendar physically refuses rather than warning.

**Colour encodes provenance and lifecycle, not service type:** blue = entered by the salon, red = booked online, orange = client requested a specific staff member, green = client has arrived, grey = client finished and left. That maps almost one-to-one onto our status set and is a far better use of colour than encoding service.

### Acuity — the outlier, and useful for it

No per-appointment duration or price override at all — both live on the appointment **type**. What it does well: a **split-button commit** (`Schedule appointment` with a dropdown offering `Schedule, but don't send confirmation notifications`); a **`Custom`** escape hatch to schedule outside availability where _"a warning will appear, but that doesn't prevent you from scheduling"_; add-ons that can carry **negative** price and duration deltas and can be **`Admin-only`**; and **chained rebooking** — _"This appointment is ending, would you like to schedule another one?"_, available up to 15 minutes after the appointment ends, pre-filled with type and client. Perfect for a barber who rebooks at the chair.

### Processing / gap time — the industry's shared model

Every serious product agrees: **a service is not one block, it is up to three, and the middle one is not the staff member's time.**

| Term                               | Client present? | Staff available? | Bookable by another client? |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------- |
| **Buffer** (before/after)          | ✗               | ✗                | ✗                           |
| **Processing / development / gap** | ✓               | ✓                | **✓**                       |
| **Finishing / extra servicing**    | ✓               | ✗                | ✗                           |

Fresha's rendering rules are the most precisely specified: extra servicing time takes the appointment's own colour; **processing time is a _faded_ segment of that colour** — _"a partially open slot"_; blocked time is a **grey** segment inside the appointment. Phorest instead draws three separate blocks — solid, gap, solid — and prompts **"keep the development time?"** when you move such an appointment.

**Fresha's faded-segment approach beats Phorest's three-blocks approach on a phone, because it keeps one drag target and one tap target.**

### Direct-manipulation patterns from the wider corpus

- **A tap must never move an event.** FullCalendar's touch model is the reference: on touch devices the user must _"tap-and-hold on the event in order to 'select' it"_, with tunables `longPressDelay`, `eventLongPressDelay`, `selectLongPressDelay`, plus `eventDragMinDistance` (kills jitter-drags) and `dragRevertDuration` (animated snap-back so failure is legible rather than silent).
- **Handles must be ≥44pt hit targets even when drawn at 20–24pt, with the hit area straddling the block's edge** so the handle steals taps from neither the body nor the neighbour.
- **Haptics**: Apple's HIG distinguishes _selection_ feedback (a value changed by a continuous gesture — what pickers use), _impact_ (something landed), and _notification_ (success/warning/error). On the web this is `navigator.vibrate()`, which is Android-only in practice, has no iOS Safari support, needs sticky user activation, and _"feels glitchy and weird"_ when fired in a rapid loop because each vibration cancels the previous.
- **Snap granularity should equal the visible grid subdivision**, or the block appears to land between lines. FullCalendar's `snapDuration` defaults to `slotDuration` for exactly this reason.
- **Keyboard resize has no dominant implementation.** FullCalendar issue #2535 has been open for years. Two credible approaches: grab-and-move with live-region announcements (and note `aria-grabbed`/`aria-dropeffect` are **deprecated in ARIA 1.1+**), or **treat each handle as a `role="slider"`** — arrow keys work natively with no grab mode, `Home`/`End` jump to the legal bounds, screen readers announce every step for free, **and the business rules live in `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` as declarative data.**

## 1.6 What we steal, what we reject — the rulings

**R1.** **Conditional rows, never disabled rows.** Apple's `End Repeat` / `Second Alert` grammar. A row that is absent is honest; a row that is disabled is a promise. Applies to promos, deposits, conflicts, outside-roster notes, the late-client pill, the split action, and the stale banner.

**R2.** **The chevron contract, re-cut for a phone sheet with no sub-screens.** Three marks, inviolable: `⌄`/`⌃` discloses an editor **beneath this row** (one open at a time); `›` opens a **page inside this sheet's own nav stack** (amended 2026-08-26; it used to mean a separate sheet); nothing means **the value is the control**. Paired to `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` from one signal.

⚠ **The 2026-08-26 token extension is REVERSED the same day (Ruling C, §3.6.1). There are no tokens.** The three-mark contract survives, **narrowed to rows**: `⌄` = a menu drops here _or_ a picker expands here; `›` = **a page inside this sheet's own nav stack**, no longer "a separate sheet"; nothing = the value is the control. One mark did change meaning, and it is `›`.

**R3.** **The picker expands in place, beneath its own row, inside the same scroll view.** HIG-sanctioned. We never push a screen to set a time.

⚠ **The 2026-08-26 reinforcement is REVERSED the same day (Ruling C, §3.6.1).** The base clause survives and is _strengthened_ by being narrowed to what it always described — **pickers**: the date calendar expands beneath its own row (Ruling A, §3.5 › `Ден`). The reconciling law: **a value with a spatial editor of its own expands in place; a row that owns several values pushes a page.** _"We never push a screen to set a time"_ holds exactly — nothing about time pushes.

**R4.** **5-minute drag snap, and a live readout is what makes it legal.** Apple stayed at 15 precisely because it never built a readout; Outlook puts the numbers in a form region away from the block. The readout is not decoration — **removing it and keeping 5 minutes would be a worse product than 15 minutes with a readout.** 5 divides 60, so the HIG's picker rule endorses it, and the block sheet already ships `step="300"` on both time fields ([staff-dashboard.html:1465](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1465), [:1478](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1478)).

**Extended to the body-drag, 2026-08-26.** The move gesture snaps at the same 5-minute quantum as the handles, and it is legal for the same reason. Apple and Google snap a _move_ at 15 because neither of them built a readout for a move either; ours names **both** boundaries and the duration for the whole gesture (§3.4.9). **One quantum on this surface.** A second vocabulary for a second gesture would be the defect, not the courtesy.

**R5.** **Reject 1-minute snapping and reject a modifier for it.** There is no modifier key on a phone held one-handed. Shift+Arrow gives ±1 on the keyboard, which is where precision belongs.

**R6.** **Reject Apple's grid quantum wholesale.** A 25-minute service cannot be placed by drag in Apple Calendar, Treatwell, or Google. A barbershop's services are 20/25/40 minutes.

**R7.** **Steal the duration-annotated end list** (Google), **anchored at start + step so an illegal range is unreachable** — and express the anchoring as native `min`/`max` on `<input type="time">` rather than as validation.

**R8.** **Steal Mangomint's split `On … │ At …` row.** Two hit targets, both tappable. Better than a stacked From/To on a phone.

**Amended, 2026-08-26: the hairline is deleted.** In the design system's real segmented list two hit targets are **two segments** — two rows each carrying their own `--sys-color-surface-secondary`, separated by a `calc(var(--sys-space-unit) / 2)` seam of page ground (§3.3.0). A drawn divider inside a `ui-list-group` is the card-with-rules grammar this document has now abandoned everywhere else; keeping one here would make this row the exception that teaches the wrong recipe.

**R9.** ~~**Steal Mangomint's sentence-not-form service line.**~~ **SUPERSEDED, 2026-08-26.** The sentence survives; the row that carried it does not. ⚠ **Re-cut a third time, 2026-08-26 (Ruling C).** It is the service **row's second line** — `{{minutes}} мин · {{price}}[· {{barber}}]` — with the barber named only when the leg's barber differs from the frame's chair (§3.6.2). Still a sentence, still with no field chrome. The labelled field pairs it defers to are the **pushed service page** (§3.6.3), not a panel beneath a token. The grammar survived every re-cut; only the carrier changed — and the list row it supposedly killed is what it came back as.

**R10.** **Steal Fresha's `Edit service` sheet's _contents_ verbatim** — price and duration as peer pre-filled fields, `Discount` defaulting to the literal `Без`, `Advanced options` as a link-coloured disclosure, destructive leading and the confirm hugging trailing, two-level commit.

⚠ **Re-amended, 2026-08-26 (Ruling C): the contents, on a PUSHED PAGE — not inline, and still not a sheet.** Fresha's field ladder is stolen field for field onto the service page (§3.6.3). **Its two-level commit is refused outright: there is no `Готово` on a child** — one commit boundary for the whole modal task, and `staff.visit.done` is deleted (§3.10). A sheet stacked on a sheet was always the weakest part of Fresha's design; taking its field ladder, refusing its container _and_ refusing its second confirm is the whole steal.

**R11.** **Adopt Fresha's decoupling ruling as law: changing duration must not change price.** State it once, in the sheet, the first time a barber edits a duration. Fresha answers it as an FAQ, which means enough people asked; we answer before they ask.

**R12.** **Adopt Vagaro's ruling: `Duration` is the total, so the drawn block always equals the number** — and draw setup/cleanup as separate non-draggable shoulders, because _"The client is quoted, and charged for, the SERVICE — not the mop-up"_ is already this repo's law ([service-terms.ts:32](../../libs/domain/catalog/src/lib/service-terms.ts:32)).

**R13.** **Steal Phorest's checkbox multi-select — relocated, 2026-08-26, not deleted.** Phorest shipped checkboxes precisely because sequential single-select was too click-heavy, and that reasoning outlives the picker sheet it arrived in. The checkbox rows now live on the **pushed add-service page** (§3.6.4), which stays open on select — Linear's rule — so three services are three taps and one round trip. **Only the container moved; the contract is untouched.** What does not survive is the confirm button and its running count: each choice commits into the draft, so there is nothing left to count and nothing left to confirm. [`booking-services-step`](../../libs/features/client/booking/src/lib/services-step/booking-services-step.ts) is still the reuse target — for its **predicates**, not its cards.

**R14.** **Steal Booksy's orthogonal add-ons** — price-only, time-only, or both — and **Fresha's rule that an add-on extends its parent leg rather than becoming a separate leg.** One block, one drag target, one tap target.

**One addition, 2026-08-26, and it falls straight out of the two write regimes.** A **zero-minute** add-on changes no geometry, so the server has nothing to re-decide: it writes immediately, Regime A (§3.2). A **duration-bearing** one is a resize wearing a chip — it **seeds the draft** and waits for `Запази`, Regime B. Booksy's price-only add-on is the only case in the entire corpus that genuinely justifies an immediate write, and it is the only case that gets one.

**R15.** **Steal Booksy's declarative promos as the default and Fresha's imperative discount as the override — and state the cascade as the code actually computes it, not as Fresha words it.**

`DiscountApplication.apply()` ([discount-application.ts:65](../../libs/domain/engagement/src/lib/discount-application.ts:65)) is **cart-level and sequential-on-remainder**. It drops any discount whose `minSpend` gate fails, sorts what is left by `compareByTotalOrder` ([:97](../../libs/domain/engagement/src/lib/discount-application.ts:97)) — kind rank (`fixed_amount` 0 → `percent_off` 1 → `free_service` 2) → magnitude → `grantedAt` → `id` — then applies each one **to a running `remainder`**, and finally trims trailing lines if `capPercent` is set ([:179](../../libs/domain/engagement/src/lib/discount-application.ts:179)).

**Ruling, restated to match the code:** _fixed amounts apply first because their kind rank is lowest, each against the whole running remainder; percentages then apply to what is left of that remainder; the cap trims from the end of the deterministic order._ That is the rule. It is genuinely coded, and every tiebreak key is a property of the discount rather than the caller's array position — the fix for legacy bug 7.4.

**What is _not_ coded, and must not be claimed:** `DiscountInput` is `{ id, label, value, grantedAt, minSpend? }` ([:16](../../libs/domain/engagement/src/lib/discount-application.ts:16)). It carries **no line, seat or service reference at all**, and the module has no add-on concept. So Fresha's _"fixed amounts apply to the individual items they name"_ and any "percentages include add-ons, fixed amounts do not" refinement are **not expressible today**. They are future scope, and they need a named extension: **`DiscountInput.appliesTo: SeatId[]` (new)**, plus a per-seat remainder in `apply()`. Sized and scheduled in M8, not assumed.

**And the caller situation is the opposite of "orphaned code."** `apply()` has a caller: `ApplyDiscountsUseCase` ([apply-discounts.use-case.ts:34](../../libs/application/engagement/src/lib/use-cases/apply-discounts.use-case.ts:34)) loads grants through `CouponGrantRepository.findUsableForUser`, projects them into `DiscountInput`s, and calls `apply()` at [:57](../../libs/application/engagement/src/lib/use-cases/apply-discounts.use-case.ts:57). The evaluator and its application use-case both exist. **What is missing is a caller from the _scheduling_ side** — nothing in the booking or staff path ever asks engagement what this appointment costs after promos. That wiring, not the arithmetic, is the work.

**R16.** **Steal Outlook's pattern-plus-hue encoding.** Hue carries the category, **pattern carries the certainty**. Solid = sold. Hatched = padding or blocked. Faded = processing. Outlined = someone else's. It survives colour-blindness and shop glare and satisfies the three-channel rule without inventing a fourth colour axis.

**R17.** **Steal Treatwell's colour-by-lifecycle** for neighbour blocks and rails. It maps one-to-one onto `pending / confirmed / arrived / completed / no_show` and is a far better use of colour than service type.

**R18.** **Steal Microsoft's ordering lesson: participants before time is the correct IA** — for _creation_. For _editing_ an existing visit, time comes first, because the thing a barber opens an existing visit to change is almost always the time.

**R19.** **Steal Outlook mobile's one-verdict-plus-escape-hatch, and reject the Scheduling Assistant grid.** A chair-move offers a plain-language verdict per barber (`Свободен` / `Зает — Петър 10:30` / `Извън смяната` — **new copy**), not a three-column chart on a 375px screen.

**R20.** **Reject the horizontal availability axis outright.** Time runs vertically everywhere else in this product. Outlook's axis inversion makes the user re-learn the axis at each tab boundary; that is a defect, not a pattern.

**R21.** **Reject "the assistant is a mode that replaces the form."** The frame lives _inside_ the sheet, as the disclosure of the row it belongs to — Surface B's visual language with Surface A's interactivity, which Microsoft has never shipped.

**R22.** **Steal Outlook's morphing commit button.** One control, one position, label derived from state. Our version: `Дойде` when clean, `Запази` when dirty, `Запази въпреки застъпването` when the draft overlaps.

**And it refuses to morph per _gesture_ (2026-08-26).** The sheet commits an appointment, not a gesture. A button that reads `Премести` one second and `Промени продължителността` the next is a flicker, not information. Move and resize genuinely are two commands on the wire, with two validators and two undo strings (§3.4.9) — and every one of those differences lives in the **toast and the announcement**, which is where Apple and Google both put it. `Запази` stays `Запази`.

**R23.** **Steal the "end early as policy" idea, not the control.** Per-service `setupMinutes`/`cleanupMinutes` already exist in `ServiceTerms` ([service-terms.ts:13](../../libs/domain/catalog/src/lib/service-terms.ts:13)) and already inherit the (barber, variant) axes for free. Set once, applied always, still overridable.

**R24.** **Steal `125p`-shaped time entry — the cheap half only.** Bare digits and dotted times (`1015`, `10.15`) normalise on `beforeinput`. **Reject Bulgarian natural-language date parsing**: it is a language project with holiday tables and morphology, and Apple only ever shipped NL on the desktop.

**R25.** **Steal Fresha's walk-in framing: walk-in is the absence of a client, not a mode — and be precise that today only the _model_ agrees, not the _write path_.**

Modelled and shipping: `SeatSubject.anonymous(label)` ([seat.ts:47](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/seat.ts:47)), and a nullable `BookingContact` whose class doc already says _"a staff-entered walk-in may genuinely have nobody to call"_ ([appointment.ts:68](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/appointment.ts:68)).

**Not shipping: a walk-in cannot be created.** `CommitBookingUseCase` refuses a falsy `ownerUserId` outright with `CommitBookingUnauthenticatedError` ([commit-booking.use-case.ts:66](../../apps/functions/src/use-cases/commit-booking.use-case.ts:66)), and `decideBooking` then requires `UserId.create(deps.ownerUserId)` to succeed ([decide-booking.ts:193](../../apps/functions/src/use-cases/decide-booking.ts:193)). The `{ kind: 'guest', label }` subject ([decide-booking.ts:57](../../apps/functions/src/use-cases/decide-booking.ts:57)) only ever reaches `SeatSubject.anonymous` through `toSubject` ([:484](../../apps/functions/src/use-cases/decide-booking.ts:484)) — i.e. for a **companion seat inside a party an authenticated owner books**. There is no path today by which a seat has no account behind it at all.

**Ruling:** the framing is right and stays. The create path is a real, sized change — `ownerUserId` must become nullable through `CommitBookingUseCase` → `decideBooking` → `toSubject`, with a staff-attributed `createdByUserId` (**new field**) replacing it for audit. **Size M, not S**, and owned by M6.

**R26.** **Steal Mangomint's one-control search-and-create.** `Търси или добави` with the create row always last in the results, always labelled with the literal typed text. **Never a keystroke that does nothing** — Apple's silently-dropped invitee is the failure mode this design most explicitly beats.

**Promoted, 2026-08-26: this is now the core contract of both pushed search pages**, add-service and add-client alike (§3.6.4, §3.7). For people the create row ships in M6. For services it is gated on **Q20**, and until that question is answered the no-match state offers a sentence and nothing else — which is still not a dead keystroke, because the sentence names what you typed.

**R27.** **Steal Square's type-before-content for creation, and reject an all-day toggle on an _appointment_ — while keeping the all-day switch that already ships for _blocks_.**

The rejection first. An all-day appointment would report a barber 100% productive via `classifyOccupancy` ([occupancy-class.ts:53](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/occupancy-class.ts:53)), fold a real `Money` into `subtotal()` ([appointment.ts:363](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/appointment.ts:363)), and occlude the next-day busy boundary. All-day is a `ScheduleException`.

**And that half already ships, which the rejection must not be read as denying.** Three pieces exist today:

| Piece                                                           | Where                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `allDay` / `allDayLabel` / `allDayAlways` inputs on the grid    | [staff-time-grid.ts:236](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:236), [:238](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:238), [:246](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:246) |
| the pinned all-day row, drawn only when something is in it      | [staff-time-grid.html:79](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.html:79)                                                                                                                                                                           |
| the all-day switch in the block sheet (`staff.day.blockAllDay`) | [staff-dashboard.html:1443](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1443)                                                                                                                                                                 |
| the exception writer behind it                                  | `StaffDayStore.blockTime` — [staff-day.store.ts:738](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:738)                                                                                                                                                           |

Three rulings follow.

**(a) The block sheet's all-day switch stays exactly as it is.** It is on the right object, it collapses the From/To pair when on (`@if (!blockAllDay())` at [staff-dashboard.html:1457](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1457)), and the grid already has somewhere to put the result. The redesign inherits it; it is not re-litigated here.

**(b) Flipping the kind switch on an existing _appointment_ to a whole-day block is two writes and one confirmation** — cancel the appointment, then write a whole-day `ScheduleException` — never a silent conversion. Same shape as R28, carrying the `toBlockLede` copy (**new key**) that names both effects and the client by name before either write happens.

**(c) A whole-day exception is not drawn in the frame, and the frame does not open on one.** The frame is a ~100-minute window of a single chair; a whole-day thing has no edges to grab, so handles would be a lie. A whole-day `time_off` / `sick` / `closed` renders as a chip in the pinned all-day row the grid already has, and tapping it opens the **block sheet**, not the visit editor. The visit editor never receives an edgeless event.

**R28.** **Reject a toggle that converts a booked visit into a block.** It would silently destroy a booking. Conversion is an explicit two-effect menu item that names the cancellation and the client.

**R29.** **Steal Apple's title-autocomplete-that-back-fills, and fix its documented defect.** `Същото като миналия път` (**new copy**) back-fills services, barber and duration from the client's last completed visit, **leaves the time alone**, announces what it took, and badges every changed value `по избор` until saved. Apple's version overwrites invisibly and their own workaround advice is _"don't title the event the same as a previous one."_

**R30.** **Steal Acuity's chained rebooking** — _"this appointment is ending, book another?"_ — as a post-completion offer, and **Acuity's split commit** shape for "save without notifying" once a notification channel exists.

**R31.** **Reject optimistic writes.** Google's optimistic save is correct for Google and wrong here. `StaffDayStore` already rules it: _"no optimistic local mutation, because the server can refuse … and a lane that lied for a second teaches staff to distrust it"_ ([staff-day.store.ts:266](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:266)). **Every reference calendar in this study commits on release. All of them are wrong for a surface whose server re-decides placement.**

**R32.** **Reject "the quick tier abandons you."** Outlook's inline creation gives title + time and then makes you commit and reopen. **Our peek and compose tiers are the same component at two heights**, so promotion is a signal flip, not a round trip.

**R33.** **Reject spring-loaded cross-day drag for v1.** Apple's is genuinely elegant, but a cross-day move re-decides roster, lead time, conflicts and terms server-side, and doing that mid-gesture with no way to preview the destination is a promise the client cannot keep. `Премести на друг ден` opens the date picker.

**Unmoved by the 2026-08-26 body-drag reversal.** The body drags **vertically, in one chair, on one day.** A horizontal drag would re-decide all four of those things mid-gesture, and the frame deliberately does not page a day when a finger is held at its edge the way Google's does. `⋯ → Смени стола` and `Премести на друг ден` remain the only cross-chair and cross-day paths — which is also what keeps §4.3's first objection answered.

**R34.** **Reject processing/development time.** Every salon product models it because hair colour needs it. A barbershop does not — and `processingMinutes` correctly does not exist anywhere in this repo today. Setup/cleanup padding already covers chair turnover, and adding it would over-fit the model and complicate every collision test.

**R35.** **Reject merging two appointments, ship splitting.** Splitting creates; merging destroys two objects to make one, across two contacts, two owners and two audit trails. Every product that offers merge does so on a desktop with an undo stack.

**R36.** **Reject a rules engine for promos on the client.** The UI renders a `DiscountBreakdown` ([discount-application.ts:32](../../libs/domain/engagement/src/lib/discount-application.ts:32)) and nothing else. A second, UI-side evaluator would guarantee divergence from the server's.

**R37.** **Reject swipe actions.** Already rejected on this surface, and correctly — a swipe on a scrolling run of cards is a coin flip.

**R38.** **Reject a magnifier.** The frame's scale is derived from `--sys-space-unit`, which is `calc(0.25rem * var(--sys-density))` ([tokens.css:51](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:51)), and `[data-density]` sets `0.92` for compact ([tokens.css:232](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:232)) and `1.08` for spacious ([tokens.css:235](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:235)). So the frame runs at **2.21 px/min compact · 2.40 default · 2.59 spacious** — and at every one of those there is no more detail to magnify: there are 5-minute steps and that is the entire vocabulary. The readout is an offset pill, and calling it a magnifier would promise precision the model refuses to have.

**Still true after the body-drag reversal.** At 2.21–2.59 px/min there is nothing to magnify for a **move** either — the destination is a 5-minute step, and the readout already names both of its boundaries.

**R39.** **Conflict is a first-class named state, not a column split.** Apple renders overlaps and flags nothing; Square warns; Fresha permits. We draw it, name it (`Застъпва се с Иван · 11:00 – 11:30`), permit it, and make the commit verb say what you are about to do.

**R40.** **Handles are `role="slider"`, not a grab mode — narrowed, 2026-08-26, to the handles.** `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` **are** the business rules, expressed declaratively. FullCalendar has had keyboard resize open as an issue for years because it reached for grab-and-move instead.

**The block body is not a slider, and cannot be bent into one.** A move carries **two** values; a slider carries one. So the block ships as a real `<button>` with a localised `aria-roledescription` (`преместваем блок`) and a grab-and-move keyboard model: `Enter` grabs, `↑`/`↓` step 5 minutes with the duration invariant, `Escape` reverts (§3.4.9). §4.4's blanket exclusion of a grab-and-move keyboard model is narrowed to **resize** in the same breath, because otherwise this document contradicts itself on its own page.

Two sizing and feedback clauses ride with this ruling.

**The hit box is authored in a fixed unit, never off the space scale.** `--control-size-regular` is `calc(var(--sys-space-unit) * 11)` ([tokens.css:75](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:75)) — 44px at default density but **40.5px at compact 0.92**, below the floor. Every touch minimum in this design is re-derived at 0.92 and then written as a constant, so density can grow a target and never shrink it below 44.

**And every interactive surface these rulings introduce carries an ungated `:active` mirror** — the two handles, **the block body** (R40), the service and client rows and the pages they push (§3.6, §3.7), the search pages' checkbox rows (R13), the search-and-create row (R26), the add-on chips (R14), both `.staff-sheet__pill` triggers, and every `button[uiDay]` in the inline calendar (Ruling A). Hover styling stays `@media (hover: hover)`-gated. `data-dragging` is a drag state, not a press state: on a phone the press is the only feedback there is, and a hover-only affordance is an affordance that does not exist.

**How much chrome that is, stated honestly.** Four `uiControlSize="large"` buttons is `4 × --control-size-large`, and that token is `calc(var(--sys-space-unit) * 13)` — density-scaled like everything else. So the button height alone is **191 / 208 / 225 px** at densities 0.92 / 1.0 / 1.08, before the two `compact` gaps in the stack (7.4 / 8 / 8.6 px each) and the action bar's own inset. On a 375×812 phone the verbs own roughly a quarter of the sheet at every density.

Row inventory, with anchors:
