Alongside them: `seatsHere`, `barberAvatarSrc`, `barberTone`, `live`/`isNext`/`past`, `seatId`. **Orphan i18n keys already exist for five of them** — `staff.day.visitService`, `visitWhen`, `visitArrived`, `visitDuration`, `visitOpen` ([bg.json:979-990](../../libs/infrastructure/i18n/src/assets/i18n/bg.json:979)), none of them referenced by any template.

**The verb ladder.** `OFFERED = ['confirmed','completed','no_show','cancelled']` ([ts:509-514](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.ts:509)). `primaryVerb` ([ts:526-549](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.ts:526)) gates in order: pending + confirmed legal → `confirmed`; not arrived and pending-or-confirmed → `arrived`; **arrived and completed legal → `completed` (arrival, not the clock, gates finishing)**; `no_show` + confirmed legal → `confirmed` relabelled `Върни часа`. `overflow` is everything else, and **can never contain `arrived`**, so a confirmed-not-arrived row renders three full-width buttons plus a docked one.

**A live copy collision, verified.** `staff.day.act.confirmed` = **"Дойде"** ([bg.json:902](../../libs/infrastructure/i18n/src/assets/i18n/bg.json:902)) and `staff.day.act.arrived` = **"Дойде"** ([bg.json:906](../../libs/infrastructure/i18n/src/assets/i18n/bg.json:906)). Two different edges render the identical word. Today they never appear together; the redesign puts the verb next to the status, which makes it visible.

**The party seam.** `toRow` filters `appointment.seats` to `seat.barberId.value === barberId` ([ts:2221-2223](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.ts:2221)), so **a two-barber party is two rows** and the sheet shows one barber's share labelled `"1 / 2"`. The cancel path already faced this and solved it per-seat (`cancelSeatId`, [ts:2326](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.ts:2326)).

**Siblings, all `ui-modal-sheet`, all reusing `.staff-cancel__body`:** `staff-zone-sheet` ([html:431](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:431)), `staff-search-sheet` ([:462](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:462)), `staff-fields-sheet` ([:1131](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1131)), `staff-visit-sheet` ([:1212](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1212)), `staff-pending-sheet` ([:1355](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1355), whose entire body is `staff.day.notBuiltYet` = _"Още не е готово — това изисква запис от сървъра (фаза B4)."_), `staff-block-sheet` ([:1389](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1389)), `staff-cancel-sheet` ([:1589](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1589)).

⚠ **One of those siblings already owns the control the visit sheet is about to want.** `staff-block-sheet` renders a labelled From/To pair of `input[uiTextField] type="time" step="300"` wrapped in `.staff-block__field` ([html:1457-1484](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1457), [css:934-937](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.css:934) — `flex: 1 1 0; min-inline-size: 0`, because a time field has a fixed intrinsic width and would otherwise hug). **Ruling: the redesign renames that class and shares it. It does not write a second one.** REUSE, NEVER COPY applies to the sheet that is being rebuilt, not only to the ones that are not.

## 2.2 The domain model — the eight questions

### Q1 · Can one appointment hold multiple services?

**Yes, via `Seat` — one seat per service-instance. But the booker is capped at exactly one seat.**

`Appointment` → `readonly seats: readonly Seat[]` ([appointment.ts:123](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/appointment.ts:123)), documented as _"A booked visit to one location, carrying one or more Seats (a party of N is one Appointment, N seats — the appointment is the consistency boundary)."_

Per-seat: service, variant, **barber (resolved, not a preference)**, `BarberPref`, subject, **terms snapshotted at commit**, start instant, outcome. Per-appointment: location, status (a derived fold), contact (name/phone/email/note), `bookedAt`/`bookedFrom`/`arrivedAt`, and the derived time envelope.

`validateSeats` ([appointment.ts:275-316](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/appointment.ts:275)) enforces exactly four things: non-empty seats; **at most one `self` seat**; no barber double-booked across overlapping seats; one shared currency. **Nothing forces seats to be parallel or sequential** — the flexible-arrangement ruling is already structural.

**The blocker:** `AppointmentMultipleSelfSeatsError` ([appointment.ts:284-289](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/appointment.ts:284)). A cart with `self → [Fade, Beard trim]` produces two `self` seats → invariant error → `invalid-argument`. **Multi-service-for-one-person is unrepresentable today, and the failing path has no test anywhere.**

⚠ **A correction to the obvious fix.** All three proposals relaxed this to "no _overlapping_ self seats" and justified it by saying `collidesWith` already prevents the broken case. **It does not.** `collidesWith` ([seat.ts:222-227](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/seat.ts:222)) only forbids the **same barber** overlapping himself. Two self seats with two _different_ barbers at the same instant — one person in two chairs — passes the relaxed rule.

⚠⚠ **And a second correction, which kills the relaxation's usefulness for the staff case entirely.** `toSubject` ([decide-booking.ts:484-497](../../apps/functions/src/use-cases/decide-booking.ts:484)) maps `{kind:'self'}` to `SeatSubject.account(ownerUserId, 'self')` — bound to the token, so a payload cannot book in someone else's name. A staff-created walk-in **has no account**, so every one of its seats resolves to `SeatSubject.anonymous(label)` and **the self-seat invariant never fires at all.** A relaxation written in terms of `self` seats does nothing for the single most common staff case.

**Ruling: the guard is a pairwise interval intersection across _all_ seats, independent of `barberId` and independent of `subject.kind`.** One human occupies one interval; the model's word for that human — `account/self` or `anonymous` — is an authorship fact, not a body fact. Anything narrower re-opens the hole for walk-ins.

### Q2 · Per-booking duration or price override?

**Neither exists, and both are refused at three layers, deliberately.**

1. **The seat has no field.** `Seat.slot` is derived from `terms.durationMinutes` ([seat.ts:198-208](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/seat.ts:198)): _"there is one answer to 'how long is this seat', and it is the one that was sold."_
2. **The wire refuses it.** `CommitBookingSeatRequest` ([booking-gateway.port.ts:8-20](../../libs/application/booking/src/lib/ports/booking-gateway.port.ts:8)): _"Notice what is NOT here: no price, no duration, no owner… A client that could name its own price would be a client that books a 40 € fade for nothing; one that could name its own duration would be one that books over the next appointment."_
3. **The server re-derives.** [decide-booking.ts:290-291](../../apps/functions/src/use-cases/decide-booking.ts:290) — `const terms = service.termsFor(barberId, variantId);` under the comment `// SERVER-RESOLVED terms — the whole point of the round trip.` `toSeats` reads only `lineId, serviceId, variantId, barberId, startIso, subject`.

**This is not a missing affordance. It is a deliberate refusal, and the redesign must break it only for a role-gated staff caller.**

⚠ **`appointmentToDocument` writes terms verbatim, so an override round-trips silently today.** Without a persisted marker, analytics could never distinguish a 45-minute fade from a 30-minute fade someone stretched — and the data is unrecoverable afterwards.

### Q3 · Are upsells / add-ons modelled? What does `upsellOnly` do?

**`upsellOnly` is a flag on `Service` with exactly one reader — the marketing landing page** ([landing-content.service.ts:94](../../libs/features/marketing/landing/src/lib/content/landing-content.service.ts:94), `filter((service) => !service.upsellOnly)`). It survives into the shared catalog view-model as inert data ([catalog-vm.ts:67](../../libs/features/shared/catalog/src/lib/content/catalog-vm.ts:67)) and stops there. It has no accessor, no method, no invariant. It is **not** read by the client booking flow, the staff dashboard, `decideBooking`, or `availableOptions`.

**Consequence: an `upsellOnly` service is fully bookable as a standalone today.** The flag is a marketing-visibility toggle wearing a commerce name.

**There is no `Service.upsellsFor` — the symbol does not exist anywhere in the repo.** Nothing in the model can answer "what goes with this?"; any Part 3 design that asks the question is proposing **new** domain surface, and must be sized as such.

The nearest thing to add-ons is `ServiceComposition` — `single | bundle{includes}` — and **`servicesConflict` ([service-conflicts.ts:68-91](../../libs/domain/catalog/src/lib/service-conflicts.ts:68), exported from the catalog barrel at [index.ts:22](../../libs/domain/catalog/src/index.ts:22)) is real, shipped, and specced.** It combines three sources of truth: authored conflicts normalised symmetrically, bundle membership derived from `composition.includes`, and conflicts inherited _through_ membership. Its companions `conflictingWith` ([:102-110](../../libs/domain/catalog/src/lib/service-conflicts.ts:102)) and `selectabilityFor` ([:112-119](../../libs/domain/catalog/src/lib/service-conflicts.ts:112)) return the blockers by id, because _"an unexplained lock is the failure mode this whole module exists to prevent."_

**But it is exclusion machinery, and an add-on is the opposite.** `servicesConflict` tells a compose surface which services may not sit together on one seat. It cannot tell it which ones _should_. **Ruling: reuse `selectabilityFor` verbatim to gate multi-select — it is the right tool and it exists — and treat "which add-on goes with this cut" as an unmodelled question with no interim heuristic available from this module.**

### Q4 · Promos / discounts?

**Modelled thoroughly. Attachable to an appointment: no. Wired to _scheduling_: not one line.**

`libs/domain/engagement` has `CouponValue` (`percent_off | fixed_amount | fixed Money | free_service`), `Coupon`, `CouponGrant` with capacity and expiration, `CouponCombinability`, `VoucherCode`, and **`DiscountApplication.apply(subtotal, discounts, {capPercent})` → `DiscountBreakdown {subtotal, lines, discountTotal, total}`** with a deterministic total order.

**The evaluator is not orphaned — it has a production caller.** `ApplyDiscountsUseCase` loads grants through `CouponGrantRepository.findUsableForUser` and calls `apply()` at [apply-discounts.use-case.ts:57](../../libs/application/engagement/src/lib/use-cases/apply-discounts.use-case.ts:57). **The orphan is one level up: `ApplyDiscountsUseCase` itself is constructed in exactly one place, its own spec** ([apply-discounts.use-case.spec.ts:87](../../libs/application/engagement/src/lib/use-cases/apply-discounts.use-case.spec.ts:87), [:116](../../libs/application/engagement/src/lib/use-cases/apply-discounts.use-case.spec.ts:116)). `COUPON_GRANT_REPOSITORY` is provided at [app.config.ts:213](../../apps/web/src/app/app.config.ts:213) and **injected by nothing.**

`appointmentToDocument` writes no discount field. `Appointment.subtotal()` ([appointment.ts:363-373](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/appointment.ts:363)) is documented as _"What the party owes **before** discounts"_ — there is no `total()`, no `discounts`, no `DiscountLine[]`.

**So the missing piece is precise: a caller from the scheduling side, plus a place on the appointment for the answer to land.** Not an evaluator. Not a cascade rule. A wire and a field. **This is the largest single gap in the owner's list, and it is smaller than it looks — which is exactly why it must not be sold as bigger.**

### Q5 · Is there an all-day concept?

**Not for appointments — but the toggle already ships for blocks, and the redesign inherits it rather than inventing it.**

Three near-neighbours exist, all about _roster_: `ScheduleException.isWholeDay()`, `DayWindows.isWholeDay()` (a client availability declaration), and the grid's all-day rail — **which is already built and rendering**. The rail takes `allDay`, `allDayLabel` and `allDayAlways` as inputs ([staff-time-grid.ts:235-246](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:235)) and draws a pinned row of caption chips per column ([staff-time-grid.html:79-90](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.html:79)). `allDayAlways` exists for a stated reason: _"A row that appears and disappears moves every hour beneath it, so the grid jumps as you page between days."_ Today the rail carries exactly one thing: an "off" chip for an unrostered barber.

And `staff-block-sheet` **already renders an all-day switch** — a `button[uiSwitch]` bound to `blockAllDay`, labelled `staff.day.blockAllDay`, which hides the From/To pair when on ([html:1443-1457](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1443)). The affordance the owner asked for exists; what does not exist is its meaning on an _appointment_.

**What would break if an all-day toggle flipped an appointment:**

1. `Seat.slot` is `TimeSlot.fromDuration(startsAt, durationMinutes)` and `TimeSlot.of` refuses `start >= end`. "All day" would be a real **1440-minute seat**, not a flag.
2. `classifyOccupancy` marks `service` as `{capacity:'scheduled', productive: true}` — **the barber reports 100% productive.**
3. `Appointment.subtotal()` folds a real `Money` — **it prices a closed shop.**
4. `busyKeysOf` ([appointment-document.ts:355](../../libs/application/booking/src/lib/ports/appointment-document.ts:355)) writes one busy doc that **occludes the next-day boundary.**
5. Writing it as an _exception_ instead would push a client's name across the **GDPR boundary** — `exceptionToDocument` ([schedule-exception-document.ts:70](../../libs/application/booking/src/lib/ports/schedule-exception-document.ts:70)) is that boundary, by name, and it strips `detail.note` on purpose.

**`staff-day.store.ts:738-783` already does the right thing for a block**: `blockTime(barberId, locationId, ranges)`, where **empty `ranges` means the whole day** → `{kind:'time_off'}` → sanitised to public `{kind:'closed'}`, and a partial block is `{kind:'admin', ranges}` → `blocked` ([staff-day.store.ts:761-765](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:761)).

🔴 **But it does exactly one thing, and the redesign's second block destroys the first.** The id is `ScheduleExceptionId.of(\`${barberId}__${day.key()}\`)`([staff-day.store.ts:754](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:754)) — **one exception document per barber per day** — written with`put`([:774](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:774)), which is a blind overwrite. Create a second block from a long-press on the frame and **the first one silently vanishes.** And`clearBlock(barberId)`([:786-800](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:786)) calls`exceptions.clear(barberId, dayKey)` — it lifts the barber's **entire day**, not one block.

**Ruling: "blocking time is already built" is false the moment a day can hold two blocks.** `ScheduleException` must accumulate ranges — read-modify-write, or a per-block document id — and `clearBlock` must take a range, before a second block can exist. That is domain work, not a UI wire.

⚠ And `blockTime` passes `note: ''` into the `admin` detail ([:764](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:764)), which the sanitizer then strips anyway — _"a reason has no field to ride in"_ ([:735-737](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:735)). **A block note has nowhere to land today.**

### Q6 · Participants

Four types, three unrelated:

| Type             | Role                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `BookingParty`   | **who books** — pre-commit roster, never persisted onto an `Appointment`                        |
| `SeatSubject`    | **who a seat is for** — `{kind:'anonymous', label}` or `{kind:'account', userId, relationship}` |
| `BookingContact` | **who the shop calls** — one per appointment, a snapshot, **nullable**                          |
| `BarberPref`     | `{kind:'any'} \| {kind:'specific', barberId}` — a _preference_, distinct from the assignment    |

**Adding a barber is adding a seat, and the model already allows it.** `collidesWith` only forbids the same barber overlapping himself; `Appointment.barberIds()` already dedupes and returns a list. **What is missing is the write path, not the model** — the aggregate exposes only `markArrived`, `confirm`, `complete`, `markNoShow`, `reopenNoShow`, `cancel`, `markSeatOutcome`. There is no `addSeat`/`removeSeat`; reshaping happens only by full rebuild in `decideBooking`.

**Quick-creating a client without an account is already fully expressible** — `SeatSubject.anonymous(label)`, documented as _"The minimum-viable subject a barber can commit one-tap mid-cut"_, and the wire already accepts `{kind:'guest', label}` ([commit-booking.ts:128-131](../../apps/functions/src/lib/booking/commit-booking.ts:128)).

🔴 **Finding an _existing_ client, however, is not expressible at all — twice over.**

**(a) No port method.** `UserRepositoryPort` ([user-repository.port.ts:56-68](../../libs/application/identity/src/lib/ports/user-repository.port.ts:56)) offers exactly three methods: `provision`, `findByDestination`, `saveRegistered`. There is no search, no prefix index, and no Firestore composite index for one. **`findClients` does not exist anywhere in the codebase** — only in prior design docs. But client search does: it lives in **governance**, not identity. `UserSearchPort.search(query)` ([user-search.port.ts:12-17](../../libs/application/governance/src/lib/ports/user-search.port.ts:12)), `SearchUsersUseCase`, `FirestoreUserSearchAdapter` ([user-search.adapter.ts:41-69](../../libs/infrastructure/firestore/src/lib/user-search.adapter.ts:41)) and the deployed composite index ([firestore.indexes.json:118](../../firestore.indexes.json:118)) all ship, and the token is provided in the web app ([app.config.ts:225](../../apps/web/src/app/app.config.ts:225)). **Ruling: the people picker wires that port; it does not build a second search.** What _is_ new is a callable to serve the barber, whom `/users` `allow list` refuses — see §3.7.

**(b) The primary persona is not permitted to run it even if it existed.** `allow list` on `/users` is `isOwner(uid) || hasAnyRole(['receptionist','admin','sysadmin'])` ([firestore.rules:96-97](../../firestore.rules:96)), under a comment saying the search surface over everyone's phone, email and birthDate is _"front-desk and admin business only."_ **A plain `barber` gets permission-denied** — and the barber is exactly the person this document says is holding the phone one-handed mid-cut. `allow get` is wider (`isStaff()`, [:95](../../firestore.rules:95)), so a barber can read a client they already have the id for; they cannot go looking.

🐛 **`barberPref` is silently dropped at the boundary.** [booking-flow.store.ts:539](../../libs/features/client/booking/src/lib/booking-flow.store.ts:539) sends it. `toSeats` ([commit-booking.ts:117-134](../../apps/functions/src/lib/booking/commit-booking.ts:117)) **never reads `seat['barberPref']`**, so [decide-booking.ts:326-329](../../apps/functions/src/use-cases/decide-booking.ts:326) always takes the else-branch. **Every appointment ever committed is recorded as `specific`.** The field the model exists for — _"the first question asked on any absence"_ — carries no information. **One field. Fix it before anything else here ships**, because the redesign surfaces a `♡ клиентът иска този бръснар` marker over it. And the repair is forward-only: **rows already written are unrecoverable, and `barberPref`-derived analytics must treat pre-fix rows as unknown, never as `specific`.**

### Q7 · What write paths does a staff client have?

**Firestore direct writes:** `appointments` is `allow create: if false` / `update: if false` / `delete: if false` ([firestore.rules:193-198](../../firestore.rules:193)) — for everyone, staff included. The rules file says why: _"The earlier `create: if isStaff()` let a receptionist write an appointment the availability engine never saw … the sanctioned walk-in path was a guaranteed double-booking."_

**Callables:**

| Callable                    | Gate                                                                                                                       | Can it move/resize?                              |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `transitionAppointment`     | `isStaffCaller` only ([transition-appointment.ts:109](../../apps/functions/src/lib/booking/transition-appointment.ts:109)) | **No.** Writes only `status` + `seats[].outcome` |
| `markArrived`               | `isStaffCaller` only ([mark-arrived.ts:45](../../apps/functions/src/lib/booking/mark-arrived.ts:45))                       | No — stamps `arrivedAt`, idempotent              |
| **`rescheduleAppointment`** | **owner-only** ([firestore-booking-store.ts:155](../../apps/functions/src/adapters/firestore-booking-store.ts:155))        | **Yes, but staff cannot call it**                |
| `commitBooking`             | any signed-in user; **requires a truthy `ownerUserId`**                                                                    | creates only                                     |
| `cancelAppointment`         | owner-only ([cancel-appointment.ts:61](../../apps/functions/src/lib/booking/cancel-appointment.ts:61))                     | No                                               |

**The store's only writes** are `blockTime`/`clearBlock` ([staff-day.store.ts:738](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:738), [:786](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:786)), `markArrived` ([:807](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:807)), and `transition` ([:835](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:835)). `TransitionAppointmentRequest` carries only `{appointmentId, to, reasonCode?, note?, seatId?}`.

🔴 **Blocker (a): `rescheduleAppointment` is owner-scoped.** `firestore-booking-store.ts:155` compares the caller's uid against the document's `ownerUserId` and returns an invalid-input failure that is _"indistinguishable from not-found on purpose."_ A barber's uid never equals the client's. **Staff cannot move any client's booking at all.** Owner ruling Q3 (2026-08-07) already granted the fix — _"staff may move a client's booking, including inside the cancellation window, audited"_ — **and the server was never changed.**

🔴 **Blocker (b): a staff walk-in cannot be _created_, and what does exist is only half-frozen.** Two separate facts, and the earlier readings got both of them wrong in opposite directions:

- **A walk-in cannot be created today at all.** `CommitBookingUseCase.execute` returns `CommitBookingUnauthenticatedError` the moment `ownerUserId` is falsy ([commit-booking.use-case.ts:66-68](../../apps/functions/src/use-cases/commit-booking.use-case.ts:66)), and `decideBooking` then requires `UserId.create(deps.ownerUserId)` to succeed ([decide-booking.ts:193-196](../../apps/functions/src/use-cases/decide-booking.ts:193)). `{kind:'guest', label}` works only for _companion_ seats inside a party that an authenticated owner is booking. **There is no unauthenticated create path.**
- **`ownerUserId: null` freezes the _client_, not staff.** `transitionAppointment` performs **no ownership check whatsoever** — it gates on `isStaffCaller` and then reads `ownerUserId` purely to address the notification ([transition-appointment.ts:302](../../apps/functions/src/lib/booking/transition-appointment.ts:302)); `markArrived` is identical ([mark-arrived.ts:118](../../apps/functions/src/lib/booking/mark-arrived.ts:118)). **Staff can already cancel and no-show a null-owner appointment.** What a null owner actually blocks is: reschedule by anyone (`firestore-booking-store.ts:155`), and cancel _by the client_ (`cancel-appointment.ts:61`).

**Ruling: the walk-in problem is a create problem, not a freeze problem.** `ownerUserId` must become nullable through `CommitBookingUseCase` → `decideBooking` → `toSubject`, with a staff-attributed `createdByUserId` replacing it for audit. That is a domain-and-wire change of real size, not a flag.

🔴 **Blocker (c): a role grouping mismatch that hands the wrong person the book.** `STAFF_ROLES` ([user-role.ts:44-50](../../libs/domain/accounts/src/lib/user-role.ts:44)) is `barber | receptionist | content_manager | admin | sysadmin`, and both callables gate on it. `firestore.rules` deliberately narrows: `worksTheBook()` ([firestore.rules:47-49](../../firestore.rules:47)) is `barber | receptionist | admin | sysadmin`, and it is what guards appointment reads ([:166](../../firestore.rules:166)) under an explicit comment — _content_manager "could read every appointment, every client name, phone and note in the shop for a role that only edits marketing copy."_

**So today a `content_manager` cannot READ an appointment, but CAN transition it and stamp its arrival.** A marketing role can no-show a client it is not allowed to see. **Ruling: the predicate the new callable extracts is `worksTheBook`, not `isStaffCaller`, and the two existing call sites are corrected in the same PR.** Shipping a staff-edit callable on `STAFF_ROLES` would hand that same role the power to move bookings and discount them.

🔴 **And a fourth, which only one reading caught.** `RescheduleBookingUseCase` rebuilds through `Appointment.reconstitute` restoring only `{id, locationId, seats, status, contact, bookedAt, bookedFromAppointmentId}` ([reschedule-booking.use-case.ts:156-167](../../apps/functions/src/use-cases/reschedule-booking.use-case.ts:156)). **`arrivedAt` is not passed — and `reconstitute` accepts `arrivedAt?` at [appointment.ts:236](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/appointment.ts:236) and [:270](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/appointment.ts:270).** Because `hasResolvedSeat` only inspects seat _outcomes_, an arrived-but-not-completed visit passes the guard, moves, and **silently loses its arrival stamp** — and `primaryVerb` gates the `Готово` verb on `arrived`, so **the completion verb disappears from the sheet after any staff edit.** One line to fix. It must land in the same PR as the callable.

### Q8 · Buffers and padding — drawn geometry vs sold duration

`ServicePadding {setupMinutes?, cleanupMinutes?}` → `ServiceTerms`, with the ruling stated at [service-terms.ts:27-43](../../libs/domain/catalog/src/lib/service-terms.ts:27): _"The client is quoted, and charged for, the SERVICE — not the mop-up. A duration that swallows cleanup lies in the confirmation."_ And: _"`ServiceTerms` is already resolved per (barber, variant), so padding declared here inherits BOTH axes for free."_

**The seam:**

| What                  | Interval                                 | Anchor                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Sold duration**     | `[startsAt, startsAt + durationMinutes)` | [seat.ts:198-208](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/seat.ts:198)                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Occupied envelope** | `[start − setup, end + cleanup)`         | [decide-booking.ts:335-338](../../apps/functions/src/use-cases/decide-booking.ts:335)                                                                                                                                  |
| **Drawn block**       | **sold duration only**                   | [staff-dashboard.ts:2224-2225](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.ts:2224), [:1369-1370](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.ts:1369) |
| **Gaps in the day**   | occupied envelope                        | [staff-day.store.ts:152-172](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:152)                                                                                                                       |

**A block with 15 minutes of cleanup draws 45 minutes tall but reserves 60**, and the missing quarter-hour shows only as an absent gap card. **A barber dragging into that apparent free space is dragging into cleanup, and the server will refuse a placement the UI showed as legal. Drawing the shoulders is a precondition for drag being safe, not a decoration.**

## 2.3 The design-system primitives available

Everything is `ViewEncapsulation.None`, `OnPush`, host class `ui-*`, variants as `data-*`, CSS in `@layer sys-components`.

**Controls** (`@creativo/ui/controls`, whose barrel also re-exports layout and patterns; this lists the ones the redesign can reach for, not the full directory): `button[uiButton]` (the one button; `data-control-size` = the three-rung scale below), `ui-avatar`, `span[uiBadge]`, `button[uiChip]` (**toggle only — two inputs, `uiSelected` and `uiControlSize` ([chip.ts:27-28](../../libs/ui/controls/src/lib/chip/chip.ts:27)); no remove slot, no trailing slot, no role variants**), `ui-date-field` (**date only — day/month/year segments, [date-field.ts:128-133](../../libs/ui/controls/src/lib/date-field/date-field.ts:128); no time**), `ui-detail-sheet`, `ui-icon` (closed union `UiIconName`, icons inherit font size), **`ui-modal-sheet`**, `ui-otp-field`, **`ui-phone-field`** (the **only** APG combobox in the repo — [phone-field.html:15](../../libs/ui/controls/src/lib/phone-field/phone-field.html:15) — and it is private), `ui-progress-view`, `ui-progress-ring`, `ui-skeleton`, `button[uiSwitch]`, `input|textarea[uiTextField]` (**two inputs, `uiControlSize` and `uiInvalid` — [text-field.ts:27-28](../../libs/ui/controls/src/lib/text-field/text-field.ts:27)**).

**Layout**: `ui-stack`, `ui-flow` (wrapping HStack — the chip cluster), `ui-grid`, `ui-scroll-row` (⚠ `overflow-x: auto` at [scroll-row.css:4](../../libs/ui/layout/src/lib/scroll-row/scroll-row.css:4) clips popovers), `ui-toolbar`, `ui-divider` (**banned inside a list group**), `ui-spacer`, `ui-sheet` + `[uiSheetBehavior]`.

**Patterns**: **`ui-list-group`** + **`ui-list-row`**, `ui-menu` + `[uiMenuTrigger]` + `[uiMenuItem]`, `ui-detent-sheet`, `ui-sheet-header` (grabber + collapsing title), **`ui-sheet-action-bar`**, `ui-calendar-grid`, `ui-calendar-scroller`, `ui-date-badge`, `ui-stepper` (⚠ **a journey `role="progressbar"`, NOT a numeric ±**), `ui-status-indicator`, `ui-card`, `ui-section-header`, `ui-page-action-bar`, `ui-empty-state`, `ui-rating`, `ui-confetti`, `ui-reward-moment`.

**Modifiers** ([modifiers.css](../../libs/ui/modifiers/modifiers.css)): `uiText`/`uiFont`/`uiWeight`, `uiForegroundStyle`, `uiPadding`, `uiRadius`, `uiFrame` (inline styles — sanctioned), `uiMaterial` (chrome only), **`uiInteractive`**, `uiOverlay`, `uiReveal`, `uiDisabled`, `uiLink`, `uiVisuallyHidden`.

### Verified facts that constrain the redesign

**`uiInteractive` is the one hover/press grammar, and its shape is a standing rule, not a convention.** Hover lives inside `@media (hover: hover)` ([modifiers.css:227-235](../../libs/ui/modifiers/modifiers.css:227)); press is **ungated** — a state layer at [:243-250](../../libs/ui/modifiers/modifiers.css:243) on the instant tier (150ms, because the owner tested a literal 0ms entry on a real iPhone and it _"felt abrupt and, combined with iOS's own touch-vs-scroll disambiguation, buggy"_), plus a `scale(var(--sys-press-scale-surface))` at [:252-258](../../libs/ui/modifiers/modifiers.css:252). Both arms exclude `:disabled`, `[aria-disabled='true']` and `[data-disabled]`, because _"feedback is a promise; a disabled surface must not make it."_

**Ruling, binding on every new interactive surface in Part 3 — the frame handle, the ghost row, the service cards, the add-on chips, the ✕ on tokens: hover styling is `@media (hover: hover)`-gated and every hover affordance carries an ungated `:active` mirror.** A `data-dragging` attribute is a _mode_, not a press state; it does not satisfy this. A barber's phone has no hover, so a surface whose only feedback is a hover rule is a surface with no feedback at all.

**`ui-modal-sheet`'s drag is bound only to `<ui-sheet-header>`** ([modal-sheet.html:40-43](../../libs/ui/controls/src/lib/modal-sheet/modal-sheet.html:40)), which carries `touch-action: none` and sits above the scroller. **Nothing in the sheet body contends with it.** The much-feared "three nested drag consumers" problem does not exist for a modal sheet.

**`ui-detent-sheet`'s drag is bound to BOTH `.ui-detent-sheet__grabber` and `.ui-detent-sheet__content`** ([detent-sheet.ts:103-106](../../libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/detent-sheet/detent-sheet.ts:103), [:125-128](../../libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/detent-sheet/detent-sheet.ts:125)), with `DRAG_THRESHOLD = 8` ([:52](../../libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/detent-sheet/detent-sheet.ts:52)) and **no bail on `button`/`a`**. `UI_DETENT_FRACTION` is `{small: 0.2, medium: 0.48, large: 0.92}` ([:30-34](../../libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/detent-sheet/detent-sheet.ts:30)) — `small` is **20% of the viewport, 162px on a 375×812 phone.** And its own doc says: _"It is therefore NOT for anything that needs an answer before the user continues."_

**`ui-sheet-action-bar`'s dock rule** ([sheet-action-bar.css:113-119](../../libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/sheet-action-bar/sheet-action-bar.css:113)) applies `margin-inline-start: auto` to **`> [data-spread]`, `> [data-button-style='borderedProminent']`, AND `> [uiprimary]`** — so _any two_ commit-shaped children both try to dock trailing. `staff-schedule-hig-mobile-audit.md §1.2` already recorded this as a phone-only regression.

**`ui-list-group`'s seam is `gap: calc(var(--sys-space-unit) / 2)`** ([list-group.css:8](../../libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/list-group/list-group.css:8)) — 1.84 / 2.0 / 2.16px across the density range — rows paint their own surface, and `> :not(.ui-list-row) { display: contents }` ([list-group.css:26-27](../../libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/list-group/list-group.css:26)) — **so a disclosure panel placed as a group child gets no surface and no corners**, and needs ~6 lines of feature CSS to paint them.

### Tokens, and why every pixel in this document is a range

`--sys-space-unit: calc(0.25rem * var(--sys-density))` ([tokens.css:50-51](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:50)), and `[data-density]` sets **0.92** (`compact`, [:232](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:232)) or **1.08** (`spacious`, [:235](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:235)) against a default of **1.0**. **Nearly every geometric token in the system multiplies that unit — including the control scale.** Any figure in this document derived from it is therefore three figures:

| Token                     | Formula             |      0.92 |       1.0 |      1.08 |
| ------------------------- | ------------------- | --------: | --------: | --------: |
| `--sys-space-unit`        | `0.25rem × density` |      3.68 |      4.00 |      4.32 |
| `--sys-space-tight`       | `× 1`               |      3.68 |         4 |      4.32 |
| `--sys-space-compact`     | `× 2`               |      7.36 |         8 |      8.64 |
| `--sys-space-regular`     | `× 4`               |     14.72 |        16 |     17.28 |
| `--sys-space-comfortable` | `× 6`               |     22.08 |        24 |     25.92 |
| `--sys-space-loose`       | `× 8`               |     29.44 |        32 |     34.56 |
| `--sys-space-spacious`    | `× 12`              |     44.16 |        48 |     51.84 |
| `--control-size-small`    | `× 9`               |  **33.1** |    **36** |  **38.9** |
| `--control-size-regular`  | `× 11`              |  **40.5** |    **44** |  **47.5** |
| `--control-size-large`    | `× 13`              |  **47.8** |    **52** |  **56.2** |
| `--staff-slot-height`     | `× 7` (per 15 min)  |     25.76 |        28 |     30.24 |
| ⤷ px per minute           | `÷ 15`              | **1.717** | **1.867** | **2.016** |

(`--sys-space-none` is `0`; there is still **no 12px rung**. Rungs at [tokens.css:52-62](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:52), control sizes at [:66-76](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:66).)

🔴 **Ruling: the 36/44/52 scale is exact only at density 1.0, and the HIG tap target is the casualty.** `--control-size-regular` — the rung the whole system treats as "the 44pt tap target" — is **40.5px at compact density**, four points under the floor. **Every touch-target threshold in Part 3 is derived at 0.92, never at 1.0.** A design that clears 44 only at default density does not clear it for the barber who turned density down to fit more of the day on screen, which is precisely the barber most likely to have done so.

Same arithmetic, same caveat, on the grid's own measurement: `SHORT_BLOCK_MINUTES = 30` is justified in-code by _"a slot is 28px … so a half-hour block is 56px tall"_ ([staff-time-grid.ts:139-153](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:139)). At 0.92 that half-hour block is **51.5px**, and after its 1px margins and 2px padding roughly 45px of content box is left against ~33px of two lines. It still fits — but the comment's number is a density-1.0 number, and the constant is one density step from being wrong.

**Colour and motion, which are not density-scaled.** `--sys-color-accent` = **`#f26b22` in both themes** ([theme-light.css:24](../../libs/ui/tokens/theme-light.css:24), [theme-dark.css:26](../../libs/ui/tokens/theme-dark.css:26)); `--sys-color-fill` is **translucent** — `color-mix(foreground × --sys-alpha-fill, transparent)` at [tokens.css:137-140](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:137), never an opaque surface; `--sys-identity-0..4` are the five chair hues, **deliberately excluding orange because the accent alone means "look here."** `--sys-color-promo` / `--sys-color-on-promo` exist ([theme-light.css:44-45](../../libs/ui/tokens/theme-light.css:44), [theme-dark.css:40-41](../../libs/ui/tokens/theme-dark.css:40)) and are **used nowhere outside the theme files.** `--control-radius-subtle|regular|prominent|hero|capsule` ride `--sys-radius-base × --sys-radius-scale` ([tokens.css:85-101](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:85)), not the space unit. Motion: `--sys-motion-duration-instant` 150 / `-regular` 200 / `-deliberate` 300 ([tokens.css:203-205](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:203)); `--sys-motion-ease-standard|emphasized|entrance`.

**The time grid.** `MINUTES_PER_SLOT = 15` ([staff-time-grid.ts:136](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:136)), `DAY_MINUTES = 1440` ([:138](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:138)), `--staff-slot-height: calc(var(--sys-space-unit) * 7)` ([staff-time-grid.css:19](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.css:19)) — **1.72–2.02 px/min, per the table above.** Placement is CSS grid rows computed with `Math.floor`/`Math.ceil` ([staff-time-grid.ts:534-539](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:534)) — **which rounds outward: a 09:05 start already draws at 09:00 on the live page grid.** The now-line, by contrast, already uses a percentage offset (`inset-block-start: calc(var(--staff-now-fraction, 0) * 100%)`, [staff-time-grid.css:686](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.css:686)) — **the sub-slot precision the frame needs already exists in this file, on one element.** `GridEvent`'s axis is **minutes-from-midnight, never an epoch** — which is what lets one renderer serve a chair-columned day and a date-columned week and takes the timezone out of the grid entirely.

**There is no pointer handling anywhere in the feature.** `grep -rEn "pointerdown|pointermove|setPointerCapture|touch-action" libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/` returns nothing. Blocks are `<button (click)="pick(event)">`. Every gesture in Part 3 is built from zero, not extended.

**Money**: `formatMoney(money, locale)` from `@creativo/domain/kernel` ([format-money.ts:18](../../libs/domain/kernel/src/lib/format-money.ts:18)) — takes the `Money` VO, reads the currency's own exponent, **decimals never dropped**, because _"`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` only lines a column up when the strings share a shape."_ **The locale is not implicit: the staff surface passes `transloco.getActiveLang()`** ([staff-dashboard.ts:1504](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.ts:1504)), so the tag is the bare `'bg'` / `'en'` that Transloco holds, never `bg-BG` — every `28,00 €` in this document is that `bg` rendering. (`CatalogPresenter.locale()` reads the same signal.) `seatsPrice` returns `null` on a currency mismatch ([staff-dashboard.ts:1501](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.ts:1501)) — ⚠ **but that branch is dead for any saved appointment**, because `validateSeats` rejects mixed currency at build ([appointment.ts:306-313](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/appointment.ts:306)) and `Appointment.subtotal()` throws `'unreachable: mixed currency'` on the same grounds ([appointment.ts:363-373](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/appointment.ts:363)). **A "mixed currency" message has no state on a persisted appointment to describe.** If Part 3 wants one, it belongs to the pre-save draft, not to the sheet.

**Time**: there is **no shared time formatter**. `shopClock`, `shopMinuteOfDay`, `minuteOfClock`, `minuteOfDay`, `time`, `hourLabel` all live locally. `SHOP_ZONE = 'Europe/Sofia'` ([staff-dashboard.ts:506](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.ts:506)).

**Verified absent from the whole repo — anything Part 3 names from this list is _new_, and must be sized:** any numeric ± stepper; any resizable calendar block; any removable chip or token (`ui-chip` has `uiSelected` and `uiControlSize`, and neither removes a token); any trailing slot or role variant on `ui-chip`; any generic combobox outside `ui-phone-field` (there is no `[uiCombobox]`); any tabular-numerals directive (`[uiTabularNumerals]`); any dismiss guard (`[uiDismissGuard]`); any `uiPlacement`/`uiViewport`/`uiWindow`/`uiSnapMinutes`/`uiEditableEventId`/`eventDraft` on `staff-time-grid`; any `--staff-minute-height` token; any `Service.upsellsFor`; any symbol named `findClients` (the real port is `UserSearchPort.search`, which exists and is wired — §3.7); any applied-promo UI; any price or time override field.

---

# Part 3 — The redesign

## 3.1 The concept, in one paragraph

The visit sheet stops being a read-only card with four stacked buttons and becomes **one component that is a segmented ladder at two heights, live at both.** There is no edit mode and no Edit button: the sheet is clean or dirty, and the only thing a tap ever changes is how tall it is. At its short height — the height it opens at, and the height it stays at for four out of five things a barber does in a day — it is a static header title, a **pinned summary strip that never scrolls away** (`Мартин Илиев · 10:00 – 10:45 · 45 мин   ● Потвърден`), the client's note as a blockquote, and a docked bar carrying the phone, the overflow menu and the one verb the state machine says comes next, all at the `--control-size-large` rung ([tokens.css:76](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:76)). That whole top region contains **no interactive control at all** — it is the safe place to read, made of text rather than of disabled fields. **Touching anything compound un-fits the sheet** and opens a draft; nothing writes on release, because `decideBooking` re-decides placement and can refuse, and a lane that lied for a second teaches staff to distrust it. Un-fitted, the ladder runs **day → picture → clock**: a `Ден` row whose tinted date pill expands a month grid **inline, as the next segment of its own list group**; beneath it a 100-minute close-up of that chair's day; and beneath that `Начало` and `Времетраене` — **the two facts a barber actually authors, from which the end time is computed and never stored.** The frame carries the booking's setup and cleanup shoulders, two accent chevrons straddling its edges that resize it in five-minute steps, and — new, and reversing this document's own earlier ruling — **a draggable body that moves the whole block**, taken on touch by a 250 ms zero-tolerance hold rather than by switching `touch-action` mid-gesture. Every group below it is the design system's real segmented list: a chromeless `ui-list-group`, a half-unit seam, per-row surfaces, prominent outer corners — **no card, no dividers, and no section titles**, because a group whose first row already says what it is does not need an eyebrow admitting the row failed. Services and clients are **rows with a `›`**: a service names its minutes, its price and — only when it differs from the chair the frame is drawing — its barber, and tapping it **pushes a page inside this sheet's own navigation stack**, where its price, its duration and its barber live together and its removal sits at the bottom of the scroll. The money block is honest about being a derivation, carries one `Промоция` row that pushes, and shows nothing promo-shaped until the last milestone. The staff note is a `＋ Добави бележка` row until there is a note to hold. There is no all-day switch on a booking; all-day is a kind switch at creation that routes to a `ScheduleException`, and that switch already ships — `staff.day.blockAllDay`, bound to a real `button[uiSwitch]` at [staff-dashboard.html:1443-1455](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1443).

## 3.2 The tier model

> **Ruling (owner ask #5, 2026-08-26): always editable. There is no Edit button, no read mode, and no moment at which a control on this sheet becomes live. "Editable" is two write regimes on one never-moded surface, split by reversibility — not by mode.**

> **⚠ 2026-08-26, second pass — the tier model SURVIVES the twelve comments intact, and this is worth saying out loud.** Rulings A, B and C rearrange what is _in_ the ladder; none of them touches what the ladder _is_. Two heights, two regimes, one commit, no mode. The one genuinely new thing the twelve comments add to this section is a **third depth that is not a sheet** — a pushed page inside this sheet's own navigation stack (Ruling C) — and the tables below name it `Deeper` rather than `Nested`, because calling a push a nesting is how a second scrim gets built by accident.

The owner's instinct is right, and it is right for a reason specific to this shop rather than because the big calendars do it. **On the phone they emphatically do not**: Apple routes an existing event through read → `Edit` → `Done` and that split survived a total design-system replacement in iOS 26; Outlook mobile shows a pencil only on events you organised; Google's pencil opens a different route entirely. What all three _also_ do is let you move and resize an event by dragging it, **with no mode and no Save** — and so does every salon product that ships direct manipulation (Mangomint drag-and-drop, Vagaro long-press-drag). Of ten products studied, **zero open an editable form on a tap; five change the single most-changed attribute — time — with no mode whatsoever**, and Fresha changes _status_ the same way.

So the industry does not separate read from edit. **It separates cheap-atomic-reversible from compound-and-consequential**, and read-first is the side effect of gating the compound form, not a goal.

We decline the form gate, because our four commonest acts are _"nudge it ten minutes"_, _"add a beard trim"_, _"mark arrived"_, _"call them"_ — and **none of them is a form.** A mode gate taxes 80% of openings to protect a 20% case that already has better protection: a commit button.

### The two regimes

|           | **Regime A — immediate**                                                                                                                                                                             | **Regime B — draft + commit**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| What      | status verbs (`Потвърди` / `Дойде` / `Приключи` / `Не дойде`), the `tel:` call, `⋯` navigation, and **an add-on whose duration delta is zero** (Booksy's price-only add-on — it changes no geometry) | the frame's handles **and the new body-drag**, `Начало` and `Времетраене`, every service and every override on its own pushed page, clients, `Ден`, the staff note, arrangement, chair move, an applied promo                                                                                                                                            |
| Draft     | none                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `draftStartMinute` / `draftDurationMinutes` / `draftSeats`, dirty × stale. ⚠ **2026-08-26: `draftEndMinute` is no longer a writable signal anywhere** — it is a `computed()` off start + duration (Ruling B), which is what makes the whole class of start-moved-but-end-didn't-follow bugs _unrepresentable_ rather than validated                      |
| Writes    | on tap                                                                                                                                                                                               | on `Запази`, once. **A pushed page is not a commit boundary** — `‹` returns, it does not save                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Recovery  | **Undo**, 5–8s, `role="status"`, `Върни` — a real inverse write through the same callable                                                                                                            | **Cancel** — the dismiss guard, plus an 8s `Върни` after the commit                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Precedent | Fresha's status change, verbatim: _"Status changes take effect immediately"_                                                                                                                         | Fresha's `Apply` → `Save` — **cited for the draft, not for the two stages: Ruling C rejects a second commit on a child page outright**; Mangomint's notify toggle; and `decideBooking`'s `checkPlacement` ([decide-booking.ts:416](../../apps/functions/src/use-cases/decide-booking.ts:416)), which re-decides placement server-side and **can refuse** |

**Regime B is not negotiable for anything geometric.** `StaffDayStore` already rules it — _"no optimistic local mutation, because the server can refuse … and a lane that lied for a second teaches staff to distrust it"_ ([staff-day.store.ts:266](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:266)) — and a time change is the one edit that will one day fire an SMS, which cannot be un-sent. An always-live surface has no moment; the commit button _is_ the moment.

### What peek and compose now mean

> **Ruling: `peek` and `compose` are HEIGHTS, not capabilities. The words "edit mode" and "read mode" may not appear in this document, in the code, or in a commit message about this surface.**

```
        ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │  TIER 0 · THE DAY GRID — already ships                   │
        └────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
                                 ▼
        ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │  ЛИСТЪТ, СГЪНАТ     ui-modal-sheet [fitted]=true         │
        │  data-tier="peek"   ·  A HEIGHT. Every control is live.  │
        │  the pinned strip · ☎ · status verbs · ⋯ · running late  │
        │  ~80% of openings finish here — because the acts that    │
        │  finish here are Regime A, not because the rest is       │
        │  locked                                                  │
        └────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
           touching ANYTHING in Regime B un-fits the sheet.
           No promotion gesture is required and none is offered.
        ┌────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────┐
        │  ЛИСТЪТ, РАЗГЪНАТ   same component, [fitted]=false       │
        │  data-tier="compose" · draft · dirty · stale · guard     │
        │  Ден (the calendar expands in place) → the frame →       │
        │  Начало + Времетраене  (§3.5 — date, picture, clock)     │
        │  услуги · клиенти · пари · бележки  (rows, no titles)    │
        └────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
           tap a service row · a client row · Промоция · a ⋯ item
        ┌────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────┐
        │  PUSHED PAGES   ui-sheet-nav · INSIDE this sheet         │
        │  DEPTH IS EXACTLY ONE, and that is a law.                │
        │  service editor · add service · client · add client ·    │
        │  apply a promo · browse all promos (off ⋯, read-only)    │
        │  ⚠ NOT sheets. One scrim, one focus trap, one Запази.    │
        │    ‹ pops. It never commits and it never dismisses.      │
        └────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
              the three things that are genuinely separate
        ┌────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────┐
        │  NESTED SHEETS / MENUS  cancel sheet (ships) ·           │
        │  chair-move verdict menu · convert-to-block ·            │
        │  ⋯ → Премести на друг ден                                │
        │  ⚠ the `Ден` DATE PICKER is DEAD (Ruling A — the         │
        │    calendar expands inline, in this scroll view); the    │
        │    service picker, the leg sheet, the people picker      │
        │    and the inline token editor are DEAD — §3.6           │
        └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**The two lower boxes are not the same thing and the diagram spends four lines saying so.** A pushed page shares this sheet's scrim, its focus trap, its `aria-modal` and its single commit; a nested sheet is a second modal on top of a modal, which the HIG forbids in one line — _"Display only one sheet at a time."_ The **four** survivors below are the four that genuinely are separate tasks: cancelling is its own decision with its own reason, moving chairs is a verdict menu, converting to blocked time destroys the appointment, and `⋯ → Премести на друг ден` re-decides placement in **another day's lane** and is committed there. That last one is the answer to the challenge this diagram used to pose — _if a fourth ever wants to be a nested sheet, it has to answer why it is not the same task_ — and it answers cleanly: `Ден` changes **this** draft's date and expands inline; a cross-day move is a different task on a different object (§3.3.9). Everything else that used to open a sheet now travels inside this one and comes back.

**Fields never _become_ editable; they always were. The sheet just gets taller.** This is §3.2's original ruling — _"there is no edit mode. The ladder is always live; the sheet is clean or dirty, nothing else"_ — and the research **confirms** it rather than overturning it. No reversal is owed here. Only §3.4.9 and §4.4 need one.

### Why `ui-modal-sheet` and not `ui-detent-sheet`

Verified, and decisive:

1. `ui-detent-sheet`'s own class doc: _"Because it is non-modal, everything behind it stays interactive and focusable… It is therefore NOT for anything that needs an answer before the user continues."_ The full height holds a dirty draft, a Save button and an unsaved-changes guard. **That is definitionally something that needs an answer first.**
2. Adopting it silently discards `aria-modal`, the focus trap, body scroll lock, and the focus-restore contract `closeVisitSheet()` → `restoreFocusToRow(id)` already relies on (WCAG 3.2.2) — [staff-dashboard.ts:761](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.ts:761) and [staff-dashboard.ts:2373](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.ts:2373).
3. `UI_DETENT_FRACTION.small` is **0.2** ([detent-sheet.ts:31](../../libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/detent-sheet/detent-sheet.ts:31)) = 162px on a 375×812 phone. The fitted height needs ~300px. It does not fit the detent it would be assigned.
4. Its drag binds to the whole content and does not bail on controls, creating exactly the nested-gesture problem the modal sheet does not have.

**Promotion is a signal flip plus `scrollToTop()` — which `ui-modal-sheet` already exposes — not a detent drag.** If a genuine detent gesture is ever wanted, it belongs as detents on the _modal_ `ui-sheet` — a DS change with a clear owner — not as a reuse of the non-modal primitive.

### Where the "no safe place to read" objection is answered without a mode

The fitted sheet's top region — the **pinned summary strip** (client · time range · minutes · status badge · arrival stamp) and the client's note as a `<blockquote>` — **contains no interactive control at all.** That _is_ the read surface. It costs zero taps, it is the first thing on screen, and it is made of **text, not disabled fields** — which is precisely Adrian Roselli's recommended alternative to a read-only control, whose verdict on the alternative is _"probably avoid them"_: TalkBack announces read-only fields as _"disabled"_, some SR/browser pairs announce nothing, and there is no default styling, so _"it's still unclear why they cannot edit the field."_

⚠ **Amended 2026-08-26 (comment 4) — and the read surface got _better_, not worse.** It used to lead with an `h2 uiSheetLargeTitle`, which **scrolls away by design**: the moment a barber reached the services, the safe place to read was gone. The summary strip is `position: sticky` chrome ([modal-sheet.css:63-64](../../libs/ui/controls/src/lib/modal-sheet/modal-sheet.css:63)), so the same four facts are still on screen at row 40 of a dirty draft. **A read surface that survives scrolling is a stronger answer to "no safe place to read" than one that did not.** See R1.

### The nine safeguards, named

1. **Undo, not confirm, for Regime A.** 5–8s toast, `Върни`, in the existing `role="status"` region.
2. **One write per commit.** Regime B accumulates into the draft; exactly one payload leaves the device.
3. **Morphing commit with the reason in the label.** `Дойде` (clean) → `Запази` (dirty) → `Запази въпреки застъпването` (overlapping) → `Избери услуга` (invalid) → a sentence and no control at all (offline). R22, unchanged.
4. **Dismiss guard** on ✕ / backdrop / `Esc` / header drag-down when dirty. Already specified; all four arrive through one `(dismissed)` output ([modal-sheet.html:18](../../libs/ui/controls/src/lib/modal-sheet/modal-sheet.html:18)).
5. **Optimistic concurrency** — `expectedVersion` on the wire; the stale-under-dirty state already has its copy.
6. **Gesture disambiguation for the body-drag** — hold-then-move with **zero movement tolerance** (§3.4.5). `pointercancel` reverts and announces.
7. **The notify switch sits immediately above the commit**, defaulting on **only when the time changed**. Regime A never notifies.
8. **Money is role-gated on the service's own page**, one push away — amended 2026-08-26 from _"inside the token editor"_. The barber's always-live surface carries no price control at all, so the highest-consequence field is never under the thumb; after Ruling C it is not even on the same screen. The control is **absent for a `barber`, never disabled** — a disabled row is a promise.
9. **A 44×44 hit floor that density cannot shrink.** The fat-thumb objection is answered with **geometry, not with a mode** — `--control-size-regular` is 40.5px at `data-density="compact"` ([tokens.css:75](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:75)), so every target takes `max(44px, …)`.

### Tier contract, re-cut

The ✕ column no longer means _"not permitted here"_. It means **"not drawn at this height"**.

⚠ **Re-cut again 2026-08-26 (second pass).** The last column was `Nested` and is now **`Deeper`**, which is **a pushed page inside this sheet** unless the cell says otherwise. Only three cells still mean a genuinely separate surface, and each one says so.

| Capability                                                                | Regime |               Fitted               |                                              Full                                               |                                Deeper                                |
