```
║  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  ║
║  │ Начало                          ( 11:00 )          │  ║  44 · live and typeable
║  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  ║
║  │ Времетраене          — · избери услуга        ⌄    │  ║  44 · em dash, never
║  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  ║  a fabricated 0 мин
```

_Gloss: `Избери услуга, за да се появи блокът.` pick a service and the block will appear · `избери услуга` pick a service · `сега` now._

⚠ **Re-cut 2026-08-26 (comments 5, 8, 9, 11).** This wireframe used to draw a `Кога` disclosure over an `От` / `До` / `Времетраене` triple. **`От`/`До` is deleted from the appointment sheet** (Ruling B): the end time is derived and stored nowhere, so a `До` cell with an em dash in it was a placeholder for a value that does not exist even when the services are chosen. The `Кога` row and the region-wide disclosure are deleted with it (comments 5 + 11). The state is unchanged; only every row it was drawn on is.

**Ruling: with no services the frame draws the day and a single start mark, never a block.** A zero-minute block is a hairline the thumb cannot grab and a lie about a duration nobody has chosen; a default block (_"assume 30 minutes"_) is worse, because it silently authors the answer to the question the sheet is asking.

What survives: the chair's real occupancy, the roster edges, the now line, and a draggable **start mark** — a full-width leader with the time on it, at the same 44px absolute hit floor as a handle. Dragging it sets the start, which is genuinely useful before a service is chosen: a barber putting a walk-in _"after Petar"_ knows **when** long before he knows **what**.

**The two typed rows are both present and they behave differently, which is the whole point of Ruling B.**

| Row           | In this state                                                                                                                   | Why                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Ден`         | **prefilled to today** and fully live — a tinted pill with its calendar one tap away                                            | the day is knowable before anything else is, and it is the one fact a new draft can honestly assume                                                                                  |
| `Начало`      | **live and typeable**, prefilled to the next 5-minute step. It is the one edge that exists                                      | it is _the_ authored instant (Ruling B). The start mark on the frame is its twin, and dragging one re-renders the other                                                              |
| `Времетраене` | reads `— · избери услуга` — **an em dash, never `0 мин`** — and its menu holds only the shop's two or three most-booked lengths | the ladder is built around the catalogue span _S_ (§3.5), and there is no _S_ yet. There is no checkmarked row and no `сума на услугите` caption, because there is no sum to caption |

**And there is no `До` anywhere on this surface to carry a third em dash.** That is the state's smallest and best consequence: the old wireframe had two blanks to explain, this one has one, and the one it has is a value the barber is about to author rather than a number the system was going to compute for him.

The commit control reads `Избери услуга` and is disabled — **the disabled reason lives in the label**, per R8. The moment the first service lands, the mark becomes a block anchored at the mark's time and growing downward, and `Времетраене` fills itself with the catalogue sum.

The handles are **absent**, not disabled — the frame is a picture right now, and a picture with grab points on it is a lie about what a drag will do. The footnote dates the cache rather than claiming it is current, because a persistent cache's whole hazard is that stale data looks exactly like fresh data. Same rule everywhere else in the sheet: **offline removes controls and dates the data; it never greys a control and never queues a write.**

⚠ **What offline removes, sheet-wide, named once because §3.8 and §3.6.5 both point here for it (2026-08-26).** **Removed, not disabled:** the dock's commit control — replaced by `Няма връзка. Часът се вижда, но не може да се запази.`; the frame's handles and body-drag; the add-client page's search field **and** its quick-create row, because creating a client is a write; and the `Промоция` row's push, which reads `Няма връзка` and does not travel (§3.8). **Fully live:** the `Ден` pill and its calendar, `Начало`, `Времетраене`, every service and client row, and **the whole service page** — all of them edit a draft, and a draft needs no network. The add-service search page serves the cached catalogue and says so (`Няма връзка — показваме запаметения каталог.`); **"no results" is never rendered offline**, because those are the two answers a barber must never be left to tell apart. **The refusal happens once, at the commit slot, and the draft is never queued.** `data-locked="offline"` is a _reason_ rendered as one footnote, never a tier (§3.2).

**Five surfaces are DELETED, 2026-08-26 — the service picker, the leg sheet, the people picker, the nested date picker and the inline token editor.**

⚠ **Re-cut the same day.** This block used to name **three** deletions and hand their contents to _"the field's suggestion grid"_ and _"the token's inline editor"_. **Two of those three destinations have since been deleted as well** (Ruling C), and two more surfaces joined the list: the `Ден` row's **nested date picker** (Ruling A) and the **inline token editor** that was briefly going to replace the leg sheet. What was three costumes for one mistake is now five.

> **Ruling: what used to open a sheet now travels inside this one.** A picked service, an amended leg and a chosen client are all **subviews of the appointment already on screen**, and a subview gets a **page in this sheet's own navigation stack** — one scrim, one focus trap, one dirty draft, one `Запази`, `‹` to come back, **depth exactly one** (§3.6.3). Not a second modal, not a popover, not a panel under the row.
>
> **And the date does not travel at all: it expands where it stands.** That is not an exception to the ruling, it is the other half of it — **a value with a spatial editor of its own expands in place; a row that owns several values pushes a page** (§3.6.1). The calendar is one value's picture and it is a _sibling segment of the `Ден` row's own group_; a service is three values plus a destructive verb, and it travels.

**Not three columns on a 375px screen.** One line per barber, in words. Where `termsForBarber` ([availability.ts:41](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/availability.ts:41)) changes the duration, the row says so before you commit — which turns the model's honesty into the feature instead of the bug.

⚠ **PROMOTED 2026-08-26 (comments 2 + 7).** This menu was a convenience. With the `Стол` row deleted and barbers out of the people field, **it is the sheet's only shop-wide staffing control** (§3.7, R19): a shop-wide reassignment is a _command_ and menus are for commands, while reassigning **one** leg is a _value_ and lives on that leg's pushed page (§3.6.3). It also stays a **menu** rather than becoming a pushed page, and the reason is the one the tier diagram gives: it re-decides `termsForBarber` against **another barber's** roster, which is a different object's availability rather than a subview of this draft.

> ⚠ **The carve-out, stated here because §3.2's tier diagram will otherwise read as a contradiction (2026-08-26).** Ruling A deletes _a_ date picker and this wireframe is _a_ date picker, so a reader arriving from §3.2 needs one sentence to tell them apart. It is not an exception to Ruling A — it is the other half of the same law.
>
> **`Ден` changes _this_ draft's date. `⋯ → Премести на друг ден` is a different task on a different object.** The `Ден` pill re-dates the appointment in front of you: same chair, same lane, same draft, same `Запази` — so its calendar **expands inline, as a sibling segment of its own row's group** (§3.3.0, §3.5 › `Ден`), and a sheet stacked on a sheet to pick one value would be the modal problem with extra layers. A cross-day move **re-decides placement in another day's lane** — roster, lead time, neighbours, `termsForBarber` — against occupancy this store has not loaded, and **it is committed there, not here.**
>
> That is the same test the cancel sheet passes and the same one §3.2 poses to any fourth candidate: _is this a decision about a different object, with its own commit?_ Two yeses, two nested sheets. **R33 is the third witness and it was written before any of this** — cross-day drag is refused for v1 precisely because _"a cross-day move re-decides roster, lead time, conflicts and terms server-side"_, and `Премести на друг ден` is named there as the path that does it honestly.
>
> **The shortest form, for the diagram's margin: a picker that changes a draft expands; a picker that starts a new decision opens.**

**Nested — the day picker (`Премести на друг ден`):**

```
╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
║  ✕                Премести на друг ден                   ║
║   пн  вт  ср  чт  пт  сб  нд                             ║
║   24  25 [26] 27  28  29  30                             ║
║    ▪   ▪▪  ▪▪▪ ▪▪   ·   ▪    —                           ║  ← load, this week
║   31   1   2   3   4   5   6                             ║
║    ·   ·   ·   ·   ·   ·   ·                             ║  ← no dots: unknown
║  Заетостта се вижда само за заредената седмица.          ║  footnote
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

**Ruling: the picker carries an occupancy signal for the days it actually knows, and draws nothing at all for the rest — with a sentence saying which is which.**

`StaffDayStore.visibleDays` is the anchor day in day view and the whole week in week view ([staff-day.store.ts:477-482](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:477)), and the lanes for exactly those days are already subscribed. That is one to seven days of real, live occupancy — free, already in memory, and enough to answer _"is Thursday busy"_, which is the question. Beyond it, answering would mean firing `barbers × days` new listeners from inside a picker; §3.12 does not size that and this design does not ask for it.

Three cells, three meanings: **`▪▪▪` / `▪▪` / `▪`** for load in the loaded week, **`·`** for "not loaded — unknown", **`—`** for closed. Asking the barber to pick blind and then discover the refusal is the failure this ruling exists to prevent; pretending an unloaded day is free would be a worse version of the same failure, and is why `·` is a neutral dot rather than an empty cell. Cells are the consumer's own `button[uiDay]` inside `ui-calendar-grid` `[exists]` — ⚠ **2026-08-26: the same component and the same cell contract Ruling A puts inline in the `Ден` row** (§3.5 › `Ден`), so the two calendars this design ships are **one component at two sizes**, not two implementations, and the occupancy marks are authored once. `ui-calendar-scroller` is not used here either: it leaves this surface entirely with the nested date picker it was going to draw. The dot is a consumer class, not a DS change.


_Gloss: `Нов час` new appointment · `Час / Блокирано` appointment / blocked · `Сега` now · `Добави услуга` add a service · `Добави клиент` add a client._

⚠ **Re-cut 2026-08-26 (comments 4, 5, 8, 9, 11 + Ruling C).** Five things this panel used to draw are now false: a `Кога` summary row carrying `11:00 → 11:30 · 30 мин` with a `⌄`, a `Ден … ›` row opening a **nested** date picker, `ХОРА` and `УСЛУГИ` **eyebrows**, and **two caret lines** where the token fields were. The ladder here is now the sheet's own ladder in the sheet's own order — `Ден` → frame → `Начало`/`Времетраене` → услуги → клиенти — and that is the point: **a creation panel that is not the edit panel is a second sheet to maintain and a second layout to learn.** Only the radiogroup and the dock's label are particular to creating.

**The title follows the kind, and within a kind it is static.** `Нов час` while `Час` is selected, `Блокирано време` while `Блокирано` is (R1). The old `Ново` was the title of a _chooser_; once the radiogroup has an answer the sheet has a task, and a sheet title names the task. **There is no summary strip** — a new draft has nothing to summarise, and `.modal-sheet__accessory:empty { display: none }` collapses it for free ([modal-sheet.css:130-132](../../libs/ui/controls/src/lib/modal-sheet/modal-sheet.css:130)), so the absence costs nothing and asserts nothing.

> **Ruling: `Сега` lives in the `Начало` row's trailing slot, beside the pill — not on a `Кога` row, and not as a fourth chip on `Ден`.** It writes the **start**; `Ден`'s relative chips (`Днес` / `Утре` / `В {{weekday}}`, Ruling A) write the **day**. Putting them in one run would be two different facts in one control, which is the defect comments 2, 4 and 7 each killed somewhere else in this sheet. Two targets in one row is legal for exactly the reason the client row's `☎` is legal (§3.7): both clear 44×44 and their accessible names differ. **`Сега` stays one tap**, because a walk-in is standing in front of you and nine times in ten the answer to _"when"_ is _"now."_

> ⚠ **REVERSED 2026-08-26 (Ruling C): both empty fields are `＋` rows, not caret lines.** This panel used to rule _"both empty token fields are a caret line and a placeholder, not a `⊕` row: a new sheet opens with the keyboard one tap from the first service."_ **The token fields are deleted** (§3.6.1), so there is no caret line left to open with — and **the property that ruling was buying survives at the same price**, because the pushed search page **autofocuses its own field** (§3.6.4). One tap on `＋ Добави услуга` still puts the keyboard under the barber's thumb; it now does so on a page that owns the viewport, instead of in a popup competing with that keyboard for 290pt.

**Two rows to fill in and three that fill themselves** — which is Mangomint's speed claim, restated honestly for this ladder rather than counted off the old one. `Ден` arrives on today; `Начало` on the next 5-minute step; `Времетраене` fills itself the moment the first service lands, and until then reads `— · избери услуга` (above). The two rows the barber actually touches are `＋ Добави услуга` and `＋ Добави клиент`, **and the second is optional** — `Или остави празно — клиент без запазен час.` is the walk-in, and it is an empty state rather than a mode.

**This whole panel is M6 and depends on a create path that does not exist.** `commit-booking.use-case.ts:66` returns `CommitBookingUnauthenticatedError` when `ownerUserId` is falsy, and `decideBooking` requires `UserId.create(deps.ownerUserId)` to succeed — so _"остави празно"_ is not a checkbox, it is a nullable `ownerUserId` threaded through two use cases plus a staff-attributed `createdByUserId` for audit. §3.12 sizes it **M**.

**Creation — `Блокирано`, all-day on:**

```
║  ( Час )   ( ● Блокирано )                               ║
║  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  ║
║  │(av)● Иван                                     ✓    │  ║
║  │(av)● Нико                                          │  ║
║  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  ║
║  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  ║
║  │ Почива цял ден                            [   ● ]  │  ║  ← ALREADY SHIPS
║  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  ║
║  (the От/До fields are GONE, not greyed — Apple's rule)  ║
║  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  ║
║  │ Бележка (само за екипа)                            │  ║
║  │ [                                                ] │  ║
║  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  ║
║  Времето спира да е свободно за записване.               ║
║  Никой не получава известие.                             ║
║  ⚠ В блокираното време остават запазени часове           ║
║  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  ║
║  │ 16:00   Петър Иванов                    Фейд       │  ║
║  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  ║
```

**Every pixel of this already exists**, inline in `staff-dashboard.html` under `sheetId="staff-block-sheet"` ([staff-dashboard.html:1388](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1388)) — the barber list, the all-day switch, the От/До pair, `blockEffect`, `blockCollisionsTitle`, `blockCollisionsNote`, the lot. Absorbing it deletes a sheet.

⚠ **`От`/`До` is CORRECT here, and it stays — 2026-08-26, Ruling B.** A reader arriving from §3.5 will expect the pair to be dead; it is dead **in the appointment sheet only.** An appointment's length is a function of its services, so it is asked for as `Начало` + `Времетраене` and the end is derived (Ruling B). **A block has no catalogue, no services and no derivable length, and it has two edges the barber genuinely holds in his head** — _"I'm out from two to four."_ The rule is not _"duration everywhere"_; it is **ask for the fact the user knows.** `staff.day.blockFrom` / `blockTo` are unchanged, the all-day switch still collapses the pair rather than greying it, and `.staff-sheet__time-field` ends the day with exactly one consumer instead of two (§3.3 R2). **Say this out loud in the ADR, or somebody will "harmonise" the two sheets and break the good one.**

**Two caveats it must carry across.** The note field has nowhere to land: `blockTime` passes `note: ''` and the sanitizer strips it ([staff-day.store.ts:757-760](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:757)). And **a second block on the same day overwrites the first** — the exception id is `` `${barberId}__${day.key()}` `` ([staff-day.store.ts:754](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:754)), one document per barber per day, written with `put`, and `clearBlock(barberId)` clears the barber's _entire day_ ([staff-day.store.ts:786](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:786)). Until `ScheduleException` accumulates ranges, **this sheet offers one block per chair per day and says so** rather than silently eating the first one.

**Nested — convert a visit to blocked time:**

```
╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
║  Превърни в блокирано време                              ║
║                                                          ║
║  Часът на Мартин Илиев (10:35 – 11:00) се отменя, а      ║
║  времето става блокирано. Мартин не получава известие.    ║
║                                                          ║
║  Причина: ( Бръснарят отсъства ) ( Салонът е затворен )   ║
║  ☐ Блокирай целия ден, не само този час                  ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║        ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓ Отмени и блокирай ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓ (dest) ║
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

Two effects, both named, reusing `OFFERED_CANCELLATION_REASONS` `[exists]` ([seat-outcome.ts:41](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/seat-outcome.ts:41)) and `blockTime` `[exists]` ([staff-day.store.ts:738](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:738)). **A toggle would have lied about this.** Note that the whole-day option lands on the same one-document-per-day constraint above: ticking it replaces every partial block that chair already had for the day, and the sheet warns before it does.

**Excluded, deliberately: adding a seat to a live appointment.**

A barber will try this in his first hour — _"add my colleague's client to this same 10:00 slot."_ Splitting a seat out is designed (§3.9 #10); merging two appointments is excluded (§4.4); **growing an existing party is excluded here, explicitly, and the UI must not imply otherwise.**

Why: the staff-edit payload replaces all seats, and a _new_ seat is not an edit of an existing one — it needs a subject (`SeatSubject.account` or `anonymous`), its own terms snapshot, its own placement decision against the chair, and a self-seat invariant that currently never fires for anonymous seats. That is the create path, wearing an edit path's clothes. Shipping it as `⊕ Нов клиент „{{query}}“` on a pushed add-client page would put the whole M6 create surface behind one tap the barber thinks is free.

**What the sheet does instead: on a committed appointment the clients group has no `＋ Добави клиент` row.** It renders the people who are coming, and stops.

⚠ **Re-cut 2026-08-26 (Ruling C).** This exclusion used to argue from the token field — _"the people field's **caret line** is **absent**… there is no `⊕` to remove, because there is no `⊕`; a token field with no caret line is a list, and a list is exactly the honest thing to show."_ **The field is gone, the exclusion is not**, so it is restated on the carrier that replaced it: **a group whose last row is not `＋ Добави клиент` is a list of the people who are coming, and a list is exactly the honest thing to show.** The mechanic is the one §3.2's tier table uses for every settled state and the one R0 already points here for (§3.3 R0, amended the same day): **there is no disabled `＋` and no page to refuse, because the row that would push it is not rendered.** An absent row is honest; a disabled row is a promise.

The `⋯` menu offers `Дублирай`, which creates a second appointment in the same window and is the honest shape of what the barber is asking for. When M6's create path lands, growing a party becomes a real option and gets its own ruling; until then the affordance does not exist, because **a row that accepts a name nothing can commit is the disabled promise this whole document is built to avoid.**

## 3.4 THE FRAME — the full interaction specification

### 3.4.1 What it is, structurally

**Not a new component. A second mode on `staff-time-grid`.** The design doc's _"Promote when a second surface asks"_ is satisfied by this surface asking — but it stays inside the feature library, because both consumers live there. Promote to `libs/ui` when a **different library** asks.

Six additions to [`staff-time-grid.ts`](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts). **All six are new.** The component ships **seven** inputs today — `columns`, `rosterStartMinute`, `nowMinute`, `zoneLabel`, `allDay`, `allDayLabel`, `allDayAlways` ([staff-time-grid.ts:194-246](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:194)) — and none of these is among them:

```ts
uiPlacement       = input<'slots' | 'proportional'>('slots');   // NEW
uiWindow          = input<{ startMinute: number; endMinute: number } | null>(null); // NEW
uiViewport        = input<'page' | 'framed'>('page');           // NEW
uiSnapMinutes     = input(15);                                  // NEW
uiEditableEventId = input<string | null>(null);                 // NEW
→ eventDraft      = output<{ id; startMinute; endMinute;
                            via: 'move'|'resize-start'|'resize-end' }>(); // NEW
```

**`uiPlacement` is the whole compatibility story, and it must default to `'slots'`.** Today ([staff-time-grid.ts:534-543](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:534)):

```ts
const startSlot = Math.floor(
  (event.startMinute - originMinute) / MINUTES_PER_SLOT,
);
const endSlot = Math.ceil((event.endMinute - originMinute) / MINUTES_PER_SLOT);
row: `${startSlot + 1} / ${Math.max(startSlot + 2, endSlot + 1)}`;
```

`MINUTES_PER_SLOT` is 15 ([staff-time-grid.ts:136](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:136)). This **rounds outward** — a 09:05 start draws at 09:00 on the live page grid — and makes a 5-minute quantum unrepresentable without 288 tracks per day. The fix is the mechanism the now-line already uses ([staff-time-grid.css:686](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.css:686), `inset-block-start: calc(var(--staff-now-fraction, 0) * 100%)`):

```css
/* NEW rule, NEW custom properties */
.staff-grid__event[data-placement='proportional'] {
  position: absolute;
  inset-block-start: calc(var(--staff-event-top) * 100%);
  block-size: max(
    calc(var(--staff-event-height) * 100%),
    var(--staff-event-min-height)
  );
}
```

The column keeps its grid tracks purely for the hour rules; `uiSnapMinutes` governs only the ruling lines and the snap hint.

⚠ **Do not couple the page-grid migration into the editor's PR.** Proportional placement touches lane packing (`--staff-event-lanes` arithmetic, [staff-time-grid.css:358](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.css:358)), `closedRuns` ([staff-time-grid.ts:444](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:444)), the hour-rule gradient pitch, the now-line, sticky column heads, and `revealWorkingDay`'s scroll math ([staff-time-grid.ts:399](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:399)) — on the surface four people use all day. Add the mode, opt the frame into it, and migrate the page grid **in its own PR** with before/after screenshots of the day, 3-day and week views at all three density settings.

`uiViewport="framed"` dispatches the other three blockers: drop `block-size: calc(100svh - …)` ([staff-time-grid.css:34](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.css:34)), drop `padding-block-end: var(--staff-grid-footer)` ([staff-time-grid.css:44](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.css:44)), keep `overflow: auto` (sticky chrome resolving against the frame is correct), and skip `revealWorkingDay()` — it keys on `columnSignature` ([staff-time-grid.ts:385](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:385)) and would fight a window that changes as you drag.

### 3.4.2 Geometry

**Fixed scale, scrolling window. Not an adaptive scale.** An adaptive scale would make the 5-minute step change size between a 30-minute cut and a 90-minute colour, and muscle memory dies.

| Property           | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Why                                                                                                            |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Scale**          | `--staff-frame-minute: calc(var(--sys-space-unit) * 0.6)` — **2.21 / 2.4 / 2.59 px/min**                                                                                                                                                                                                               | 5 min = **11.0 / 12 / 13.0px**, a felt and aimable step                                                        |
| **Frame height**   | `--staff-frame-height: calc(var(--sys-space-unit) * 60)` — **221 / 240 / 259px**                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | **100 minutes visible at every density** (see below). ~27–32% of a 375×812 viewport, leaving the ladder alive  |
| **Content extent** | event ±120 min, widened to cover `rosterStart − 30 … rosterEnd + 30`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | an hour of room in each direction without hunting                                                              |
| **Scrolls**        | yes, vertically, clamped **hard** at the extent bounds                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | a 90-min service plus shoulders exceeds 100 minutes immediately                                                |
| **On open**        | one-shot scroll placing the block's **start one quarter down the frame**, keyed on `appointmentId` via `afterNextRender`                                                                                                                                                                               | the exact heuristic `revealWorkingDay()` already uses                                                          |
| **Clipped edge**   | `calc(var(--sys-space-unit) * 6)` = **22.1 / 24 / 25.9px** gradient from `--sys-color-surface` + a **tappable** `⌃`/`⌄` jump control                                                                                                                                                                   | _"the block continues above/below"_ — the difference between usable and not. See "What the window cannot hold" |
| **Gutter**         | `--staff-gutter` narrowed to `calc(var(--sys-space-unit) * 12)` — **44.2 / 48 / 51.8px**, down from the page grid's `* 14` ([staff-time-grid.css:20](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.css:20)); labels every **30 min**, translated `-0.5em` to sit _on_ the line | 30 min = 66.2 / 72 / 77.8px at frame scale                                                                     |
| **Columns**        | **one. This chair. Always.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | see the ruling below                                                                                           |
| **Owner header**   | `.staff-frame__owner` **[new]** — one line ABOVE the scrolling axis, inside the frame's ring, **outside `--staff-frame-height`**                                                                                                                                                                       | 2026-08-26: the frame draws one chair, so the chair is named on the picture instead of in a row. §3.4.3        |

#### Density is not a rounding error, and the window is density-invariant

`--sys-space-unit: calc(0.25rem * var(--sys-density))` ([tokens.css:50-51](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:50)), and `[data-density]` sets **0.92** and **1.08** ([tokens.css:231-235](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:231)). Every figure derived from the unit therefore has three values, and the compact tier is the one that breaks things:

|                                 | compact 0.92               | regular 1.0        | spacious 1.08                          |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| `--sys-space-unit`              | 3.68px                     | 4px                | 4.32px                                 |
| Frame scale (`× 0.6`)           | **2.21 px/min**            | 2.4                | **2.59**                               |
| 5 / 15 / 30 / 60 min            | 11.0 / 33.1 / 66.2 / 132.5 | 12 / 36 / 72 / 144 | 13.0 / 38.9 / 77.8 / 155.5             |
| Frame height (`× 60`)           | **221px**                  | 240                | **259**                                |
| **Window**                      | **100 min**                | **100 min**        | **100 min**                            |
| Gutter (`× 12`)                 | 44.2                       | 48                 | 51.8                                   |
| Handle capsule (`× 10` / `× 5`) | 36.8 × 18.4                | 40 × 20            | 43.2 × 21.6                            |
| Auto-scroll dead zone (18%)     | 39.8px                     | 43.2               | 46.7 — **18 minutes at every density** |

**Ruling: the window is 100 minutes at every density, and that is not luck — it is the reason both the scale and the height are stated in the same unit.** `(unit × 60) / (unit × 0.6) = 100`, and the unit cancels. Density changes how big 100 minutes _is_; it never changes _how much time you can see_. Any future frame measurement that is not expressible as a multiple of `--sys-space-unit` breaks this and is rejected.

⚠ **The owner header is chrome, not axis, and the invariant is why.** `--staff-frame-height` measures the **scrolling window** and nothing else. `.staff-frame__owner` adds its own ~44px above it, so the frame's _outer_ box grows by one line while the _time_ it shows does not move. Had the header been subtracted from the window instead, `(unit × 60 − 44) / (unit × 0.6)` would yield **80 / 82 / 83 minutes** — three different windows at three densities, which is exactly the thing this ruling exists to forbid. **Anything added to the frame that is not the time axis is added outside the height token.**

**Ruling: touch targets are stated in fixed px, never in space units.** 44pt is a platform floor, not a taste preference; a user who asks for a denser layout is asking for less whitespace, not for a smaller thumb. Everything decorative scales with density. Everything a finger lands on does not. §3.4.4 applies this.

#### The page grid's own scale token

`--staff-minute-height` is **new (proposed)** — it does not exist in the repo. What exists today is [staff-time-grid.css:19](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.css:19):

```css
--staff-slot-height: calc(
  var(--sys-space-unit) * 7
); /* 25.8 / 28 / 30.2px per 15 min */
```

— **1.72 / 1.87 / 2.02 px/min**. The migration is a pure re-derivation and must be byte-for-byte:

```css
/* NEW */
--staff-minute-height: calc(var(--sys-space-unit) * 7 / 15);
/* CHANGED */
--staff-slot-height: calc(var(--staff-minute-height) * 15);
```

The slot resolves to `unit × 7` exactly as before, at all three densities; nothing on the page moves. The derivation runs minute → slot, never the reverse. _(Dividing by `var(--sys-space-unit)` inside `calc()` is invalid CSS — `calc()` permits division only by a plain number — and the whole declaration would fail to parse silently. Dividing by the literal `15` above is legal.)_

#### One column. The chair-column idea is dead.

**Ruling: the frame draws exactly one column — the chair the sheet was opened at — in every case, including a genuinely parallel party.** 375px minus a 44–52px gutter leaves 323–331px; three columns is **108–110px each**, which cannot carry a name and a time. That is a chart, not a control, and a control is what this is. Any earlier statement that the frame shows "one column per barber, capped at three" is **withdrawn**.

What replaces it, for a party whose second seat sits in another chair at the same time:

- The other leg is drawn **in this column**, in the other barber's tone at 7%, with a 1px separator outline, labelled `Иван · 10:35` — the same treatment as any neighbour, and explicitly `aria-hidden`.
- It carries **no handles.** The frame edits the seat it was opened at. Editing the sibling seat is a separate open, reached by tapping the sibling's row in the party list above the frame.
- The handles bound against **the whole party's envelope** — `min(start)`…`max(end)` across every seat (§3.3.9 ruling 2), _not_ this seat's range alone. The staff-edit payload replaces all seats, so a drag that pushes one leg past another leg's edge would write an arrangement the domain refuses. The frame draws both legs; the sheet's party row states any disagreement in words; the readout stays this seat's own interval, because that is what is under the finger.
- `frameSummary()` names the sibling explicitly, so the fact never depends on a 7% tint being seen.

#### What the window cannot hold

Two cases exceed 100 minutes, and both need a ruling or the drag handle is off-screen at open.

**(a) An event longer than the window** — a three-service sequential party, a two-hour colour, a 90-minute job with shoulders.

**Ruling: scroll. Never zoom.** The fixed scale is the whole point; an event that resizes the ruler destroys the muscle memory the fixed scale bought. Four supports make scrolling survivable:

1. **The clipped-edge caret becomes a real control.** `⌃ 09:00` / `⌄ 12:30` — a `<button>` in the gradient, labelled with the time it will reveal, that scrolls the opposite edge into view in one tap. It is **new**, it is interactive, and it therefore carries the ungated `:active` mirror of §3.4.4.
2. **On open the frame anchors to the START edge**, not to the block's centre, whenever the block exceeds the window. The start handle is always reachable without a scroll; the end handle is one tap away.
3. **Edge auto-scroll pins the dragged edge**, so once a drag begins the handle under the finger is on screen by construction.
4. **`frameSummary()` states both boundaries unconditionally**, so the screen-reader path never depends on scroll position.

**Ruling: above 180 minutes the frame opens anchored to the START edge and the body-drag is suppressed.** The handles stay live and the jump carets do the travel. A move whose destination is two windows away cannot be aimed, and offering the gesture anyway would be a control that only works by accident. `Премести на друг ден` and the typed `Начало` — which **holds the duration and slides the whole block** (§3.5, Ruling B, 2026-08-26) — remain the paths.

⚠ **The old ruling — _"above three hours the frame is not the editor; the sheet opens on the typed clock instead"_ — is withdrawn, 2026-08-26.** It had no content left once ask #3 put the typed fields permanently on screen beside the frame (§3.5): there is no editor to open _instead_, because both are already there, and there is no stored `timeEditor` preference for a long appointment to override. Its useful half — _at three hours the two handles are roughly two windows apart and every edit becomes a scroll-hunt_ — survives as the ruling above.

**(b) A neighbour further away than the window shows.** The conflict readout and the buffer footnote both name a neighbour the frame may not be drawing.

**Ruling: nothing may be named that the frame cannot reach, and nothing named may rely on being seen.**

- **Overlap is self-limiting.** You cannot overlap a block your own edge is not touching, so an overlapping neighbour is at most a few minutes outside the window. When the readout turns destructive and the named neighbour is not drawn, the frame **auto-scrolls to include it** in the same frame the readout changes.
- **Buffer advice is not.** A cleanup shoulder can foul a setup shoulder 25+ minutes away, off-screen. The footnote therefore carries the **name and the time in text** — `Няма време за подготовка преди Петър 11:30.` _(No setup time before Petar 11:30.)_ — never a bare `Няма време за подготовка.` pointing at a drawing that is not there. **This is the one case that survives comment 6's deletion of the frame footnote, and this bullet is exactly why:** it is a verdict about something the frame cannot reach, not the frame narrated. §3.4.3, "The frame carries no standing caption."
- **`Виж` scrolls, it does not assume.** Every conflict row's `Виж` scrolls the frame to the offender and flashes its outline once. If the offender is outside the **extent** (>120 min away) the row is not drawn at all, because a block that far away cannot conflict.

### 3.4.3 What is drawn

| Layer                  | z   | Treatment                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Interactive                                     |
| ---------------------- | --- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Column ground          | —   | `--sys-color-background`                                                                                                                                                                                                               | —                                               |
| **Outside the roster** | 0   | `--sys-color-surface-secondary`, opaque, `pointer-events: none` — identical to `.staff-grid__closed` ([staff-time-grid.css:346-351](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.css:346))                    | no                                              |
| Roster edge            | 0   | one 1px `--sys-color-separator` rule, labelled once in the gutter: `09:00 отваря`                                                                                                                                                      | no                                              |
| Hour / 30-min rules    | 1   | `repeating-linear-gradient` on `::after`, `pointer-events: none` — **elements were tried and auto-placement walked them down the column; do not retry**                                                                                | no                                              |
| **5-minute ticks**     | 1   | **hidden at rest; faded in only under `[data-dragging]`** at 25% separator strength every 11.0 / 12 / 13.0px                                                                                                                           | no                                              |
| Blocks / time-off      | 2   | neutral 45° hatch at 8px pitch, labelled `Блокирано`                                                                                                                                                                                   | no                                              |
| **Neighbours**         | 2   | barber tone at **7%** (half the page grid's measured 15%, [staff-time-grid.css:412-416](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.css:412)), 1px separator outline, labelled `Иван · 09:30`, `aria-hidden` | no                                              |
| **Buffer shoulders**   | 2   | `repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, tone 10%, transparent)` 4px/4px, above and below the sold slot, **labelled at ≥10 minutes** (22.1 / 24 / 25.9px)                                                                                     | **no — derived from `seat.terms`**              |
| **The edited block**   | 3   | tone at 15% (`--staff-event-tint`, reused verbatim); `[data-dirty]` swaps the tint to `--sys-color-accent` at 15%; `[data-moving]` lifts it — `scale(1.02)` + `--sys-elevation-overlay`, origin ghost at 7%                            | **yes — it drags to move (§3.4.5, branch two)** |
| Leg seams              | 3   | 1px `--sys-color-separator` inside a multi-leg block, **each leg labelled at ≥15 minutes** (33.1 / 36 / 38.9px)                                                                                                                        | no                                              |
| **Midnight rule**      | 3   | 1px `--sys-color-separator`, labelled `полунощ` in the gutter; only when the extent crosses 24:00                                                                                                                                      | no                                              |
| Now line               | 4   | `--sys-color-accent` rule + gutter capsule `сега 10:22`, only when the day is today and now falls in the extent                                                                                                                        | no                                              |
| Handles                | 5   | §3.4.4                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | **yes**                                         |
| Jump carets            | 5   | §3.4.2, in the clipped-edge gradient                                                                                                                                                                                                   | **yes**                                         |
| Readout                | 6   | §3.4.6                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | no (`aria-hidden`)                              |

**The thresholds above are stated in minutes, not pixels, deliberately.** A label rule written as "≥36px" is three different rules at three densities and silently drops the leg seam label on a compact phone. Written as "≥15 minutes" it is one rule everywhere, and the px follow.

**Frame tokens:** ground `--sys-color-background`; ring 1px `--sys-color-separator`; radius `--control-radius-regular` ([tokens.css:90](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:90)); overflow clipped. Handle fill `--sys-color-accent` ([theme-light.css:24](../../libs/ui/tokens/theme-light.css:24)), glyph `--sys-color-on-accent`, radius `--control-radius-capsule` ([tokens.css:101](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:101)) — _the accent alone means "look here"_, and a drag handle is exactly that. Readout `--sys-color-surface-elevated` + `--sys-elevation-overlay` ([tokens.css:195](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:195)), swapping to `--sys-color-warning` outside the roster and `--sys-color-destructive` on overlap. Motion `--sys-motion-duration-instant` ([tokens.css:203](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:203)) + `--sys-motion-ease-emphasized` ([tokens.css:215](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:215)) for non-drag transitions; **`[data-dragging] { transition: none }`** — _"a drag must track the finger 1:1."_

#### The owner header — the chair, named on the picture, not stated in a row

> **Ruling (owner comments 2 + 7, 2026-08-26): the frame gains a one-line header naming the barber whose column it draws, and that header is the only place this appointment's chair is stated. The `Стол` row is deleted from the ladder and the people field becomes clients only (§3.7).**

The frame already draws exactly one column — _this chair, always_ (§3.4.2). A `Стол` row above it, a barber chip inside the people field and the block's own tone were **three renderings of one fact**, two of which were editable projections of the third. Editing "Иван" in a people field would have had to answer _which of his legs did you mean_, and there is no honest answer. **Labelling a picture is not a source of truth; a `ui-list-row` carrying the same value is.**

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ (av)● Иван                                         │  ← .staff-frame__owner
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤     44px floor, OUTSIDE
│ 09:30 ┊░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ │     --staff-frame-height
│       ┊──────────────────────────── 09:00 отваря ─│
│       ┊▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒ Мартин · до 09:50 ▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒ │  ▒ neighbour 7%
│ 10:00 ┊▚▚▚▚▚▚▚▚ подготовка 5 мин ▚▚▚▚▚▚▚▚▚▚▚▚▚▚ │  ▚ setup shoulder
│       ┊═══════════════ ⌃ ══════════════════════ │  ← START handle
│       ┊████████████████████████████████████████ │  ← the block, it drags
│ 10:30 ┊═══════════════ ⌄ ══════════════════════ │  ← END handle
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  ← and NOTHING under it
```

_`(av)` is `ui-avatar`; `●` is the tone swatch in its corner. Gloss: `Иван` the barber's name; `09:00 отваря` opens at 09:00; `подготовка` setup._

```html
<header class="staff-frame__owner">
  <!-- NEW class -->
  <span class="staff-scope__face">
    <!-- exists -->
    <ui-avatar
      [uiSrc]="chairAvatarSrc()"
      [uiName]="chairName()"
      uiControlSize="small"
    />
    <span
      class="staff-scope__swatch"
      [attr.data-barber-tone]="chairTone()"
      aria-hidden="true"
    ></span>
  </span>
  <span uiText uiFont="subheadline" uiWeight="medium">{{ chairName() }}</span>
</header>
```

| Property                 | Value                                                                                                                                                                                         | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Composition**          | `.staff-scope__face` wrapping `ui-avatar uiControlSize="small"`, with `.staff-scope__swatch[data-barber-tone]` pinned to its corner                                                           | **Not a new idiom — the shipped one.** [staff-dashboard.html:348-358](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:348) composes these three exactly this way for the scope switcher and [staff-dashboard.html:1423-1433](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1423) again for the block sheet; the rules are already written ([staff-dashboard.css:1534-1560](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.css:1534)). `.staff-frame__owner` is a **layout** class — flex row, gap, padding — and adds no tone, no ring, no avatar sizing |
| **Height**               | one line at the 44px floor, above the axis, **outside `--staff-frame-height`**                                                                                                                | §3.4.2's invariant: the window stays 100 minutes at every density because nothing but the axis is measured by the height token                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Interactive**          | **no.** It is a label                                                                                                                                                                         | changing the chair is `⋯ → Смени стола` — a shop-wide command that rewrites every leg's barber at once (§3.7). A tappable header would imply it edits _this frame's_ chair alone, and no such value exists                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Per-leg disagreement** | the header names the column that is **drawn**; when a leg's barber differs, **the service row says so** (§3.6), and the sibling leg is drawn in this column at 7% with its own label (§3.4.2) | the header never summarises the party — that is what made the old `Стол` row a lie on a two-barber visit                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Screen reader**        | `aria-hidden="true"` on the swatch only. The name is plain text, and `frameLabel` / `frameSummary` name the barber anyway (§3.4.10)                                                           | the tone swatch is a second encoding of a name already spoken — the same rule every decorative layer in the table above obeys                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

#### The frame carries no standing caption

> **Ruling (owner comment 6, 2026-08-26): the visible line under the frame is silent by default. It speaks only when it carries a verdict the frame cannot draw, and it is deleted in every other case.**
>
> **Deleted:** the always-on footnote that narrated the roster edge and the neighbours — _"Смяната е 09:00 до 18:00. Преди него Мартин до 09:50."_ The owner is right: it is the picture read aloud to somebody who is looking at the picture. Both facts are already **drawn** — the roster edge as a 1px `--sys-color-separator` rule labelled once in the gutter as `09:00 отваря`, every neighbour as a 7% tone block labelled with its name and its time (both in the table above).
>
> **Survives, unchanged:** `frameSummary()` still says all of it — **SR-only**, through `[uiVisuallyHidden]` (§3.4.10). A full sentence is the right medium precisely where there is no picture. Removing the visible copy costs a sighted barber nothing and costs a screen-reader user nothing, which is how you know the two were never one control.

The line under the frame is therefore a **slot with three tenants**, and each of them states something the drawing cannot:

| Tenant                 | Copy                                                       | Why it is a verdict and not a caption                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Buffer collision**   | `Няма време за подготовка преди Петър 11:30.`              | it names a neighbour that may be **off-screen** — §3.4.2 (b). The frame cannot draw 25 minutes away, so the words carry the whole fact. Secondary ink, no relabel, **advice** |
| **Outside the roster** | `Часът излиза извън смяната — няма да се предлага онлайн.` | a **consequence**, not a position. The hatch says _where_; only the sentence says what it means for online booking. Warning tone, and permitted (§3.4.7)                      |
| **Price decoupling**   | `Промяната на времето не променя цената.`                  | fires **once**, on the first duration edit — it answers a question the frame provokes and cannot answer (§3.5)                                                                |

**Everything else is silence.** No _"this is Иван's schedule"_, no _"the shift is 09:00 to 18:00"_, no restatement of the block's own times: the readout (§3.4.6) carries them during a drag and the two rows beneath the frame carry them at rest (§3.5). A third rendering would be the same defect one row lower — which is the defect comment 6 actually found.

#### The all-day row, and the thing with no edges

A whole-day `time_off` / `sick` / `closed` exception has no start and no end inside the day, so it has nothing to grab. Drawing it as a full-height block would put a 24-hour rectangle under two handles that must refuse every drag — the worst possible affordance.

**Ruling: whole-day facts render in the frame's pinned all-day row, never on the time axis.** The row already exists and needs no new component: `allDay` maps column id → labels ([staff-time-grid.ts:236](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:236)), the markup is [staff-time-grid.html:79-88](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.html:79), and the page already feeds it ([staff-dashboard.ts:1306](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.ts:1306), bound at [staff-dashboard.html:579-581](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:579)). Four consequences:

1. **`uiViewport="framed"` sets `allDayAlways` to `false`.** On the page an always-present empty row is correct — it stops the hours below it jumping as you page between days. In a 221–259px frame the same empty row costs ~10% of the window to say nothing. The frame's row appears only when it has content.
2. **The chip names the kind, in the shop's words:** `Отпуск` (time off) · `Болничен` (sick) · `Затворено` (closed). `pointer-events: none`, no handles, no drag. `closed` is the kind `rosterWindow` already zeroes ([roster-window.ts:61](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/roster-window.ts:61)).
3. **The axis behind it takes the `.staff-grid__closed` treatment end to end**, and the edited block draws **on top of it** (z 2 over z 0) — the same arrangement that already lets a booking overrunning closing time stay visible. A barber who opens an appointment on a day the barber is off must see the appointment, not a grey wall.
4. **The handles stay live.** Dragging inside a whole-day closure is the `Извън смяната` warning path of §3.4.7 — permitted, amber, `outsideWindow: true`. The shop knows something the roster does not; that is the whole reason the warning is a warning and not a refusal.

When the sheet's kind switch flips an appointment to all-day, the frame's part is simply this: the time axis collapses, the handles unmount, and the row gains a chip. The two writes and the one confirmation that produce that state are §3.9's business, not the frame's.

### 3.4.4 The handles

```html
<button
  type="button"
  class="staff-frame__handle"
  data-edge="start"
  data-drag-owner
  role="slider"
  [attr.aria-label]="t('staff.visit.handleStart')"
  [attr.aria-valuemin]="startMin()"
  [attr.aria-valuemax]="startMax()"
  [attr.aria-valuenow]="draftStartMinute()"
  [attr.aria-valuetext]="t('staff.visit.handleValue',
           { time: draftStartLabel(), minutes: draftMinutes() })"
  (pointerdown)="onHandleDown($event, 'start')"
  (keydown)="onHandleKey($event, 'start')"
>
  <ui-icon uiName="frame.handleStart" uiScale="small" aria-hidden="true" />
</button>
```

**It must be a real `<button>`, for two load-bearing reasons.** `role="slider"` on a native button gives free keyboard, free focus ring, free press state. And `UiSheetBehavior.onDragStart` already bails on `closest('button, a')` ([sheet-behavior.ts:207](../../libs/ui/layout/src/lib/sheet/sheet-behavior.ts:207)), so a button handle can never be eaten by the sheet's own gesture — a benefit that costs nothing.

| Property       | Coarse pointer                                                                                                                                                  | Fine pointer                                                                                           |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Visual         | capsule `calc(--sys-space-unit * 10)` × `calc(--sys-space-unit * 5)` — **36.8 × 18.4 / 40 × 20 / 43.2 × 21.6**; `⌃`/`⌄` glyph, centred on the edge              | `× 8` / `× 4` = 29.4 × 14.7 / 32 × 16 / 34.6 × 17.3 at rest, growing to the coarse size on block hover |
| **Hit target** | **44 × 44 fixed px, never density-derived** — see the construction below                                                                                        | **24 × 24 fixed px** (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8), `cursor: ns-resize`                                          |
| `touch-action` | **`none` on the handle only** — never on the frame, or the frame stops scrolling                                                                                | —                                                                                                      |
| Focus          | `:focus-visible`, `--sys-focus-ring-width` 2px at `--sys-focus-ring-offset` 2px ([tokens.css:170-171](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:170)), `--sys-color-ring` | same                                                                                                   |

**The hit target must not be expressed as an inset.** The obvious construction — `::before { inset-block: -12px; inset-inline: -2px }` — reaches 44 × 44 only at density 1. At compact it yields **42.4 × 40.8**, under the floor in both axes, and the failure is invisible in review because the reviewer's browser is at density 1. The correct construction states the floor directly and lets the visual float inside it:

```css
.staff-frame__handle::before {
  /* NEW */
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  inset-block-start: 50%;
  inset-inline-start: 50%;
  translate: -50% -50%;
  min-block-size: 44px; /* fixed. not a space unit. */
  min-inline-size: 44px;
}
```

**Why the hit area straddles the edge.** Wholly inside, it steals taps from the block body; wholly outside, from the neighbour. Straddling is the correct construction — 22px in, 22px out.

**Short blocks.** Two 44px hit areas need 88px, and the minutes that buys depend on density:

|                              | compact 0.92 | regular 1.0 | spacious 1.08 |
| ---------------------------- | ------------ | ----------- | ------------- |
| Both handles full-size above | **40 min**   | 37 min      | 34 min        |

**The rule is a formula, and it is stated in pixels precisely so it is density-proof:**

```
hitHeight = min(44, blockHeight / 2 + 22)     // blockHeight measured, in px
```

Nothing in the implementation may compare against a minutes constant — the threshold must fall out of the measured height, or it is wrong at two densities out of three. At and above the density's threshold both handles are a full 44. At the 10-minute floor (22.1 / 24 / 25.9px) each is **33 / 34 / 35px** tall — under 44 in the block axis, but 44 wide, non-overlapping, and extending outward where there is nothing to steal from. **This is stated honestly in the handle's accessible name and in the docs, and the typed fields beside the frame are the guaranteed path below the threshold — which on a compact phone means below 40 minutes, not below 37.**

**The same 88px buys the body-drag's suppression floor, and deliberately so.** Above the threshold the two hit areas do not overlap and there is block left between them: that leftover _is_ the move region (§3.4.5, branch two). Below it there is nothing between the handles to grab, so the body-drag is simply absent rather than cramped. **One number, one derivation, two features** — do not introduce a second threshold for the move.

#### Press and hover, house rules

Every interactive surface this section introduces is **new**, so every one of them owes the house ruling:

- **`:active` is ungated and mandatory** on the handle, the jump caret, the conflict row's `Виж`, and the block body — which is now always focusable and always draggable, so "wherever it is focusable" no longer narrows anything. `[data-dragging]` and `[data-moving]` are drag states, not press states, and neither discharges this.
- **Hover is `@media (hover: hover)`-gated**, without exception. The fine-pointer growth in the table above lives inside that query; on a phone the handle is simply always at its coarse size.
- A press mirror that only fires after a 44px hit test is not a press mirror — the `::before` above is the hit surface, so `:active` styling targets the handle and the `::before` carries the geometry.

**Icons to register** — **all new registry entries**, all of which must pass [`icon.spec.ts`](../../libs/ui/controls/src/lib/icon/icon.spec.ts)'s check against the pinned `material-symbols` set (the registry has a recorded regression where an unresolvable ligature rendered as its own name in 24px caps): `frame.handleStart` → `keyboard_arrow_up`, `frame.handleEnd` → `keyboard_arrow_down`, `frame.jumpUp` → `expand_less`, `frame.jumpDown` → `expand_more`, `visit.requested` → `favorite`, `visit.late` → `more_time`, `visit.split` → `call_split`, `visit.chair` → `chair`, `note.internal` → `edit_note`, `money.promo` → `sell`.

### 3.4.5 The drag lifecycle — two branches

**Branch one: a handle, which resizes. Branch two: the body, which moves.** They share the snap quantum, the auto-scroller, the readout, the live region and the revert rules, and they differ in exactly three places: how the gesture is claimed, what the delta does to the interval, and what the commit is called. Anything written twice below is written twice because it genuinely differs.

#### What a drag writes — the end is derived, 2026-08-26

> **Ruling (owner comment 8 → §3.5, Ruling B): `endsAt` is DERIVED and never stored, so no gesture on this frame writes an end. The bottom handle writes `Времетраене`. The `От`/`До` pair the drag lifecycle used to feed is deleted from this sheet; it survives only in the block sheet, which has no catalogue and therefore no derivable length.**

The geometry is untouched — two handles, one body, a 5-minute snap, the same clamps and the same auto-scroller. **What changed is the destination of the write**, and it changed for one reason: a barber authors a _length_, not an instant he would otherwise have to compute in his head.

| Gesture                    | Holds    | Changes on screen    | **Writes**                     |
| -------------------------- | -------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Drag the **block body**    | duration | start _and_ end      | `Начало`                       |
| Drag the **bottom** handle | start    | end                  | **`Времетраене`**              |
| Drag the **top** handle    | end      | start _and_ duration | `Начало` **and** `Времетраене` |

The top handle is the only two-value write on this surface, and it is the honest form of _"I'll start ten minutes later but still finish at eleven."_ It is **not** two commands: §3.4.13's discriminated `{ kind: 'resize', edge: 'start' }` already carries exactly this shape and the wire payload is unchanged. What moved is the sheet's signal graph.

```
draftStartMinute      ← writable signal   (block drag · top handle · the Начало row)
draftDurationMinutes  ← writable signal   (bottom handle · top handle · the Времетраене menu)
draftEndMinute        = computed(() => draftStartMinute() + draftDurationMinutes())
```

**`draftEndMinute` is no longer writable anywhere**, and that is the whole benefit. Every clamp in §3.4.5 and §3.4.7 that _reads_ `draftEnd` keeps reading it verbatim — a `computed()` reads identically — while every line that used to _write_ it now writes the duration. "I moved the start and the end didn't follow" becomes unrepresentable rather than tested for. The bottom handle's clamp `[draftStart + 10, extent.end]` is therefore restated in the terms it now writes — `duration ≥ 10` **and** `draftStart + duration ≤ extent.end` — the same two numbers, one source.

**Live during the drag:** the `Времетраене` row's trailing value tracks the handle at every snap and reads in full — `45 мин · до 10:45`. It is the readout's typed twin, and it is the whole payoff of those two rows sitting immediately beneath the frame (comment 9's reorder: `Ден` → frame → `Начало`/`Времетраене`).

##### Where the delta lands when the services do not add up

A drag can ask for a length the catalogue does not sell. **It never rescales the services, and it never silently shortens one.** Let _S_ be the catalogue span of the current arrangement, _D_ the dragged length and _K_ the slack already on the appointment. §3.5's decision table is the law; this is what the barber sees happen **on the frame**:

| Condition                        | The delta lands in                                                       | What the frame does                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **one service, any _D_**         | a per-appointment **duration override on that service**                  | the block redraws to _D_; the service row gains the `по избор` marker (§3.6)                                     |
| **≥2 services, _D > S_**         | **named slack** — a `Допълнително време · 15 мин · 0,00 €` row in Услуги | a leg seam appears at _S_ and the tail beyond it draws as that slack leg, labelled at ≥15 minutes like any other |
| **≥2 services, _S − K ≤ D < S_** | the existing slack, **consumed first**                                   | the slack leg shrinks; at zero its seam disappears                                                               |
| **≥2 services, _D < S − K_**     | **nowhere. The handle clamps at the floor.**                             | destructive readout `най-малко 45 мин — променете услуга`; announced once on release; tapping it pushes Услуги   |
| **_D_ off-grid**                 | snapped to 5 before anything else                                        | the number that appears is the number that saves                                                                 |
| **any _D_**                      | **never the price**                                                      | `Промяната на времето не променя цената.` fires once in the caption slot above                                   |

**The fourth row is the one that gets argued with, and it is a hard clamp rather than a warning.** Below that floor there is no honest place for the delta, because the only remaining move is to shorten a service the gesture never named — which is how a 30-minute cut quietly becomes 22 minutes in the reporting and nobody finds out. **A gesture may not shorten a service it does not name.** So it refuses at the floor and points at the region that can name one: the readout's destructive line is the pointer, and Услуги is the destination (§3.6, Ruling C — a service is a pushed page, not an inline expansion).

⚠ **§3.4.7's 10-minute floor is not repealed — it is now the lower of two.** Both handles clamp at a length of **`max(10, S − K)`**, measured from whichever edge is standing still. On a **single-service** appointment the service term drops out and the floor is simply **10**, because row 1 makes any _D_ ≥ 10 representable as an override on that one service. On a **two-service** appointment with no slack the floor **is _S_** and the handle stops there, with the destructive readout naming the fix.

#### Branch one — a handle

```
pointerdown on handle
 ├─ event.button !== 0 (non-primary mouse)              → return
 ├─ event.preventDefault()          [the handle owns this pointer]
 ├─ event.stopPropagation()         [belt and braces; the sheet already bails]
 ├─ handle.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)
 ├─ CLAIM IMMEDIATELY — no 8px threshold.
 │    The 8px threshold exists to protect a surface that must still accept
 │    taps. A dedicated 44pt handle is unambiguous. (The block BODY is the
 │    other branch and does carry one — 5px on a mouse, 0px on a finger.
 │    See "Branch two" below.)
 ├─ record originMinute, pointerY0, frame.scrollTop, performance.now()
 ├─ frame[data-dragging] → transitions off, 5-minute ticks fade in over 150ms
 ├─ haptic: navigator.vibrate?.(10)             [impact-light, "picked up"]
 └─ readout appears, anchored to the OPPOSITE edge of the block

pointermove   (every event; the browser already coalesces)
 ├─ raw     = originMinute
 │          + (clientY - pointerY0 + (frame.scrollTop - originScrollTop))
 │            / pxPerMinute            ← MEASURED, not a constant: 2.21/2.4/2.59
 ├─ snapped = Math.round(raw / 5) * 5
 ├─ clamp:  start handle → [extent.start,        draftEnd - floor]
 │          end   handle → [draftStart + floor,  extent.end]
 │          floor = max(10, S - K)   ← the SERVICE floor. 10 on a single
 │            service, because an override makes any length representable;
 │            S - K on two or more. See "Where the delta lands" above
 ├─ if (snapped !== lastSnapped):
 │    ├─ write draftStartMinute / draftDurationMinutes  ← SIGNALS, never
 │    │    the store, and NEVER draftEndMinute: it is computed (above).
 │    │    top handle writes BOTH; bottom handle writes the duration alone
 │    ├─ haptic: navigator.vibrate?.(4)           [selection tick]
 │    └─ lastSnapped = snapped
 ├─ recompute validity → readout text + data-tone
 ├─ if newly clamped this frame: haptic 18 ONCE  [notification-warning]
 └─ edge auto-scroll (below)

edge auto-scroll
 ├─ dead zone: top and bottom 18% of the frame — 18 MINUTES at every density
 │    (39.8 / 43.2 / 46.7px), which is why the zone is a percentage
 ├─ velocity ramps 0 → 600 px/s, proportional to depth into the zone
 ├─ driven by requestAnimationFrame, NEVER setInterval
 ├─ block stays pinned under the finger while content moves beneath it
 ├─ stops at the extent bounds — never scrolls into empty space; instead the
 │    extent GROWS by 30 min, up to rosterEnd + 60
 └─ stops the instant the pointer leaves the frame's bounds
      (HIG: "if they continue the drag outside of the container, automatic
       scrolling is no longer necessary")

pointerup
 ├─ releasePointerCapture
 ├─ clear [data-dragging] → ticks fade out, transitions back on
 ├─ haptic: 12 on valid  [impact-medium]
 ├─ readout fades over --sys-motion-duration-instant
 ├─ swallow the trailing `click` in the CAPTURE phase, once
 │    (detent-sheet.ts:325-330 is the precedent, registered at :156-159 —
 │     extract it)
 ├─ announce once through the frame's role="status"
 └─ NOTHING IS WRITTEN. The draft is dirty. `Запази` commits.

pointercancel        ← THE iOS CASE NOBODY PLANS FOR
 ├─ momentum scroll in an ancestor fires this MID-GESTURE
 ├─ REVERT to the last committed draft value — this is NOT a drop
 ├─ announce the revert: "Преместването е отменено."
 └─ never commit a half-finished time the barber did not choose

lostpointercapture   ← the belt-and-braces net
 └─ if capture is lost with no preceding pointerup, treat it as pointercancel:
    revert, announce, clear [data-dragging]. There is no third outcome.
```

#### Branch two — the block body

> **Ruling (owner ask #4, 2026-08-26): the event body drags to move, and there is no ± pair anywhere on this surface.** §3.4.9's _"no body-drag in v1"_ is overruled. The construction that makes it work on iOS Safari — and why the original rejection was right about the browser and wrong about the conclusion — is set out in §3.4.9; the geometry and the lifecycle are here, because this is the same drag machinery branched, not a second one written.

##### Activation — branched by pointer type, because Apple's own model is

Apple ships **two activation models for the same gesture**: on macOS a mouse press on the body drags immediately — _"drag the event to another day or time"_ — and on iOS it is touch, hold, then drag. Where the input is precise and undo is a keystroke away, no delay. Where the input is a thumb, a hold. **A web implementation that wants HIG parity branches on `pointerType`; it does not pick one delay.**

| Input                      | Activation                                                                                                                                                            | Corroboration                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Mouse / trackpad / pen** | immediate on `pointerdown` + a **5 px** movement threshold. No delay                                                                                                  | Angular CDK `dragStartThreshold: 5`, FullCalendar `eventDragMinDistance: 5`, dnd-kit's 5px distance constraint                                                                                                   |
