| **Touch**                  | **long press 250 ms, movement tolerance 0 px** — any `touchmove` before the timer fires cancels the pending drag and hands the gesture back to the scroller untouched | the field's band is rbd 120, dnd-kit 250, Android `DEFAULT_LONG_PRESS_TIMEOUT` 400, iOS 500, FullCalendar 1000. **250 reads as deliberate without feeling sticky**, and it is the number to re-confirm on device |

⚠ **The tolerance is 0, not 5, and the reason is mechanical rather than aesthetic.** Chromium marks `touchmove` `cancelable: false` once scrolling is already in progress, and a `preventDefault()` on a non-cancelable event is a no-op. Zero tolerance means a drag can only ever activate from a **stationary** finger — which means scrolling has never started, which means the take-over is still honoured. **A non-zero tolerance re-opens exactly that window.** Do not "improve" it. §3.4.9 carries the full reasoning.

##### Threshold, snap, geometry

| Property                            | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Snap**                            | **5 minutes** — the same quantum as the handles                                                                                                                                                                | Apple and Google both snap a move to 15 **because neither built a readout**. We have one. One quantum, no second vocabulary                                                                                                            |
| **Move region**                     | the block minus **22 px at each end** — the inward half of each straddling handle hit area (§3.4.4)                                                                                                            | the handles already own that geometry; the body takes what is left                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Suppression floor**               | **88 px of block — the same number as two non-overlapping 44px handles: 40 min compact / 37 regular / 34 spacious.** Below it the handles own the whole block and there is no move region                      | **reuses the figure §3.4.4 already derived** instead of inventing a second threshold. Below the floor, moving is `Начало` typed, which holds the duration and slides the whole block                                                   |
| **Above 180 min**                   | **suppressed**, per §3.4.2                                                                                                                                                                                     | a destination two windows away cannot be aimed                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **`touch-action`**                  | **`manipulation`, permanently, never changed mid-gesture**                                                                                                                                                     | the whole reversal turns on this. Double-tap-zoom is suppressed; the frame is still scrollable by a touch that starts on the block                                                                                                     |
| **Lift**                            | `scale(1.02)` + `--sys-elevation-overlay` ([tokens.css:195](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:195)), the origin slot left behind at 7% translucent, `navigator.vibrate?.(10)` **guarded and never load-bearing** | Apple's block _"becomes opaque in colour"_; Google's activation signal **is** the haptic — which iOS Safari does not have, so on the platform where the 250 ms tax bites hardest **the lift carries the whole lesson alone**           |
| **Auto-scroll**                     | **the existing one, unchanged and shared with branch one** — 18% dead zone, 18 minutes at every density, ramp 0 → 600 px/s, `requestAnimationFrame`, extent growth, stop on exit                               | SortableJS 30px flat and dnd-kit's 20% corroborate the band. Ours is density-invariant and ramped. **Do not write a second auto-scroller**, and do not inherit SortableJS's `bubbleScroll: true` — the frame is the only scroll target |
| **Cross-day paging on a held edge** | **not implemented**                                                                                                                                                                                            | Google pages a day when you hold at the edge; our frame is one day, and R33 keeps cross-day off the gesture                                                                                                                            |

##### The lifecycle

```
touchstart / pointerdown on the BLOCK BODY
 ├─ pointerType === 'mouse' | 'pen'  → arm immediately, threshold 5px
 ├─ pointerType === 'touch'          → start a 250ms timer, tolerance 0
 │    └─ ANY touchmove before it fires → cancel the pending drag,
 │         do NOT preventDefault, hand the gesture to the frame. Silent.
 ├─ on activation:
 │    ├─ latch the frame's own scroll off — overflow-y: hidden for the
 │    │    duration; auto-scroll drives scrollTop directly (§3.4.12 L3)
 │    ├─ setPointerCapture(pointerId)
 │    ├─ lift: scale + shadow + origin ghost + haptic 10 (guarded)
 │    ├─ block[data-moving], frame[data-dragging] → ticks in, transitions off
 │    └─ readout appears ABOVE the block's start edge, 48 fixed px from the
 │         touch point — a body drag puts the finger in the MIDDLE, so
 │         §3.4.6's opposite-edge rule does not apply

touchmove (passive: false) / pointermove
 ├─ if (event.cancelable) event.preventDefault()      ← the take-over
 ├─ delta   = (clientY - y0 + (frame.scrollTop - scrollTop0)) / pxPerMinute
 ├─ snapped = Math.round(delta / 5) * 5
 ├─ TRANSLATE: draftStartMinute += snapped. THE DURATION SIGNAL IS NOT
 │    TOUCHED — that is what makes this a move and not two resizes, and
 │    since 2026-08-26 the graph enforces it rather than discipline: the
 │    end is computed, so a move CANNOT move it independently
 ├─ clamp: [extent.start, extent.end - duration]
 │         AND draftEnd > arrivedAt when arrivedAt exists   ← §3.4.13
 ├─ haptic 4 on each new snap; 18 ONCE on a newly-clamped frame
 ├─ readout: "10:35 – 11:00 · 25 мин"   ← BOTH boundaries, always
 └─ edge auto-scroll — the shared one, unchanged

pointerup
 ├─ unlatch the frame's overflow, releasePointerCapture, clear [data-moving]
 ├─ haptic: 12 on valid
 ├─ swallow the trailing `click` in the CAPTURE phase, once — the same
 │    extracted helper branch one uses
 ├─ announce once through the frame's existing role="status" (§3.4.10)
 └─ NOTHING IS WRITTEN. The draft is dirty. `Запази` commits.

pointercancel  /  lostpointercapture without pointerup
 └─ revert to the last committed value, unlatch the frame, announce
    "Преместването е отменено." — identical to branch one, and never
    a partial commit
```

**The three nested vertical gestures this branch now contends with are resolved structurally, not by arbitration — §3.4.12.**

#### A drag that leaves the frame is not a special case

**Ruling: `setPointerCapture` means there is no "outside".** Once the handle captures the pointer, `pointermove` and `pointerup` keep arriving at the handle wherever the finger goes — outside the frame, outside the sheet, off the bottom of the viewport. A drag that leaves the frame is a **normal drag that commits on `pointerup`**; the only thing that changes is that auto-scroll stops, per the HIG line already quoted. Do not add bounds-checking that reverts on exit — a barber whose finger drifts 10px off the frame's edge while pulling an end handle down has not cancelled anything, and reverting would be theft.

The genuinely uncontrolled endings are exactly three, and each has a rule:

| Ending                                   | What actually happened                                                                           | Rule                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pointercancel`                          | The OS took the pointer: a system edge gesture, an incoming call, momentum scroll in an ancestor | Revert to the last committed value. Announce. Never a partial commit                                                                    |
| `lostpointercapture` with no `pointerup` | The handle element was replaced, moved between documents, or disabled mid-drag                   | Identical to `pointercancel`. The handle-identity rule below is what makes this rare rather than routine                                |
| Sheet dismissed mid-drag                 | The drag never ends; the component does                                                          | Revert on destroy, and the dirty draft dies with the sheet — the sheet's own dismiss guard already asks before discarding a dirty draft |

⚠ **Haptics, honestly.** `navigator.vibrate()` is Android-only in practice, has **no iOS Safari support**, and requires sticky user activation. Every call above is `?.()`-guarded and **none is load-bearing.** The visual and textual readout carries the whole job on its own — which is precisely why Apple can tolerate 15-minute snapping with no readout and we cannot tolerate 5-minute snapping without one.

⚠ **Handle identity must survive re-render.** The draft signal re-renders the block on every snap; if the handle element is replaced, `setPointerCapture` is lost mid-drag and the `lostpointercapture` branch fires on every single tick. Track by a stable key and assert it in a test.

### 3.4.6 The readout

**Position: pinned to the block's edge _opposite_ the handle being dragged**, inset from the leading edge, offset **48 fixed px** from the touch point. Finger occlusion is physical; it does not get smaller because the user asked for a denser layout, so this offset is one of the few numbers in the frame that is not a space unit.

**The opposite-edge rule is a resize rule, and it does not survive the move branch.** A body drag puts the finger in the _middle_ of the block, so there is no far edge to hide behind: while the body is dragged the readout sits **above the block's start edge**, at the same 48 fixed px from the touch point.

| While                       | Reads                                 | Gloss                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| resizing top                | `от 10:35 · 25 мин`                   | new start · resulting duration                                                                                            |
| resizing bottom             | `до 11:00 · 25 мин`                   | till 11:00 · 25 min                                                                                                       |
| **moving the whole block**  | `10:35 – 11:00 · 25 мин`              | **both boundaries, always** — a move changed both and kept the duration, so naming one edge would hide the other          |
| overlap                     | `Застъпва Петър 11:30`                | destructive tone                                                                                                          |
| after close                 | `След затваряне`                      | destructive                                                                                                               |
| too short (single service)  | `Най-малко 10 мин`                    | destructive                                                                                                               |
| **too short (≥2 services)** | `най-малко 45 мин — променете услуга` | destructive. The **service floor** of §3.4.5, which names the fix instead of stating the bound — tapping it pushes Услуги |
| would newly cross midnight  | `Не може да мине през полунощ`        | destructive — see §3.4.7                                                                                                  |
| outside the roster          | `Извън смяната`                       | **warning tone, and permitted**                                                                                           |

**Always both the boundary time and the resulting duration**, because that is Google's duration-annotated-dropdown insight applied to a gesture. **`aria-hidden="true"`** — it duplicates the slider's own `aria-valuetext`, announced natively on every arrow press.

### 3.4.7 Collisions, bounds, refusals

**The table below is written for a resize, because a resize can break every invariant in it.** A move breaks a strict subset — it cannot shorten the block, it cannot invert the edges, and it sweeps both buffers instead of one — and §3.4.13 states which checks the server skips and which it re-runs. Where the two diverge, §3.4.13 governs.

| Situation                                              | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Minimum duration**                                   | Hard clamp at **`max(10, S − K)`** — the platform floor and the service floor, whichever is higher (§3.4.5). The 10 is not 20: `SHORTEST_SELLABLE_MINUTES = 20` ([staff-day.store.ts:40](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:40)) governs what the public may **book** — it is the filter on sellable gaps at [staff-day.store.ts:220](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:220) — not what staff may **place**, and a beard tidy-up is a real ten-minute job. _(The second floor is new, 2026-08-26: with the end derived from a duration, a shrink that used to be arithmetic is now an edit to the services, and a gesture may not make one it cannot name.)_ |
| **Overlap with a neighbour**                           | **Drawn, named, permitted.** The frame draws it side-by-side in lanes; the readout turns destructive; on release the sheet grows a conflict row with a `Виж` that scrolls the frame to the offender; **`Запази` relabels to `Запази въпреки застъпването`.** One extra tap, no dialog. The barber who chose it knows something the model does not — one client in the chair, one under the dryer                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Buffer collision** (cleanup touching the next setup) | Softer. Secondary-ink footnote naming the neighbour and its time: `Няма време за подготовка преди Петър 11:30.` No relabel. **Advice, not a verdict**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Outside the roster**                                 | **Permitted.** Warning tone, amber note, `outsideWindow: true` on the resulting occupancy                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **Into the past / over the now line**                  | **Permitted, silently.** A barber recording that a cut actually started at 10:10 is the commonest correction in the shop; warning here would be noise                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Server refuses on save**                             | `BookingGatewayError` ([booking-gateway.port.ts:110](../../libs/application/booking/src/lib/ports/booking-gateway.port.ts:110)) → `translateDomainError` → rendered **in the region that earned it**, `role="alert"`. The draft survives; the button re-enables                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

#### Midnight: existing crossings are editable, new ones are not

The blanket refusal "the frame never crosses midnight" contradicts what this app already ships. Cross-midnight appointments exist and are drawn today:

- The day agenda stamps them: `@if (visit.crossesMidnight) {<span>⁺¹</span>}` ([staff-dashboard.html:1229](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1229)), from a VM field ([staff-dashboard.ts:148](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.ts:148)) computed at [staff-dashboard.ts:2281](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.ts:2281).
- The grid does **not** wrap them to the top of the day. Its `extent` **grows past 24:00** to hold them: `const end = Math.ceil(Math.max(DAY_MINUTES, ...ends) / 60) * 60` ([staff-time-grid.ts:273](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:273), `DAY_MINUTES = 1440` at [:138](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:138)), under a comment that states the rule outright: a 23:30 cut ending at 00:15 belongs to the day it started on, "so the axis stretches to hold it rather than wrapping it round to the top" ([staff-time-grid.ts:255-275](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/time-grid/staff-time-grid.ts:255)).

**Ruling: staff may not CREATE a crossing in the frame. Existing crossings stay fully editable.** Concretely:

- **Opening on one.** The frame's extent uses the same `Math.max(DAY_MINUTES, …)` rule as the page grid — no new arithmetic, no wrap. The gutter continues past midnight as `00:00⁺¹`, `00:30⁺¹`, and a 1px separator labelled `полунощ` marks the crossing (§3.4.3). **Both handles are live.**
- **What the end handle may do on an existing crossing.** Anything inside the extent, including pulling the end back _before_ midnight. The clamp is one-directional.
- **What it may not do.** A block that starts and ends before 24:00 cannot be dragged across. The end handle clamps at 23:59; the readout says `Не може да мине през полунощ.` The key stays `noMidnight`; the copy is corrected from the old absolute phrasing to this one, because the old phrasing asserted something false about the product.
- **The one-way door, stated plainly.** Pull an existing crossing back before midnight and it stops crossing — and it cannot be pushed across again, because the create-side rule now applies. That is a real edge, the barber should be told about it once, and the confirmation on `Запази` says so: `Часът вече няма да минава полунощ.` _(This appointment will no longer cross midnight.)_
- **Moving a crossing to a different day** changes `dayKey` and the busy projection. That remains a different operation, served by `Премести на друг ден`.

#### The domain consequence of permitting overlap

**It must be named, not assumed.** `decideBooking`'s `checkPlacement` ([decide-booking.ts:416](../../apps/functions/src/use-cases/decide-booking.ts:416), called at [:340](../../apps/functions/src/use-cases/decide-booking.ts:340)) refuses a colliding placement. The staff callable therefore needs a **new** `deps.allowOverlap`, defaulted `false`, set `true` only when the request carries a **new** `acknowledgedOverlap: true` — which is what the second tap on `Запази въпреки застъпването` sets. **`allowOutsideWindow` is NOT the same shape.** It is set unconditionally `true` for `staffEditAppointment` — [roster-window.ts:98-113](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/roster-window.ts:98) already rules that _"Staff may place an appointment anywhere, including outside these windows"_ — so there is no request field, no second tap and no commit-label variant. Amber is advice; red is a decision. **A client-side "permitted" that the server refuses is worse than a clamp.**

### 3.4.8 Keyboard

**The typed rows are the real keyboard contract; the frame's keyboard support is a courtesy.** Say it plainly, because pretending a drag surface is a first-class keyboard surface is how accessibility theatre happens. A keyboard user tabs to `Начало` and types, or opens the `Времетраене` menu and picks — with no switch to find first, because ask #3 put both rows permanently on screen beside the frame (§3.5).

**This is also the WCAG 2.5.7 argument for the body-drag, and it may never be traded away.** SC 2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA) requires that everything operable by dragging be operable _without_ dragging by a single pointer. **The gesture alone fails it; the always-visible `Начало` row and `Времетраене` menu are what rescue it.** Any future proposal to put those two rows behind a disclosure, a preference or a width breakpoint is a conformance regression, and is refused on that ground before taste is even discussed. _(2026-08-26: the pair used to be `От`/`До`. Ruling B replaced them and §3.4.5 re-points the writes; the conformance argument is unchanged, because what 2.5.7 asks for is a non-drag path to the same outcome, not a particular pair of fields.)_

That said, the frame is fully operable, and for free, because each handle is a real slider:

| Key                   | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `↑` / `↓`             | ∓5 min                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `Shift + ↑/↓`         | **∓1 min** — the precision escape. Fantastical and BusyCal ship Shift-drag for this; as a keyboard verb it needs no modifier held during a gesture                                                                      |
| `PageUp` / `PageDown` | ∓60 min                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `Home` / `End`        | the earliest / latest legal minute — **which the `aria-valuemin`/`aria-valuemax` already encode, so a blind user lands exactly on the neighbour's edge without ever being told a block is there**                       |
| `Tab`                 | `Ден` pill → _(relative chips → calendar grid, only while the calendar is expanded)_ → upper jump caret (when drawn) → start handle → **block** → end handle → lower jump caret (when drawn) → `Начало` → `Времетраене` |

**The tab order is load-bearing, not incidental — and it is DOM-truthful rather than tidy.** A caret drawn at a clipped edge precedes the block it points at; the calendar's cells exist only while the calendar is expanded; the two typed rows follow the frame because that is where they now sit on the page.

> ⚠ **Amended 2026-08-26 (owner comment 9).** This paragraph used to read _"the no-drag path comes first, always: a keyboard or switch user reaches the two typed fields and the duration menu before any gesture surface."_ **The order is reversed** — `Ден` → frame → `Начало`/`Времетраене` — and the guarantee survives verbatim, because **SC 2.5.7 requires the single-pointer, non-drag alternative to _exist_, not to _precede_.** The `Начало` row and the `Времетраене` menu are the very next tab stops after the frame, both handles are independently `role="slider"` and arrow-operable, and the block has its own grab-and-move vocabulary below. A keyboard or switch user still finishes the entire edit without performing a single drag.
>
> **What is NOT weakened, and is the clause worth quoting at a reviewer:** the `Начало` row and the `Времетраене` menu **may never be hidden behind a disclosure, a preference, a toggle or a width breakpoint.** Only their position on the page moved. Any proposal to collapse them is a conformance regression and is refused on that ground before taste is discussed.

#### The block's own keyboard vocabulary — grab and move

The block is a real `<button>` and is in the tab order anyway, so the move gesture owes it a keyboard twin. **A move is two values and a slider carries one**, so this one cannot be `role="slider"`; it is grab-and-move, and that is the single place §4.4's exclusion of a grab-and-move keyboard model is narrowed rather than upheld — the exclusion was always about _resize_, where the slider is strictly better.

| Key               | Effect                                                                                            |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Enter` / `Space` | grab. Announce `Хванат. Стрелките местят по 5 минути.` _(Grabbed. The arrows move by 5 minutes.)_ |
| `↑` / `↓`         | ∓5 min, **whole interval, duration invariant.** Announce each step                                |
| `Shift + ↑/↓`     | ∓60 min                                                                                           |
| `Enter` / `Space` | drop into the draft                                                                               |
| `Escape`          | revert and announce                                                                               |

**We do not port Apple's `⌃⌥↑/↓` literally.** On a Bulgarian layout `Ctrl+Alt` is AltGr, and several OSes claim the chord. The semantics — arrows nudge — survive; the modifier is dropped, because the grab already scopes the arrows safely.

**Atlassian's action-menu alternative is deliberately not built.** Pragmatic drag-and-drop dropped directional keyboard dragging after testing — _"directional arrow movement doesn't always make sense when you can't see the interface"_ — and shipped a per-item menu instead. **Their items have no numeric address. Ours do: a time and a length.** The `Начало` row **is** the explicit-command path for a move, and the `Времетраене` menu is one for a resize — both beat an action menu, because they take absolute values rather than relative nudges.

The block carries `role="button"` plus a **localised** `aria-roledescription` — `staff.visit.blockRole` = `преместваем блок` _(movable block)_, **new key**. dnd-kit's default `"draggable"` is English and would ship untranslated.

**Every change announces through `aria-valuetext` natively.** No live region is needed for the handles. **Keyboard editing is never clipped:** any arrow press that moves a handle outside the drawn window scrolls it into view first, so the "event longer than the window" case of §3.4.2 has no keyboard equivalent of an off-screen handle.

### 3.4.9 Moving the whole block

> ### ⚠️ OVERRULED BY THE OWNER, 2026-08-26 — this section is kept for its reasoning, not its conclusion
>
> The shop asked for **the event body itself to be draggable**, in addition to the two chevron handles that resize it. That reverses the ruling below, _and_ §4.4's exclusion of the same feature, and it reverses Q9's _"later, as its own PR"_. It lands **in M4, beside the handles**, because the block's geometry — where a handle's hit area ends and the move region begins — can only be authored once.
>
> **What survived the reversal, because it was a browser fact rather than taste:** `touch-action` **is latched by the browser at the moment the touch begins, and changing it mid-gesture is a no-op.** MDN says so outright: _"changes made after the gesture has started will not affect the current gesture."_ Both designs on the table in the original ruling depended on flipping `pan-y` → `none` when a long-press timer fired, and both would have shipped a block that lifts while the frame scrolls under it.
>
> **What changed is the construction, not the browser.** The working design does not switch `touch-action` at all:
>
> |                             | Original design (correctly rejected)     | The shipping design                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
> | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
> | `touch-action` on the block | `pan-y`, flipped to `none` on activation | **`manipulation`, permanently.** Never changed. Double-tap-zoom is suppressed; the frame can still be scrolled by a touch that starts on the block                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
> | How the gesture is taken    | the `touch-action` flip                  | **Touch Events with `{ passive: false }`**, `preventDefault()` on every `touchmove` after activation, guarded by `if (event.cancelable)`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
> | Why that is reliable        | it was not                               | **zero movement tolerance.** Any `touchmove` before the timer fires cancels the pending drag, so a drag can only ever activate from a _stationary_ finger — which means scrolling has never started, which means `touchmove` is still `cancelable` and `preventDefault` is still honoured. Chromium marks `touchmove` `cancelable: false` **once scrolling is in progress**; the zero-tolerance rule closes that window, and a non-zero tolerance re-opens it |
>
> This is react-beautiful-dnd's model (120 ms / **0 px**), which is the cleanest in the field, run at dnd-kit's touch delay. It is also the model every mobile calendar that ships this gesture uses: **Apple requires touch-and-hold, Google requires hold-until-it-vibrates, and Outlook mobile is only shipping drag-to-reschedule in late 2026 — restricted to day and multi-day views.** The industry answer to _"how do you tell a body-drag from a scroll on a touch screen"_ is unanimous: **you don't — you make the user declare intent by holding still.**
>
> **What the reversal costs, honestly. Six things, none of them free:**
>
> 1. **A second input code path.** The handles are Pointer Events with `setPointerCapture`; the body is Touch Events with `preventDefault`. One component, two vocabularies, and a `pointerType` branch on top. **No other surface in this repo has this**, and §4.3's fourth objection — _"answered by not writing a new one"_ — no longer holds as written.
> 2. **A device-test matrix that did not exist**: iOS Safari, Android Chrome, iPadOS with a trackpad, at all three densities, on a short block and a long one. This is a gate on M4, not a follow-up.
> 3. **A 250 ms tax on every touch move.** A barber who drags immediately gets a scroll, which reads as _"it ignored me"_ until he learns to hold. The lift and the haptic are what teach it — and on iOS the haptic does not exist (`navigator.vibrate` has no iOS Safari support), so **the lift carries the whole lesson on the platform where it matters most.**
> 4. **The frame stops being a plain `overflow: auto` box.** Its own scroll must be latched off for the duration of a drag and driven programmatically by auto-scroll, which means a scroll controller instead of a CSS property (§3.4.12, L3).
> 5. **A second keyboard vocabulary.** `role="slider"` handles resize with no mode; a move is two values and cannot be a slider, so the block gets grab-and-move (§3.4.8) — and **§4.4's exclusion of "a grab-and-move keyboard model" must be narrowed to resize**, or the document contradicts itself.
> 6. **Move and resize become two commands on the wire**, with two validators, two undo strings and two announcement shapes (§3.4.13). That is more work than one `PATCH` of two timestamps, and it is the correct amount of work.
>
> **What the reversal does NOT buy.** Cross-chair and cross-day movement stay off the gesture — **R33 stands.** A horizontal drag would re-decide roster, lead time, conflicts and terms server-side mid-gesture with no way to preview the destination. `⋯ → Смени стола` and `Премести на друг ден` remain the paths, and §4.3's first objection is still answered by removing the sideways gesture entirely.

**Original reasoning, retained — it is why the shipping construction looks the way it does:**

> ⚠ **Both long-press-to-move designs on the table depend on switching `touch-action` from `pan-y` to `none` when the timer fires. `touch-action` is latched by the browser at the moment the touch begins; changing it mid-gesture is a no-op on iOS Safari.** The long press would fire, the block would lift, and the frame would scroll under the finger instead of the block moving.
>
> **Ruling: no body-drag in v1.** Moving is fully served by paths that all work: drag one handle then the other; the typed `От` field, which carries the end with it; and `⋯ → Смени стола` / `Премести на друг ден` for the cross-axis cases.
>
> If body-drag is wanted later it is its own PR with a device test, and the only construction that works is `touch-action` **fixed** on the block body, with the gesture taken from the pointer stream rather than from a mid-gesture property flip.

**Moving now has three paths, and the ± nudge is not among them** — it is deleted from this surface entirely, ruling #4:

1. **Drag the block body.** §3.4.5, branch two.
2. **Type `Начало`**, which holds the duration and slides the whole block — the keyboard, switch and WCAG 2.5.7 path, not a fallback (§3.4.8). _(Amended 2026-08-26: this row used to read "type `От`, which carries `До` with it." There is no `До` on this sheet any more — §3.5, Ruling B — and the behaviour it described is now a property of the duration, not of a second field.)_
3. **`⋯ → Смени стола` / `Премести на друг ден`** for the cross-axis cases the gesture deliberately refuses.

### 3.4.10 Screen reader

```html
<section
  class="staff-frame"
  role="group"
  [attr.aria-label]="t('staff.visit.frameLabel', {start, end})"
  data-drag-owner
>
  <p uiVisuallyHidden>{{ frameSummary() }}</p>
  <p role="status" aria-live="polite" uiVisuallyHidden>{{ announcement() }}</p>
  <header class="staff-frame__owner">…</header>
  <!-- §3.4.3 — plain text,
       no role, not focusable; only the tone swatch inside is aria-hidden -->
  …
</section>
```

`frameSummary()` is the **authoritative** description, and it is what makes every decorative layer safe to hide:

> _Часът е 10:35 до 11:00, 25 минути, при Иван. Преди него Мартин до 09:50. След него свободно до 12:00. Смяната е 09:00 до 18:00. Подготовка 5 минути преди, разчистване 10 минути след._

It states both boundaries and both neighbours **regardless of what the window is currently showing**, which is the whole reason the scroll rulings of §3.4.2 cost nothing here. For a party it names the sibling leg and its chair; for a whole-day exception it names the closure instead of the axis.

**Since 2026-08-26 it is also the _only_ narration of the frame.** Comment 6 deleted the visible footnote that said the same sentence to somebody who was already looking at the picture (§3.4.3); `frameSummary` and `frameLabel` survive verbatim and stay SR-only. One consequence belongs in the review checklist rather than in the copy: with no visible twin left, a regression in this string is **invisible to everyone who can see**. Assert its _content_ in a test, not its presence.

Neighbours, shoulders, roster shading, the midnight rule and the now line are all `aria-hidden="true"` — they are visual encodings of facts this one paragraph already states, and walking three positioned buttons to learn what one sentence says is worse than not knowing.

**`role="group"`, not `role="application"`, not a grid.**

#### What `announcement()` says

The `role="status"` region carries only the things `aria-valuetext` cannot: outcomes, refusals and things that happened _to_ the drag rather than _because of_ it. One row per event, and every row fires **once**.

**The block's move gesture reuses this same region** — §3.11's _"exactly three live regions in the whole surface"_ is unchanged by ruling #4, and a move can never race a resize into two regions, because one pointer cannot do both.

| Event                                        | Announcement                                                                                         | Gloss                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Move committed**                           | `Преместено: 14:30 – 15:15. Продължителност 45 мин. (без промяна)`                                   | _Moved: 14:30–15:15. Duration 45 min (unchanged)._         |
| **Resize committed, end handle**             | `Край: 15:30. Продължителност 60 мин.`                                                               | _End: 15:30. Duration 60 min._                             |
| **Resize committed, start handle**           | `Начало: 14:15. Продължителност 60 мин.`                                                             | _Start: 14:15. Duration 60 min._                           |
| Drag committed over an overlap               | `10:35 – 11:00. Застъпва Петър 11:30.`                                                               | the conflict, in the same breath                           |
| Keyboard grab on the block                   | `Хванат. Стрелките местят по 5 минути.`                                                              | _Grabbed. The arrows move by 5 minutes._                   |
| Each keyboard move step                      | `10:35 – 11:00. 25 минути.`                                                                          | both boundaries, because a move changed both               |
| **`pointercancel`**                          | `Преместването е отменено.`                                                                          | _Move cancelled._ — the revert, never a silent snap-back   |
| **`lostpointercapture` without `pointerup`** | `Преместването е отменено.`                                                                          | identical; the barber does not care which of the two fired |
| Drag ended with the finger outside the frame | — **nothing**. It committed normally                                                                 | announcing an "exit" that changed no outcome is noise      |
| Clamped at a bound (first time in this drag) | `Най-малко 10 минути.` / `Най-малко 45 минути — променете услуга.` / `Не може да мине през полунощ.` | the refusal, once, not per tick                            |
| Extent grew during auto-scroll               | `Показани са още 30 минути.`                                                                         | _30 more minutes shown._                                   |
| Jump caret used                              | `Показан е краят, 12:30.`                                                                            | _End shown, 12:30._                                        |
| `Запази` relabelled after an overlap         | `Запази въпреки застъпването.`                                                                       | the button changed under them; say so                      |

**The asymmetry between the three commit rows is deliberate, and it mirrors the payload.** A move changed both endpoints and kept the duration, so it says all three numbers. A resize changed **one** endpoint, so announcing both times is noise that hides the thing that actually changed.

**Each resize row already names the value it now writes, which is why Ruling B changes none of them.** `Край: 15:30. Продължителност 60 мин.` states the derived end _and_ the authored duration in that order, because the end is what the barber was aiming at and the duration is what was stored — the same two readings the `Времетраене` row carries as `60 мин · до 15:30` (§3.5). The start-handle row says both for the same reason: it is the one gesture that writes `Начало` **and** `Времетраене` at once (§3.4.5). Atlassian's rule — name the item, the former position, the new position — is what this implements, with the time doing the work their items have no equivalent of.

### 3.4.11 Reduced motion

Direct manipulation is **not** "motion" in the `prefers-reduced-motion` sense — it tracks the finger, which is the point. Under `reduce`:

- the 5-minute-tick fade → instant
- **the body-drag's lift → opacity only, no `scale(1.02)`.** The origin ghost still fades, because it is the answer to _"where did it come from"_ and not decoration
- the on-open reveal → jump, not smooth-scroll
- the jump caret's scroll → jump, not smooth-scroll
- edge auto-scroll → flat **300 px/s**, no acceleration curve (it is navigation, not decoration, so it still happens)
- block resize after a service change → jump
- the conflict row appears without a height transition
- disclosure open/close → instant
- the success moment → the status line only, no confetti

`[data-dragging] { transition: none }` makes most of this free, and `[data-moving]` falls out of the same rule rather than needing its own. Per the conventions, reduced motion is global and a component adds a block only **to add motion back** — none of the above does.

### 3.4.12 The nested-gesture question, resolved structurally

> **This section is rewritten, 2026-08-26.** Its old conclusion — _"the much-discussed three nested drag consumers problem is an artefact of choosing the detent sheet"_ — was true while the block was inert. **Ruling #4 makes the block a fourth consumer, and the answer is now structural rather than an observation that the problem never arose.**

There are four vertical gesture consumers stacked on one another, and each is resolved by construction rather than by arbitration:

```
L1  ui-modal-sheet     — drag-to-dismiss (vertical, downward)
L2  sheet body         — vertical scroll
L3  the frame          — vertical scroll
L4  the event block    — body-drag (move) + two edge drags (resize)
```

| Layer  | Resolution                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **L1** | **already solved, by construction.** `UiSheetBehavior.onDragStart` bails on `closest('button, a')` ([sheet-behavior.ts:207](../../libs/ui/layout/src/lib/sheet/sheet-behavior.ts:207)) **and** the sheet's drag is bound only to `<ui-sheet-header>` ([modal-sheet.html:40-43](../../libs/ui/controls/src/lib/modal-sheet/modal-sheet.html:40)), which carries `touch-action: none` and sits above the scroller. The block is a `<button>`, so L1 is out of contention for free. ⚠ **That is now load-bearing rather than incidental: write a unit test asserting the block matches `closest('button')`**, because a future refactor to `div[role="button"]` would break the whole gesture silently |
| **L2** | contends with L4 only, and is arbitrated by the activation rule of §3.4.5 — immediate-with-5px on a mouse, 250 ms-with-0px on a finger. This is the ordinary problem every drag library solves, solved the way they solve it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **L3** | **latched off for the duration of a drag.** `overflow-y` flips to `hidden` at activation and back on `pointerup` / `pointercancel`; the drag's auto-scroll drives `scrollTop` directly. Outside a drag the frame carries **`overscroll-behavior-y: contain`**, so it never chains into L2 — free, structural, and it kills pull-to-refresh inside the frame as a side effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **L4** | the block: `touch-action: manipulation` **permanently**, never flipped (§3.4.9). The handles keep `touch-action: none` **on themselves only** — never on the frame, or the frame stops scrolling                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

**Auto-scroll targets the frame and nothing else.** SortableJS's `bubbleScroll: true` default is exactly wrong here — a drag that scrolls the sheet body under the frame would move the destination while you aim at it. dnd-kit's `canScroll` opt-out is the right shape.

**Ship `data-drag-owner` anyway** — it is **new** — as one line at the top of `onDragStart` in **both** consumers:

```ts
if ((event.target as Element).closest?.('[data-drag-owner]')) return;
```

For `ui-detent-sheet` it is genuinely required — its drag binds to `.ui-detent-sheet__content` and does **not** bail on `button`/`a`, so any future drag surface inside one is broken by default. For `ui-modal-sheet` it is free insurance and documents the contract, sitting one line above the existing bail. **A `stopPropagation()` inside the frame would have been the wrong fix**, because it breaks the sheet's scroll hand-off.

### 3.4.13 Move and resize are two writes, not one edit

Every mature implementation treats them separately, and **the shape of the delta _is_ the semantic difference.** FullCalendar's `eventDrop` carries **one** `delta`; `eventResize` carries **`startDelta` and `endDelta`**, of which exactly one is normally non-zero. It also gates them with three separate permissions — `eventStartEditable`, `eventDurationEditable`, `eventResizableFromStart` — not one `editable`.

> **Ruling: `staffEditAppointment` takes a discriminated command, not a `PATCH` of two timestamps.** `{ kind: 'move', start }` versus `{ kind: 'resize', edge: 'start' | 'end', at }`. The server validates differently, the audit log records which happened, and the domain stays rich rather than degenerating into a bag of nullable fields. **Three permission booleans on the callable, not one.**

Consequently `eventDraft` names the gesture: `output<{ id; startMinute; endMinute; via: 'move' | 'resize-start' | 'resize-end' }>()`. The sheet cannot re-derive `via` from the numbers, because a move that happens to land on a legal duration is arithmetically indistinguishable from two resizes, and the toast and the announcement (§3.4.10) both depend on knowing which one the barber performed.

Funnelling both into a single `validateAppointmentTimes(start, end)` would lose the ability to say **which edge** is the problem — the only thing that makes the error actionable:

| Invariant                      | **Move** (translate; duration invariant)                                                                                                                        | **Resize** (one edge; duration changes)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Duration ≥ Σ service durations | **cannot break it. Skip the check**                                                                                                                             | **the primary check**, and it now has a full decision table rather than a single verdict: over-length becomes named slack, under-length consumes slack and then **clamps**, and a single-service appointment takes a per-service duration override. See "Where the delta lands" in §3.4.5. _(Amended 2026-08-26: the override is authored on the service's **pushed page**, not in an inline token editor — §3.6, Ruling C.)_ |
| `end > start`                  | cannot break it                                                                                                                                                 | enforced per edge; a start drag past the end **clamps, never inverts**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Inside the roster window       | re-check **both** boundaries                                                                                                                                    | re-check **only the moved edge**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Collision + buffers            | the whole interval sweeps: check the **entire destination interval**, and **both** buffers move with it                                                         | only the moved edge advances: check that edge's neighbourhood and **only that side's buffer**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Capacity / parallel lane       | a move can change the lane — **re-solve placement**                                                                                                             | the lane is kept; only its occupancy grows                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **`arrivedAt`**                | **a move that lands `draftEnd` before a recorded `arrivedAt` is a data-integrity problem, not a scheduling one.** Hard clamp, destructive readout, its own copy | a start-resize hits the same rule; an end-resize is unaffected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |

`Appointment.arrivedAt` is real and already persisted ([appointment.ts:162](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/appointment.ts:162), written at [appointment-document.ts:108-111](../../libs/application/booking/src/lib/ports/appointment-document.ts:108)), so this clamp has something to clamp against on day one.

**New copy:** `beforeArrival` = `Клиентът е дошъл в {{time}} — часът не може да свърши преди това.` _(The client arrived at {{time}} — the appointment cannot end before that.)_
**New error code:** `booking.staffEdit.before_arrival` → `errors.booking.staffEdit.before_arrival`.

#### Undo wording — name the action, never say only "Отмени"

Apple's `NSUndoManager.setActionName:` rule, adopted: **the name is set at the same moment the operation is registered**, so the two cannot drift. Google's mobile equivalent is a snackbar with `Undo` after every drag commit.

| Operation            | Toast                                         |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Move                 | `Часът е преместен на 14:30.` · **Отмени**    |
| Resize, end handle   | `Краят е променен на 15:30.` · **Отмени**     |
| Resize, start handle | `Началото е променено на 14:15.` · **Отмени** |

> **Ruling: the sheet's primary label does NOT vary by gesture.** The sheet commits an appointment, not a gesture; a button that reads `Премести` one second and `Промени продължителността` the next is a flicker, not information. `Запази` stays `Запази` — and `Запази въпреки застъпването` when overlapping, per R22. **The per-gesture wording lives in the toast and in the announcement**, which is where Apple and Google both put it.

---

## 3.5 The time section

> **The order of this region, settled 2026-08-26 (owner comment 9): `Ден` → the frame → `Начало` / `Времетраене`.** Date first, because it is the coarsest fact and the one that reframes everything below it; the frame second, because it is where the appointment is _placed_; the typed rows last, immediately beneath the picture they are the typed twin of. This **reverses** the previous _"the fields sit ABOVE the frame"_; the reasons that ordering rested on are answered one by one in §3.3 R2 › ruling 2, and the WCAG 2.5.7 clause it carried survives **verbatim** — only its position on the page moved.
>
> Two things this section no longer contains, and neither is an omission: **there is no `Кога` summary row and no `КОГА` eyebrow** (comment 11 — every group is unlabelled or `aria-label`led, never titled), and **there is no `Стол` row** (comment 7 — the chair is named on the frame, §3.4.2, and per service where it differs, §3.6).

### `Начало` + `Времетраене` — the end is derived, and stored nowhere

> **⚠ Reversed 2026-08-26 (Ruling B, owner comment 8): `От` / `До` is deleted from the appointment sheet.** The two authored facts are **`Начало`** — one instant — and **`Времетраене`** — one span. **The end is a `computed()` and is persisted nowhere.** The owner is right, and the reason is structural rather than ergonomic. `От`/`До` stays in the **block** sheet exactly as it ships.
>
> **⚠ Reversed 2026-08-26 (owner comment 9): the typed rows sit BELOW the frame.** The order is `Ден` → frame → `Начало`/`Времетраене`. §3.3 R2 › ruling 2 carries the three-reason table; the short form is that the _occlusion_ argument which put the fields first **dissolved when `До` left**, because nothing in this region raises a keypad any more, and the _causality_ argument re-points rather than breaking: the frame is where you place the appointment, and `Начало` is its typed twin sitting immediately beneath it.
>
> **What survives, unamended:** the frame and the typed path are on screen together, always — no toggle, no preference, no default (owner asks #3 + #4, 2026-08-26). The `[ ▤ ] [ ⌨ ]` switch this section used to open with is **dead**, and so is the per-device `localStorage` preference behind it. A switch between two editors is a question the barber should never have been asked: both are cheap, both fit, and the one that is hidden is always the one he needed.

#### Why the end is an output

In a product where every service carries a duration and an appointment's length is the arrangement's span over its services, the end time is not a fact anyone holds. It is a computation:

```
   AUTHORED                            DERIVED
   ────────                            ───────
   startsAt          ─┐
   service[n].dur    ─┤   ──────────►  span(arrangement)  ──►  endsAt
   arrangement       ─┤                 (sum sequential, max parallel)
   slackMinutes      ─┘
```

`От`/`До` asks the barber to author a value the system already knows how to compute — **and to compute it in his head in order to do so.** The HIG closes it in one bullet: _"Get information from the system whenever possible. Don't ask people to enter information that you can gather automatically."_ Two more bullets shape the control that replaces it: _"When possible, offer choices instead of requiring text entry"_, and, on pickers, _"If you need to display a fairly short list of choices, consider using a pull-down button instead of a picker."_ A barbershop's realistic duration set is about eight values. **That is a `ui-menu`, not a wheel and not a field.**

Three consequences follow, and each is a class of bug that becomes **unrepresentable** rather than validated:

| #   | What becomes impossible                           | Why it mattered                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **`До ≤ От`**                                     | A non-negative duration has no invalid state. NN/g: _"Remove illogical date options."_ Satisfied by construction, which is strictly better than satisfied by validation — and it is why **`errors.booking.staffEdit.invalid_range` is not needed and must not be added** (§3.10). |
| 2   | **"I moved the start and the end didn't follow"** | Google Calendar's most-filed complaint on this exact control. It exists only because the end is stored.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| 3   | **Two sources of truth for one number**           | An editable derived field is a conflict surface, not a control: every service edit would have to decide whether it moves the end or is clamped by it — permanently, in exchange for a convenience obtainable another way.                                                         |

**And the market check is nearly unanimous inside our actual category.** Fresha, Phorest, Vagaro, Booksy, Square, Mangomint: **start + duration, no end field — 6/6** (§1.4). The only two products in the wider corpus that keep an end field are Jobber and Housecall Pro, and they are the two whose length is _not_ catalogue-determined; Housecall Pro, which shares our exact structure, derives the end from the price-book sum and keeps the field only as an override. Google and Outlook keep an end field **and** annotate every row of its dropdown with the duration it produces (§1.3) — a confession that the user reasons in duration, paid for with a translation on every row. They have no catalogue to derive from. **We do. Don't inherit the workaround.**

#### The group, before and after

```
BEFORE                                     AFTER
┌───────────────────────────────┐          ┌───────────────────────────────┐
│ От           До               │ 44+lbl   │ Начало               10:00    │  44
│ [10:00]    [10:20]            │          ├───────────────────────────────┤
├───────────────────────────────┤          │ Времетраене  45 мин · до 10:45│  44
│ Стол               Стол 2  ›  │          └───────────────────────────────┘
└───────────────────────────────┘             (`Стол` is deleted — comment 7,
                                               the chair is named on the frame)
```

The `От`/`До` pair was this sheet's only two-input, two-field construct and its only horizontal `ui-stack` inside a list group. **Both disappear.**

#### `Начало` — the one authored instant

Trailing is `input[uiTextField] type="time" step="300"` inside `.staff-sheet__pill`, styled as the same tinted capsule the `Ден` row wears.

> **Ruling: we do not build a time wheel.** Tapping the pill raises the **platform's own** time picker — the wheel on iOS, the dial on Android — which is exactly what Apple's compact-time half delegates to (§1.1). We build the calendar (Ruling A) because we have data to draw on it: occupancy. **We build nothing for time because we have nothing to add.** A hand-rolled wheel would be a second implementation of a solved control, with its own focus trap, its own reduced-motion story and its own bug queue, in exchange for nothing the platform does not already do better.

`min = rosterStart − 60`, `max = rosterEnd + 60`, as **native attributes**. Ruling #2 of the old nine survives verbatim in substance — an illegal value is unreachable rather than validated — it is simply no longer coupled to an end field, so it has one arm instead of two.

**Moving `Начало` holds the duration and slides the whole block.** Apple's behaviour, and correct for a shop: a client arriving ten minutes late does not get a ten-minute-shorter cut. There is no longer an "escape" to learn, because there is nothing to escape from — the duration is the stored fact, so it is _always_ pinned. The old ruling #7's carry-over-with-an-escape is now an invariant.

#### `Времетраене` — the authored span, carrying its own consequence

The trailing value carries two readings on one line:

```
45 мин · до 10:45
└──┬──┘   └───┬──┘
   │          └─ the DERIVED end · --sys-color-tertiary-label · never tappable
   └─ the value · --sys-color-secondary-label
```

That annotation is Google's parenthesis moved to where it belongs: **attached to the number the barber authors**, answering the question he asks next — _"when am I free?"_ — with no second arithmetic step in the other direction. Google puts it on the end row, which means the barber reads a duration to choose an end in order to get a duration.

**Formatting (bg):** `20 мин` · `45 мин` · `1 ч` · `1 ч 15 мин` · `2 ч 30 мин`. **Never `90 мин`, never a decimal.** Crossing midnight, the end reads `до 00:15 (утре)` — `staff.visit.durationNextDay`, and it is the only place in this sheet where a time carries a day.

**The menu** — `ui-menu` anchored to the trailing pill (§3.3 R2 names why it may not be a direct child of the group), items as `role="menuitemradio"`, which the component already derives from `uiSelected` being set ([menu.ts:53-54](../../libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/menu/menu.ts:53)) — so the role costs nothing:

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│  20 мин              до 10:20    │
│  30 мин              до 10:30    │
│  40 мин              до 10:40    │
│✓ 45 мин              до 10:45    │
│    сума на услугите              │  ← quiet caption, tertiary
│  60 мин              до 11:00    │
│  1 ч 30 мин          до 11:30    │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│  Друго…                          │  → minutes entry, grid-snapped
│  До определен час…               │  → time picker, back-solves duration
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

_Gloss: `сума на услугите` sum of the services · `Друго…` other… · `До определен час…` until a specific time…_

> **Ruling: every row is a duration AND the end it yields.** No arithmetic in either direction, ever, for anyone. The catalogue sum is checkmarked **and captioned**, so the row you would hit by accident is the correct one — which is the cheapest safety this control can buy.

**Ladder construction, not a fixed list.** Take the catalogue span _S_, snap to the booking increment _g_ = 5, emit `S−2g, S−g, S, S+g, S+2g`, union the shop's two or three most-booked lengths, dedupe, sort, **cap at 8**. Beyond that is `Друго…`.

> **Ruling: the ladder IS the stepper, spelled as choices — and `ui-stepper` may not be bent into this.** The stepper literature wants a dominant value with small deviations either side, which is exactly what the ladder emits; but `ui-stepper` in this system is a `role="progressbar"` journey component, not a numeric `±` ([stepper.ts:66](../../libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/stepper/stepper.ts:66)), and there is **no `±` nudge pair anywhere on this surface** (§3.3 R2). A menu of named outcomes gets the same ergonomics with none of the component abuse.

**`До определен час…` is the entire end-time escape hatch** — one unobtrusive accelerator, per Nielsen #7. It opens the same platform time control as `Начало`, computes `duration = chosen − start`, snaps to _g_, and **writes the duration**. A time at or before the start is **not selectable**: the illogical option is removed, not validated. That one row is the whole of what `До` used to be, and it costs a row in a menu instead of a field on the sheet.

#### The frame is the other duration control, and it already exists

| Gesture                    | Holds    | Changes              | Writes                   |
| -------------------------- | -------- | -------------------- | ------------------------ |
| Drag the **block body**    | duration | start                | `Начало`                 |
| Drag the **bottom** handle | start    | end                  | `Времетраене`            |
| Drag the **top** handle    | end      | start _and_ duration | `Начало` + `Времетраене` |

The top handle is the honest form of _"I'll start ten minutes later but still finish at eleven."_ All three snap at 5; all three **live-update the `Времетраене` trailing value as they move**; all three announce on release (§3.4.10). Apple documents direct manipulation as a peer of the picker, not a novelty: _"touch and hold the event, then drag it to a new time, or adjust the grab points."_

> **Ruling: buffers are drawn on the frame as hatched shoulders and are NOT inside `Времетраене`, and NOT inside `до 10:45`.** The number describes when the **client walks out**; the frame describes when the **chair frees**. Two questions, two surfaces, neither lying. (R12 / R23 unchanged; §2.2 Q8 is where the two geometries are separated.)

#### Over- and under-length edits — the full decision table

Let _S_ = the catalogue span of the current arrangement, _D_ = the requested duration, _K_ = the slack already on the appointment.

| #   | Condition                            | What happens                                                                                                                                                                         | What the barber sees                                                         |
| --- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | one service, any _D_                 | a per-appointment **duration override on that service**                                                                                                                              | `Подстригване · 20 мин` carrying the `по избор` marker. **Price unchanged.** |
| 2   | ≥2 services, _D > S_                 | the delta becomes **named slack**                                                                                                                                                    | a `Допълнително време · 15 мин · 0,00 €` row in Услуги — visible, deletable  |
| 3   | ≥2 services, _S − K ≤ D < S_         | **consume the slack first**, down to zero                                                                                                                                            | the slack row shrinks, then disappears                                       |
| 4   | ≥2 services, _D < S − K_             | **refuse the silently-lossy edit.** Ladder rows below the floor are `disabled`; the floor row captions `най-малко 45 мин — променете услуга` and tapping it pushes the Услуги region | **no service is ever shortened by a control that does not name it**          |
| 5   | _D_ off-grid                         | snap to _g_ = 5                                                                                                                                                                      | the number that appears is the number that saved                             |
| —   | **rescale every leg proportionally** | **never**                                                                                                                                                                            | —                                                                            |

**Rule 4 is the one that gets argued with and the one that matters.** "Shrinking silently shortens the last service" is how a 30-minute cut quietly becomes 22 minutes in the reporting and nobody finds out for a quarter. The floor is a refusal with a named remedy, not a disabled control with a shrug.

**Price never moves with duration** — R11 unchanged — and `staff.visit.durationKeepsPrice` = `Промяната на времето не променя цената.` still fires **once**, on the first duration edit, then never again.

#### The nine rulings, re-cut

| #   | Old ruling                                                                               | Status                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | the primitive is `input[uiTextField] type="time" step="300"`, the one that already ships | **Survives**, on `Начало` alone. Zero new field code; the platform's own time keypad, label semantics and SR support for free. `ui-date-field` is date-only and cannot serve here.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| 2   | `min`/`max` encode the business rules declaratively                                      | **Survives, halved.** `Начало` takes `min = rosterStart − 60`, `max = rosterEnd + 60`. The `До` arm (`min = draftStart + 10`, `max = min(nextBookingStart, rosterEnd + 60)`) is **deleted with the field**, and the error state it removed stays removed — now by construction.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
