## 4.2 Open questions for the owner

**Q1 · Does the editor edit the appointment or the seat?**
**Recommendation: the appointment, opened at a seat.** The frame highlights the opened seat's leg; the ladder shows all of them; a genuinely parallel leg in another chair is drawn in the same column, outlined in that barber's tone, and named in words (§3.4.2). This forces replacing `visitSheetRow()` with an `appointmentId`-keyed VM in M3 — which is required anyway, because the staff-edit payload replaces every seat.

**Q2 · Should an overlapping placement be permitted at all?**
**Recommendation: yes, behind an explicit second tap.** Fresha permits, Square warns and permits, Apple silently renders. The barber who chooses it knows something the model does not — one client in the chair, one under the dryer. The cost is `deps.allowOverlap` and an `acknowledgedOverlap` flag on the request. A drag that refuses to move feels broken; a commit verb that names what you are about to do teaches.

**Q3 · Minimum staff-placed duration: 10 or 20 minutes?**
**Recommendation: 10.** `SHORTEST_SELLABLE_MINUTES = 20` ([staff-day.store.ts:40](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-day.store.ts:40)) governs which _gaps are offered as sellable_, not what staff may place, and a beard tidy-up is a real ten-minute job.

The handle-crowding threshold must be re-derived at the **worst** density, not the default. The frame's scale is `--sys-space-unit`-derived and therefore ranges **2.21–2.59 px/min** across `[data-density]` ([tokens.css:50-51](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:50), [:231-236](../../libs/ui/tokens/tokens.css:231)). The 44pt floor does _not_ scale — it is an absolute accessibility minimum. Two stacked handles therefore need 88 absolute px in the block axis:

| Density           | px/min | Handles fall under 44pt below |
| ----------------- | ------ | ----------------------------- |
| `compact` (0.92)  | 2.21   | **40 min**                    |
| default (1.0)     | 2.40   | 37 min                        |
| `spacious` (1.08) | 2.59   | 34 min                        |

**Ruling: the documented figure is 40 minutes, the compact-density case.** Below it the typed fields are the guaranteed path, and §3.4.4 must say 40, not 37.

**And since 2026-08-26 that table carries a second job.** 88 absolute px is also exactly what the **body-drag** needs to exist — the move region is the block minus the inward half of each straddling handle, so below the same 40 / 37 / 34-minute figures the two handles own the whole block and there is nothing left to grab. **Body-drag suppression reuses this number; it does not derive a second one.** Below the floor, moving a booking is `Начало` typed — which carries the end with it, because the end is derived (Ruling B, 2026-08-26). ⚠ That is _more_ true than when this paragraph was written: it used to say `От` _"carries `До` with it"_, which was a behaviour the code had to implement. It is now an identity.

**Q4 · May a barber override price, or only duration?**
**Recommendation: duration yes, price no.** A barber knows a fade ran long; discounting the shop's money is a receptionist/admin act. This is why the role model must land with M7 rather than after it. If the answer is "any staff member", say so now, because the callable's shape changes.

⚠ **Widened 2026-08-26 (comment 3), and the widening is a third arm rather than a softening of the first two.** "Discounting" was covering two different acts. **Honouring a grant the client already holds** (`CouponGrantRepository.findUsableForUser`) is not discounting — the shop made the promise and the barber is keeping it — and **a `barber` may do it**. **Authoring an ad-hoc discount** is spending the shop's money and stays `receptionist | admin | sysadmin`. **Browsing** the promo catalogue is readable by everyone who can open this sheet. The `Цена` row on the service page is unaffected: **absent** for a barber, never disabled. If the owner disagrees with the grant arm, say so before M8, because it decides whether the apply page has one role branch or two.

**Q5 · Should `Запази` ever write without an explicit tap?**
**Recommendation: no. Flat, with no exception** — **rewritten 2026-08-26.** The single exception this answer used to carry was the `±5` nudge's 900 ms coalesce, and the nudge is deleted (§3.4.9). Nothing else on the surface ever writes on a timer.

**What replaces it is not a `Запази` bypass, it is a different class of write.** Regime A (§3.2) covers the writes that are one value, instantly reversible and never re-decided by the server — a status verb, a zero-minute add-on — and each of those commits on its own tap and carries its own undo. Regime B covers everything geometric or compound, and it waits for `Запази` without exception, because `decideBooking` re-decides placement and can refuse. The store's own ruling is what both regimes serve: _"a lane that lied for a second teaches staff to distrust it."_

**Q6 · Does the notify switch ship disabled, or not at all?**
**Recommendation: not at all, replaced by the honest sentence.** `staff.day.blockEffect` already sets the precedent. A live-looking switch over a dead channel is worse than a sentence saying there is no channel. Build the channel (M9), then the switch. This is the same rule that moved the add-on chips out of M1 — and, before it was deleted outright, the `±` nudge with them.

**Q7 · Does `Заредили сме услугите от 12 юли` overwrite silently, or announce?**
**Recommendation: announce and badge.** Apple's version overwrites invisibly and their own workaround advice is _"don't title the event the same as a previous one."_ Ours states what it took and marks every changed value `по избор` until saved.

**Q8 · Does the frame ever show other chairs?**
**Recommendation: no — with one exception, and it is not browsing.** The frame never becomes a multi-chair grid you can shop around in: three columns inside a 375px phone leave ≈108–110px each across the density range, which is a chart, not a control. Outlook mobile reached the same conclusion by demoting its grid to a second screen. The question "who's free if I move this?" is answered better by M2's chair-move verdict menu, in words. The exception is **this appointment's own genuinely parallel legs** — a party booked across two chairs at the same time still draws **one** column, but the sibling leg is drawn inside it, outlined in that barber's tone and named in the party row, because a leg the frame refuses to draw is a leg the next save silently drops. Drawn, named, not draggable (§3.4.2). §4.4 states the same boundary.

**Q9 · Body-drag to move the block — now, later, or never?**
**ANSWERED BY THE OWNER, 2026-08-26: now, in M4.** ~~_Recommendation: later, as its own PR, with a device test._~~ The recommendation is struck, and so is the exclusion it justified (§4.4).

The browser fact that produced the original answer survives untouched: the mid-gesture `touch-action` switch every reference design reaches for **is** a no-op, on every browser, because `touch-action` is latched when the touch begins. What was wrong was the conclusion that the only alternative is permanent `touch-action: none` plus a hand-written scroller. The construction that ships keeps **`touch-action: manipulation` permanently** and takes the gesture with **Touch Events under a 250 ms, zero-tolerance long press** — zero tolerance being what guarantees `touchmove` is still `cancelable` when the drag activates (§3.4.9). The device test the old answer asked for is retained as a **gate on M4**, not a follow-up.

**Q10 · The page-grid placement migration — bundled or separate?**
**Recommendation: separate, and after M4.** The outward rounding is a real lie and worth fixing, but it touches lane packing, closed runs, the hour gradient, the now-line, sticky heads and the reveal scroll on the surface four people use all day. Ship `uiPlacement` as a mode, let the frame opt in, then migrate with screenshots at all three densities.

**Q11 · Recurring appointments — deferred or designed now?**
**Recommendation: deferred, and if ever built, as materialised occurrences rather than a recurrence rule.** Shops move individual visits constantly, and a rule fights that on day one. `Дублирай` plus the post-completion rebook prompt cover the real behaviour at the chair.

**Q12 · Should `staff-time-grid` be promoted to `libs/ui`?**
**Recommendation: no, not yet.** The prior ruling says _"Promote when a second surface asks."_ The frame is a second **mode**, not a second library. Promote when a different library asks.

**Q13 · Does the sheet keep zero bespoke CSS as a goal? — ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-26.**
**Answer: yes, and the count did not move.** Three classes were born and three deleted by the twelve comments, so the four exceptions below stand at four: `.staff-sheet__disclosure`, **`.staff-sheet__pill`**, **`.staff-sheet__consequence`** and the `.staff-frame__*` family (which now includes **`.staff-frame__owner`**). Deleted: `.staff-sheet__tokens`, `.staff-sheet__token-label`, and `data-token-kind` / `data-unresolved` / `data-ambiguous` / `data-open` with them. **A redesign that reverses three rulings and adds no net CSS is the strongest available evidence that the reversals went toward the system rather than away from it.** The original text stands below, re-pointed where it named a token.

**Recommendation: yes — four new exceptions (amended 2026-08-26; it was two), and one rename instead of a fifth.**

The earlier draft named `.staff-visit__field` as a new class for the labelled time-field pair. That is a copy, and REUSE, NEVER COPY forbids it: **`.staff-block__field` already exists** ([staff-dashboard.css:934-937](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.css:934)) and already wraps exactly the labelled `input[uiTextField] type="time" step="300"` From/To pair the visit sheet wants ([staff-dashboard.html:1459-1484](../../libs/features/staff/dashboard/src/lib/staff-dashboard/staff-dashboard.html:1459)). **Ruling: rename it `.staff-sheet__time-field` in M1, alongside the `.staff-cancel__body` → `.staff-sheet__body` rename, and both sheets use it.** `.staff-visit__field` is deleted from the new-classes block and does not get written.

That leaves exactly four genuinely new classes: `.staff-sheet__disclosure` (**new** — six lines, because `ui-list-group`'s `display: contents` rule does not reach a non-row child, and since 2026-08-26 its **one** consumer is the inline calendar), ~~`.staff-sheet__tokens` and `.staff-sheet__token-label`~~ → **`.staff-sheet__pill`** (the `Ден` trigger and the `Начало` wrapper, six declarations) and **`.staff-sheet__consequence`** (the pushed page's live range line), and `.staff-frame__*` (**new**, now including `.staff-frame__owner`). `.staff-sheet__figures` and `.staff-sheet__time-field` were already counted and are not new. ⚠ **One prefix, `staff-sheet__`** — the sheets share these classes, which is the whole point of the `.staff-cancel__body` → `.staff-sheet__body` and `.staff-block__field` → `.staff-sheet__time-field` renames. No `staff-visit__` class is ever written; where the name appears in this document it is naming something deliberately _not_ created. Everything else stays tokens and primitives, which is what the sheet is today and what makes it maintainable.

**Q14 · The drag-to-reschedule override — where is it recorded?**
**Recommendation: `docs/design-research/decisions.md`, dated, before a line of frame code is written**, answering each of the four original objections individually. The original document says it was recorded _"so it stops being re-proposed."_ A rejected feature that returns without a written override returns again next quarter.

**Amended 2026-08-26: there are now two reversals to record, not one.** The first is the original — [staff-schedule-uiux-design.md:366](../../docs/design-research/staff-schedule-uiux-design.md:366)'s outright rejection of drag-to-reschedule, overridden by §4.3. The second is **this document overruling itself**: §3.4.9's _"no body-drag in v1"_ and §4.4's matching exclusion, both reversed by the owner. A document that quietly deletes its own ruling is worse than one that never made it, so **both entries go in the same file, dated, before M4 starts** — the second one carrying the six costs §3.4.9 names, so the next person to ask _"why does this component have two input vocabularies?"_ finds the answer instead of re-deciding it.

**Q15 · May a `content_manager` touch the book at all?**
**Recommendation: no — and today they can.** [firestore.rules:47-49](../../firestore.rules:47) already excludes `content_manager` from `worksTheBook()`, with an explicit comment that a copy-and-media role has no business reading every client's name, phone and note. But both server callables gate on `STAFF_ROLES` ([user-role.ts:44-50](../../libs/domain/accounts/src/lib/user-role.ts:44)), which includes it. So a `content_manager` cannot read an appointment and _can_ transition it and stamp an arrival. That is a live inconsistency, not a design question — the only question is whether the owner agrees the rules file is the correct side. If yes, M2 2.1 closes it. If the owner wants `content_manager` to work the book, the rules file changes instead and the comment comes out. **Answer before M2 starts**, because it decides the callable's gate.

**Q16 · Does a `barber` get client search, or guest-only?**
**Recommendation: a narrow callable, not a rules change.** `allow list` on `/users` is `receptionist | admin | sysadmin` only ([firestore.rules:96-97](../../firestore.rules:96)) — "front-desk and admin business only" — so the persona this document keeps describing, the barber holding a phone one-handed mid-cut, gets **permission-denied** on the picker's search. Widening the rule hands every barber a dump of the whole clientele's phone, email and birth date. **Recommendation: a callable behind the Admin SDK that returns name + last-visit only, nothing else, for role `barber`;** receptionists and admins keep the direct list. The fallback, if the owner would rather not build it, is barbers-only search plus quick-create-as-guest, with the client list simply absent — never an error state that implies a failure. Either way §3.7's picker needs its **Not permitted (role `barber`)** state written.

**Q17 · Who owns a staff-created walk-in?**
**Recommendation: nullable `ownerUserId` plus a new `createdByUserId`.** The two candidates:

| Option                                         | For                                                                                                                                                       | Against                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Nullable `ownerUserId` + `createdByUserId`** | Honest — nobody's account owns this booking, because nobody signed in. Audit still names the staff member. Matches how guest companion seats already work | Touches `CommitBookingUseCase` → `decideBooking` → `toSubject` (**M**), and every client-path ownership check must keep refusing null rather than matching it                                                                                  |
| **A shop service account as owner**            | No signature changes at all; every existing ownership check passes unchanged                                                                              | A fake user in `/users` that no rule can distinguish from a real one; every "my appointments" query for that account returns the shop's entire walk-in history; and the moment a walk-in client registers, the migration has no seam to cut on |

The service account buys one **M** of work now and pays for it forever in a data model that lies about who a booking belongs to. **Take the nullable owner.** This blocks M6 6.1 — and M3 3.6, if the minimal create is hoisted — so it is the first of these three to answer.

**Q19 · Did "time override" mean the duration/price fields, or placing a booking somewhere the engine refuses?**
**Recommendation: assume both, and ship them as two different things.** §3.5 reads the phrase as `durationMinutesOverride` on a leg — a per-booking number that beats the catalogue's — and that is what M7 builds. The other reading is `allowOutsideWindow` + `allowOverlap` in M2 — of which only `allowOverlap` is _acknowledged_; the roster bound is simply not a staff rule (M2 2.4) — which is a different mechanism with a different audit trail. They should never merge into one control: one says _this cut takes longer than the price list claims_, the other says _I know this is double-booked and I am doing it anyway_. If the owner meant only the second, M7's fields can wait.

**Q18 · Is the no-show grace window 10 minutes?**
**Recommendation: 10, and make it a named constant, not a literal.** The gate drops `no_show` out of the full-width verb run before `start + 10 min` and leaves it inside `⋯`, so the number controls emphasis, never permission. (It is _not_ a `primaryVerb` arm — see §3.9 #3.) Ten is the industry-common grace, but this is a shop-floor number and the owner is the only person who knows whether their regulars run five minutes late or twenty. If the answer is "it depends on the barber", say so and it becomes shop configuration in M7 rather than a constant in M1.

**Q20 · Can a one-off, non-catalogue service exist? (new, 2026-08-26)**
**Recommendation: yes, eventually — via a `SERVICE_CUSTOM` sentinel rather than a nullable id.** The question is unavoidable the moment a search field exists: searching invites typing, and typing invites `Подстригване на брат ми`. Today `SeatProps.serviceId` is non-nullable ([seat.ts:62](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/seat.ts:62)), so there is nowhere to keep such a thing. ⚠ **Unaffected by Ruling C (2026-08-26):** the search moved from a token field to a pushed page, and a page invites typing exactly as much as a field did.

| Option                          | For                                                                                                                          | Against                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Nullable `serviceId`**        | No new concept                                                                                                               | **Every `serviceId` read becomes a branch** — pricing, terms, occupancy, the upsell heuristic, the agenda card. A null that means _"real, just not in the catalogue"_ is the worst kind of null |
| **A `SERVICE_CUSTOM` sentinel** | One lookup that resolves to a per-seat name, duration and price. The type stays total; nothing downstream learns a new shape | A sentinel is a value everybody must know about, and it needs its own terms snapshot                                                                                                            |

**Take the sentinel. Size M, M9.** Until it is answered, `customService` (renamed from `tokenCustom`) **does not render**: the no-match state offers the sentence `Няма услуга „{{query}}“.` (`noMatch`) and nothing else — which is still not a dead keystroke (R26), because it names what you typed. **It is a row on the pushed search page, not a token**, and it is explicitly **not** in M5.

**Q21 · Is 250 ms the right long-press for the body-drag? (new, 2026-08-26)**
**Recommendation: ship 250 as a named constant, then re-measure it on device during M4's gate.** The field's band is react-beautiful-dnd **120**, dnd-kit **250**, Android's `DEFAULT_LONG_PRESS_TIMEOUT` **400**, iOS **500**, FullCalendar **1000**. 250 reads as deliberate without feeling sticky, and it is the number every touch-drag library that also has to coexist with a scroller converges near. But this is a shop-floor number like Q18's ten minutes: it wants a barber, wet hands and one hand on a phone, not a spreadsheet. **The tolerance is not up for measurement** — 0 px is mechanical, not aesthetic (§3.4.9), and a "friendlier" 5 px re-opens the window where `touchmove` is already non-cancelable.

**Q22 · Should the fitted sheet keep the running-late chips at all, now that they only promote? (new, 2026-08-26)**
**Recommendation: yes.** They stopped being writes (M2 2.12) and became draft seeds, which is a real demotion — one tap now un-fits the sheet instead of finishing the job. Keep them anyway. One tap still gets you exactly as far as _"push him twenty"_ ever got you; what changed is that you see the collision **before** you commit rather than eating a server refusal after it. The alternative is a barber hunting for the frame during the one minute of the day he is least able to hunt. ⚠ **If the answer is no, §3.2's promise that the fitted top region carries no interactive control gets easier, not harder** — which is the honest argument for the other side, and the owner should hear it before ruling.

**Q23 · Does `ui-sheet-nav` belong to `ui-modal-sheet`, or beside it? (new, 2026-08-26 — the twelve comments)**
**Recommendation: beside it — a separate pattern component that a sheet _hosts_, not a capability a sheet _has_.**

⚠ **Numbering note: this is the question the resolution brief calls "Q21 (new)". Q21 and Q22 were already taken** by the long-press constant and the running-late chips, both opened earlier the same day. It and the next are **Q23 and Q24**; nothing was renumbered and no earlier question moved.

Ruling C makes a page stack inside a modal sheet a real, shipping mechanism, and the mechanism has to live somewhere. Folding it into `ui-modal-sheet` is the tempting answer and the wrong one, for a reason that is structural rather than aesthetic: **`ui-detent-sheet` is the _non-modal_ sheet** — no scrim, no focus trap, no `aria-modal` — and if the stack lives on a shared base, a non-modal sheet can accidentally acquire a navigation hierarchy. That is the HIG's _"app within your app"_, and it is the one thing a sheet must never become. Keeping `ui-sheet-nav` a separate component that a **modal** sheet composes makes the bad configuration unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged. It also needs two small host affordances either way: **`[uiLeading]` on `ui-sheet-header`** (which projects only `[uiTitle]` and `[uiTrailing]` today, [sheet-header.ts:71-72](../../libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/sheet-header/sheet-header.ts:71)) and the `[sheet-action]` slot on `ui-modal-sheet`. **Answer before M3**, because M3 is where the component lands.

**Q24 · Should the service page hide its `Бръснар` row in a one-barber shop? (new, 2026-08-26 — the twelve comments)**
**Recommendation: yes — hide it when `listActiveBarbers().length === 1`.**

Comments 2 and 7 move staffing onto the service page, which is right for a two- or three-chair shop and is pure tax for a one-chair one: a menu row on **every** service page, at 44pt, for a value that can never change. Hiding it costs one condition and loses nothing — the frame's `.staff-frame__owner` header already names the barber once, which is the whole argument for not repeating a fact per row. ⚠ **The counter-argument, so the owner hears it:** a shop that hires its second barber gets a row appearing in a screen it had learned by heart, with no announcement. That is a real cost, and it is smaller than the row. **Not a blocker for M5** — ship the row, add the condition when a single-barber shop actually complains — but it wants an answer before the service page's layout is treated as settled.

---

## 4.3 The four original objections, answered

[staff-schedule-uiux-design.md:366](../../docs/design-research/staff-schedule-uiux-design.md:366) rejected drag-to-reschedule _"outright, at every phase."_ This document overrides it. Each objection gets a named answer, not a shrug. **Re-checked 2026-08-26, after the owner reversed this document's own body-drag exclusion:** objections 1, 2 and 3 stand exactly as written — objection 3 in particular is _why_ a body-drag can be permitted at all, because release still commits nothing. **Objection 4 does not stand, and is re-cut below rather than quietly left in place.**

**1. _"`termsForBarber` means the same fade is 30 min with Иван and 45 with Нико, so a block changes height when dragged sideways."_**
True and unavoidable. **Answered by removing the sideways gesture entirely.** Cross-chair movement is M2 2.11's menu with a plain-language verdict per barber, and where the terms differ the row says `Свободен · 45 мин` **before** you commit. The model's honesty becomes the feature instead of the bug. Vertical, same-chair resize — the owner's actual ask — never triggers it.

**2. _"A party spans lanes, so dragging one seat either drags the envelope or violates the double-booking invariant."_**
**Answered by Q1's ruling.** The editor edits the appointment, opened at a seat, on an `appointmentId`-keyed VM. Genuinely parallel legs are drawn in the **one** column the sheet was opened at — the sibling leg outlined in that barber's tone, carrying no handles, named in the party row (§3.4.2). Each seat is edited by opening it, and the handles bound against that seat's own barber's neighbours — which the invariant already permits, because `Seat.collidesWith` is `this.barberId.equals(other.barberId) && this.slot.overlaps(other.slot)` ([seat.ts:223-227](../../libs/domain/scheduling/src/lib/seat.ts:223)): it only forbids a barber overlapping _himself_. A single-column frame never shows a seat it cannot correctly bound.

**3. _"`reschedule` re-decides placement server-side and can refuse."_**
**Answered by never committing on release.** The drag fills a draft; `Запази` calls the server; a refusal renders through the existing `rowError` machinery with the draft intact. And the client never offers a placement the server would reject: overlap is offered only because `allowOverlap` will accept it, and outside-roster only because `allowOutsideWindow` will.

**4. _"This repo has already paid once for a custom drag-threshold saga."_**
~~**Answered by not writing a new one.**~~ **RE-CUT, 2026-08-26. That answer no longer holds, and pretending otherwise would be exactly the kind of quiet contradiction this document exists to prevent.**

The handle half is unchanged: a handle claims immediately, because a dedicated 44pt target is unambiguous and needs no threshold. **But the block body does need one** — and it needs a second input path, Touch Events with `{ passive: false }`, beside the handles' Pointer Events. That is a real cost and §3.4.9 names all six parts of it.

**What limits the cost is that the threshold is not invented here.** It is **250 ms with zero movement tolerance** — a number and a rule taken from react-beautiful-dnd, corroborated by dnd-kit, FullCalendar, AOSP and UIKit, with the _mechanical_ reason for the zero written down (§3.4.9) so that nobody later "improves" it into a bug. The saga this repo paid for was a threshold argued from taste; this one is argued from `touchmove.cancelable`.

The capture-phase click swallow is still copied rather than reinvented — a native capture listener registered in the constructor at [detent-sheet.ts:151-161](../../libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/detent-sheet/detent-sheet.ts:151), handler at [:325-330](../../libs/ui/patterns/src/lib/detent-sheet/detent-sheet.ts:325) — and it is now **extracted** rather than duplicated a third time. The sheet-level collision everyone feared still does not exist: `ui-modal-sheet`'s drag is bound only to `<ui-sheet-header>`, and `UiSheetBehavior.onDragStart` bails on `closest('button, a')`, which the block is. ⚠ **That is now load-bearing rather than incidental**, so it ships with a unit test asserting the block matches `closest('button')`. And the one collision that _is_ real — the frame's own scroll against the block's drag — is resolved **structurally**, by latching the frame's `overflow-y` for the duration of a drag, not by arbitration.

---

## 4.4 What is deliberately excluded, and why

| Excluded                                                                  | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ~~**Body-drag to move the block, in v1**~~                                | ~~The mid-gesture `touch-action` switch does not work on iOS Safari. Two handles, typed fields and the ±5 nudge cover the ask.~~ **OVERRULED BY THE OWNER, 2026-08-26 — see §3.4.9.** The browser fact stands; the conclusion does not. The construction that works keeps `touch-action: manipulation` permanently and takes the gesture with Touch Events under a **250 ms, zero-tolerance** long press. **Ships in M4**, beside the handles, because the block's geometry can only be authored once.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **A horizontal multi-attendee availability grid**                         | Time runs vertically everywhere else in this product. Outlook's axis inversion makes the user re-learn the axis at each tab boundary — a defect, not a pattern.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Chair columns for chairs this appointment does not occupy**             | The frame never becomes a browsable multi-chair grid: three columns inside a 375px phone leave ≈108–110px each across the density range, which is a chart, not a control. **This is a bound on browsing, not on the object.** A party with genuinely parallel legs still draws **every one of its legs** — §3.4.2 and Q8 — because a leg the frame refuses to draw is a leg the next save silently drops. It draws them _inside the one column_, outlined in the sibling barber's tone and named in words, never as a second column. "Who else is free?" is answered by M2 2.11's verdict menu, in words.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| **1-minute snapping, or a modifier for it**                               | There is no modifier key on a phone held one-handed. `Shift+Arrow` gives ±1 where precision belongs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **A magnifier**                                                           | At 2.21–2.59 px/min — the frame's scale across the three densities — there is no more detail to magnify. There are 5-minute steps and that is the whole vocabulary. **This now covers the body-drag too** (R38): a move lands on a 5-minute step like everything else, and the readout already names both of its boundaries.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Spring-loaded cross-day drag**                                          | Elegant, and it re-decides roster, lead time, conflicts and terms server-side mid-gesture with no way to preview the destination. `Премести на друг ден` opens the picker.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Swipe actions**                                                         | Already rejected, correctly — a swipe on a scrolling run of cards is a coin flip.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Bulgarian natural-language parsing**                                    | `125p` is the cheap half and it ships. Full NL is a language project with holiday tables and morphology, and Apple only ever shipped it on the desktop.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Processing / development time**                                         | Every salon product models it because hair colour needs it; a barbershop does not. Setup/cleanup already covers turnover, and adding it would over-fit the model and complicate every collision test.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Merging two appointments**                                              | Splitting creates; merging destroys two objects across two contacts, two owners and two audit trails. Every product that offers it does so on a desktop with an undo stack.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Payments, tips, checkout**                                              | The moment this sheet takes money it becomes the POS. Deposits render; nothing charges.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **A rounding control on the total**                                       | The money group is a derivation. A total you can type over is a total nobody can reconcile.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **Chips for committed participants**                                      | ⚠ **RE-INSTATED 2026-08-26, on its original reasoning.** The objection — _every participant carries a second load-bearing fact and a chip has no room for it_ — was struck earlier that day in favour of `ui-token`, and Ruling C removed the token too. **The objection was right all along about the constraint and only ever wrong about the remedy.** A committed participant is a **two-line `button[uiListRow]` that pushes a page**, which has room for the second fact, the third fact and a destructive verb. `ui-chip` keeps exactly three jobs: the arrangement pair, the applied-promo run, and the relative date row.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **A nested sheet, a popover, an inline expander or a menu for a service** | _(new, 2026-08-26 — Ruling C, and each rejection has its own quotable line.)_ A **nested sheet**: _"display only one sheet at a time… close the first before displaying the new one"_, and `ui-detent-sheet` is the **non-modal** sheet — stacking it over a modal one is the anti-pattern with a second scrim. A **popover**: _"avoid displaying popovers in compact views… present information in a full-screen modal view like a sheet instead"_ — at 375pt a popover **is** a bottom sheet. An **inline expander**: _"use no more than one disclosure button in a single view"_, and a per-row expander in a repeated list is N of them. A **menu**: menus carry _"a command, option, or state"_ and never host text entry, and price is typed money. **The remedy is a pushed page, at depth exactly one.** |
| **A `ui-value-stepper` primitive**                                        | _(reason re-cut twice on 2026-08-26)_ `ui-stepper` is `role="progressbar"` and must not be bent — that part never changed. What changed is the example: **there is no `±` pair left anywhere on this surface**, and after Ruling B the one numeric value a barber authors most often, `Времетраене`, is a **`ui-menu` ladder of outcomes** (`45 мин · до 10:45`) on the sheet's own row. **The ladder IS the stepper, spelled as choices** — it satisfies the stepper literature's dominant-value-plus-small-deviations shape (`S−2g, S−g, S, S+g, S+2g`, union the shop's common lengths, cap at 8) while naming the consequence of every option, which no `±` control can do. If a numeric stepper is ever genuinely needed it is a new primitive, not a reinterpretation.                                     |
| **A separate read-only detail sheet before the editor**                   | _(strengthened, 2026-08-26)_ Apple routes everything through an `Edit` switch and it costs a tap and a transition on the most common act. Fitted and un-fitted are the same component at two heights, live at both (§3.2) — there is no `Edit` button and no mode to leave. **And the research confirms the cost is real, not theoretical: Apple's read and edit views have diverged in row count and row shape**, which is that maintenance bill made visible. Ours would diverge in Bulgarian too, and twice as fast.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **A grab-and-move keyboard model _for resize_**                           | _(narrowed, 2026-08-26)_ For an **edge**, `role="slider"` is strictly better: no mode, native announcement, and the business rules as declarative min/max. FullCalendar has had keyboard resize open for years because it chose grab-and-move. **The block's MOVE gesture does get grab-and-move**, because a move is two values and a slider carries one (R40, §3.4.9).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Optimistic writes**                                                     | The most-copied behaviour in the corpus, and wrong for a server that can refuse.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Travel time, time zones, alerts, `Show As`**                            | One location, one zone. `staff-zone-sheet` already says so: _"Салонът работи в една часова зона, така че няма какво да се сменя."_                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Multi-select and bulk edit**                                            | A real need on a desktop admin surface; the wrong shape for a phone. Filed for the admin app.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Attachments and before/after photos**                                   | A media pipeline, a storage-rules change and a GDPR conversation. None of it belongs in a time editor.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **Confetti on every save**                                                | Celebration belongs to the last cut of the day. An expressive moment that fires forty times is chrome, not a moment.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
